**NEWS** | Nov. 25, 2026

# Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut, U.S. Navy commence CARAT Indonesia 2026

By Lt. Camillia Nguyen, Commander, Destroyer Squadron 7 Public Affairs

 SURABAYA, Indonesia–
Maritime defense forces from U.S. 7th Fleet and Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut (TNI-AL) convened in Surabaya, Nov. 25, to commence Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Indonesia.

The 32nd iteration of CARAT Indonesia launched with an opening ceremony, building upon previous maritime exercises and operations between the U.S. and Indonesia. CARAT is a maritime exercise designed to promote regional security cooperation, maintain and strengthen maritime partnerships, and enhance interoperability among participating forces.

“CARAT represents a commitment shared by the United States and Indonesia to promote maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific,” said Chris Green, U.S. Consul General in Surabaya. “After more than 30 years, CARAT continues to enhance our ability to work side-by-side across a wide range of naval competencies.”

Avenger-class mine countermeasures ship USS Warrior (MCM 10) from Commander, Task Force (CTF) 77 arrived in Indonesia, Nov. 25, to kick off preliminary events. The sea-phase of the exercise will also feature a P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft from CTF-72, as well as three TNI-AL Sigma-class corvettes, Fani-class mine countermeasures vessels KRI Pulau Fani (MCMV 731) and KRI Pulau Fanildo (MCMV 732), two Airbus AS656 Panther helicopters, and one TNI-AL CN 235 aircraft from TNI-AL. The sea-phase of this iteration will feature anti-submarine warfare drills, mine countermeasures best practices, and surface action group coordination to exercise command and control across units.

Additional personnel and staff supporting CARAT Indonesia 2026 include Commander, Destroyer Squadron (DESRON) 7, the U.S. 7th Fleet Band, and subject matter experts from CTF-73, CTF-75, and Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific. Subject matter expert exchange (SMEE) topics will include aviation, cyber, salvage diving, explosive ordnance disposal, and **U.S.–TNI-AL** combined musical performances. The SMEEs, held ashore in Surabaya, will facilitate information-sharing and promote interoperability at sea through building people-to-people relationships.

“We are grateful to our Indonesian partners for their warm welcome and hospitality in Surabaya,” said U.S. Navy Capt. Alfonza White, chief of staff, CTF-76, and head of delegation. “CARAT strengthens our coordination, builds mutual trust, and helps us preserve a free and open Indo-Pacific.”

CARAT is a long-standing exercise series designed to enhance U.S. and partner forces abilities to operate together in response to shared maritime challenges in the region.

As the U.S. Navy’s forward-deployed DESRON in Southeast Asia, DESRON-7 serves as the primary tactical and operational commander of assigned ships in the Southeast Asia area of operations.

U.S. 7th Fleet, the Navy’s largest forward-deployed numbered fleet, routinely interacts and operates with allies and partners in preserving a free and open Indo-Pacific.

美国以产能过剩为由对中国和欧盟征收新关税
资料照片：中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于 2026 年 5 月 14 日参观北京天坛。BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/Pool via REUTERS/资料照片
美国以产能过剩为由对中国和欧盟征收新关税
作者：艾丽西亚·迪亚兹（彭博社）——在唐纳德·特朗普总统推动恢复全面的全球进口税的推动下，美国宣布计划对来自中国、欧盟和其他十几个经济体的商品征收新一轮关税，最高法院认为这些关税违宪。
根据美国高级官员的说法，根据中国之前与特朗普政府达成的协议，从中国的进口税率将升至 20%，不过，如果两国谈判破裂，这一税率可能会翻一番，达到 40%。在周三宣布这一消息之前，这位不愿透露姓名的官员向记者做了简报。
根据美国贸易代表办公室的说法，根据美国与欧盟的协议，来自欧盟的产品将被征收 15% 的税，不过税率也可能升至 20%。
关税将适用于特朗普政府指责某些国内行业生产过剩并损害美国公司利益的经济体的产品。它们仍需接受公众意见征询，并且可能会发生变化。这位官员表示，最终行动最早可能在一月份采取。
新的征税措施标志着政府为恢复广泛的关税议程而做出的最新努力，其中包括利用紧急权力实施的逐国征税。今年二月，这些提议被高等法院法官否决，迫使特朗普援引其他法律权威来推进他的议程。
这是一个具有政治风险的举动。民主党在本月早些时候的中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，部分原因是选民对生活成本的愤怒以及对总统处理经济的不满。
中国和欧盟也可能进行报复，尽管它们最初发出的信号比较平静。
中国外交部发言人郭家琨周三早些时候在新闻发布会上表示，美国对其出口产品征收新关税的前景是“政治操纵”，并表示两国应共同努力维持贸易休战。
该公告似乎符合美国和欧盟之间的 2025 年贸易协定，该协定将欧盟大部分出口产品的关税上限限制在 15%。因此，此举目前可能不会激怒跨大西洋关系。欧盟委员会发言人奥洛夫·吉尔表示，“我们强烈反对欧洲是结构性产能过剩根源的前提”，并补充说欧盟预计新征税将遵守关税协议。
美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔表示，新关税旨在保护现有交易，同时解决产能过剩问题。
格里尔周三在 CNBC 上表示：“我们达成的许多交易实际上解决了我们在产能过剩方面看到的很多问题，或者可以解决这个问题。” “我们已经与我们的贸易伙伴讨论了这个问题。他们知道我们的提议。我认为其中很多内容都是经过深思熟虑的。”
来自日本、韩国、瑞士——所有美国主要贸易伙伴——的进口将受到 15% 的关税打击。美国贸易代表办公室表示，韩国的这一数字可能高达 25%，其他两个国家的这一数字可能高达 20%。如果与华盛顿的贸易协定最终确定，印度产品将面临 17% 的关税，不过这一税率可能会增加到 25%。
亚洲几个较小的国家也受到打击。针对墨西哥和挪威的类似预期措施并未包括在内

U.S. Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
FILE PHOTO: China's President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump visit the Temple of Heaven in Beijing on May 14, 2026. BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/Pool via REUTERS/File Photo
U.S. Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
By Alicia Diaz (Bloomberg) –The US announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional.
The rate for imports from China would rise to 20%, in line with the country’s prior agreement with the Trump administration — though that rate could double to 40% if talks between the two countries fall apart, according to a senior US official. The official briefed reporters on condition of anonymity ahead of Wednesday’s announcement.
Products from the EU will be taxed at 15% in compliance with the US’s deal with the bloc, though that could also rise to as much as 20%, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative.
Tariffs will apply to items from economies the Trump administration accuses of overproduction in some domestic industries and hurting American companies. They are still subject to a public comment process and could change. A final action could come as early as January, the official said.
The new levies mark the latest effort by the administration to reinstate an expansive tariff agenda that included country-by-country levies implemented using emergency powers. Those were struck down by high-court justices in February, forcing Trump to invoke other legal authorities to advance his agenda.
It’s a politically risky move. Democrats swept to a landslide victory in the midterm elections earlier this month thanks in part to voter anger over the cost of living and disapproval of the president’s handling of the economy.
China and the EU could also retaliate, though initial signals from them were muted.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a briefing earlier Wednesday that the prospect of new US tariffs on its exports was “political maneuvering” and said the two nations should work together to maintain their trade truce.
The announcement appears to comply with the 2025 trade agreement between the US and EU, which capped tariffs at 15% on most of the bloc’s exports. As a result, the move likely won’t antagonize transatlantic relations for now. European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said “we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity” and added the bloc expects new levies to abide by the tariff agreement.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the new duties were designed to preserve existing deals while addressing overcapacity concerns.
“A lot of these deals we made actually solve a lot of the problems we see in excess capacity or can go toward it,” Greer said Wednesday on CNBC. “We’ve talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we’re proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in.”
Imports from Japan, South Korea, Switzerland — all prominent US trading partners — would be hit with a 15% rate. The number could go up to 25% for Korea and 20% for the other two, USTR said. Indian products would face a 17% charge if a trade pact with Washington is finalized, though that could increase to 25%.
Several smaller nations in Asia were also hit. Similar expected measures aimed at Mexico and Norway were not included but remain under consideration, the official said. Greer said on CNBC the US has “had some very good conversations with Mexico” on the issue.
The tariffs follow a probe that began in March into alleged excess manufacturing capacity, utilizing Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a process seen as more resistant to legal challenges than Trump’s prior tariff wall. The tariff rates aren’t expected to surpass already agreed-upon levels in trade agreements with each economy.
The move will test the tolerance of economic partners, who have largely held back from retaliating, opting instead to negotiate deals with the US to minimize their tariffs. That dynamic could be on display next month, when Trump meets again with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Group of 20 summit. Their trade truce is set to expire in January unless the two powers agree to extend it.
“If we were to go beyond the 20% or something like that, they would view that as breaking our deal,” Greer said,
The trade ambassador said Washington and Beijing are also “proposing to implement” tariff reductions under its new board of trade on around $30 billion of non-sensitive exports.
Greer signaled that the new levy will not stack on top of existing duties of 10% or 12.5% under a separate investigation into negligent enforcement of forced-labor laws. “Those are not really additive,” he said on CNBC.
For products eligible to be hit by both sets of duties, only the higher rate would apply, the official said earlier.
The official added that there would be goods exempted from the tariffs, including oil and gas and food products that cannot be grown in the US. Other products that are already subject to sectoral duties, including tariffs on pharmaceuticals and critical minerals, are also exempted.
After the Supreme Court loss, Trump immediately announced plans to rebuild his tariff wall under a different legal authority. Under the Section 301 framework, the president can implement tariffs following an investigation into allegedly unfair foreign trading practices.
While Section 301 tariffs are seen as more legally sound and flexible than other powers Trump has eyed, they’re also more time-consuming. An earlier investigation under the same legal authority into policies around forced labor from US trading partners resulted in tariffs on some 60 economies. Those duties are currently facing legal challenges.
The new tariffs apply to Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.
USTR also announced it is raising tariffs on imports from Brazil, altering a previously-conducted trade investigation into the country’s digital policies and trade practices. The US is considering increasing the out-of-quota tariff rate on raw and refined sugar and proposing a 10% tariff on finished aircraft.
The increased levy on imports from Brazil comes weeks after Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro lost his presidential election bid to progressive incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

The United States International Trade Commission.
Request for comments regarding International Trade Commission's Economic Analysis, Investigation No. MISC-054.
Pursuant to Section 332 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the United States International Trade Commission (Commission) is seeking information from the public on its economic analysis, including its methodology and areas of focus.
To ensure consideration, written comments must be submitted on or before March 25, 2027.
Lisa R. Barton, Secretary to the Commission, U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Washington, DC 20436, telephone 202-205-2595. General information concerning the Commission may be obtained by accessing its internet server at https://www.usitc.gov. Hearing-impaired persons are advised that information can be obtained by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal on (202) 205-1810.
You may submit comments, identified by docket number MISC-054, by any of the following methods:
Agency Website: https://www.usitc.gov. You may submit comments on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov. For help accessing EDIS, please email EDIS3Help@usitc.gov.
Email: Submit comments via to Secretary@usitc.gov. Include docket ( printed page 76266) number MISC-054 in the subject line of the message. Comments submitted by email must be: in letter format and double-spaced (unless the document is less than two (2) pages); in portable document format (PDF); and signed with either a typed or written signature. All comments received will be posted without change to the agency's public record, including any personal information provided.
Instructions: All submissions received must include the agency name and docket number (MISC-054, along with written comments addressing the topics on which the USITC seeks information. All comments received will be posted without change to https://www.usitc.gov, including any personal information provided. Written comments filed on EDIS must conform to the provisions of section 201.8 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.8).
Docket: For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to https://www.usitc.gov and/or the U.S. International Trade Commission, 500 E Street SW, Room 112, Washington, DC 20436.
Jennifer Andberg, Office of External Relations ((202) 205-3404, or Jennifer.Andberg@usitc.gov). Hearing-impaired individuals may obtain information on this matter by contacting the Commission's TDD terminal at 202-205-1810. General information about the Commission is available by accessing the Commission website at www.usitc.gov. Persons with mobility impairments who will need special assistance in gaining access to the Commission should contact the Office of the Secretary at (202) 205-2000.
1. Relevant Statutory Authorities
Pursuant to section 332 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1332 (“section 332”)), whenever requested, the Commission submits to the President, and, by delegation, the United States Trade Representative (USTR); the Senate Finance Committee (SFC); or the House Ways and Means Committee (HWM) information and analysis on any matter related to tariffs, international trade, and industry competitiveness. Additionally, the President or Congress can task the Commission with factfinding investigations on various topics, which the Commission can also institute on its own initiative. Other statutes such as section 131 of the Trade Act of 1974 and statutes for specific trade agreements also provide authority to conduct factfinding investigations.
The Commission's work under section 332 and these other authorities utilize some degree of economic analysis. In such investigations, the Commission often analyzes the ways that trade and trade policy affect U.S. workers, producers, consumers, and the U.S. economy as a whole. The analysis helps inform policymakers' decisions on trade policy and international trade negotiations. In conjunction with other factfinding tools such as public hearings and written submissions, the Commission often uses analytical approaches including quantitative models, which are simplified, mathematical representations of an economy or industry using certain real-world data, to help isolate—and thereby understand—the impact of a past or future change when many factors could affect the outcomes.
To ensure that the Commission can meet the challenges posed by changing global and economic circumstances that are highly relevant to trade, it has decided to evaluate on an ongoing basis its analytical tools, data sources, and methodologies to ensure its work remains accurate, relevant, and responsive to its stakeholders.
2. Commission Analytical Approaches and How They Are Used
Given the variety of topics the Commission is obligated to analyze, the Commission uses a variety of analytical techniques, which can be combined to suit the topic(s) to be examined, including qualitative analysis, quantitative analysis without modeling, and quantitative analysis with economic modeling, which, as mentioned, can help assess the impact of a policy change by filtering out other factors, with important caveats.
The Commission's models vary by technique and scope. Major simulation models are built at the level of an industry or the entire economy. At the economy-wide level, the main modeling approach at the Commission has historically been the computable general equilibrium (CGE) model, based on the Global Trade Analysis Project (GTAP) database. This approach has been deployed numerous times in both factfinding investigations, such as in the evaluation of the likely impact of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) that the Commission published in 2019 (Inv. No. TPA-105-003, U.S.-Mexico-Canada Trade Agreement: Likely Impact on the U.S. Economy and on Specific Industry Sectors). Meanwhile, industry-level partial equilibrium models focus on a single economic sector without modeling the interactions between economic sectors, such as in the Commission's regular assessments of the USMCA automotive rules of origin (Inv. No. 332-600, USMCA Automotive Rules of Origin: Economic Impact and Operation, 2025 Report).
Although less frequently deployed in factfinding investigations as stand-alone models, econometric models have been used, for example, to measure the extent of “pass-through” from tariffs to U.S. prices in the Commission's analysis of the impact of the tariffs imposed in 2023 under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 (Inv. No. 332-591, Economic Impact of Section 232 and 301 Tariffs on U.S. Industries). More recently, in place of a CGE model, the Commission used an econometric “gravity” equation as part of a general equilibrium gravity model in a 2026 study on the impact of revoking China's permanent normal trade relations status (Inv. No. 330-609, Effects on the U.S. Economy of Revoking China's Permanent Normal Trade Relations Status).
In addition to the above trade models that have generally been focused on medium- and long-run outcomes, such as by assuming the entire U.S. labor force is employed and can move freely across sectors, the Commission is considering how to develop and deploy economic models that are more equipped to look at short-term outcomes before employment, wages and other aspects of the economy fully adjust to any policy change.
Because models cannot capture every feature of the real world, they necessarily rely on assumptions and simplifications. Different modeling approaches may also emphasize different channels through which policies affect economic outcomes. Economy-wide simulation models, such as CGE models, have been subject to criticism regarding certain assumptions, including assumptions about full employment and worker mobility across sectors, particularly when used to analyze the effects of trade policy changes.
II. Topics on Which USITC Seeks Information
The Commission seeks information from the public on any of the following topics. After the comment period concludes, the Commission intends to produce a report that includes a summary of comments. The comments will also inform how the Commission moves forward with its factfinding Section 332 and related responsibilities. ( printed page 76267)
1. Do you think the Commission currently has the right analytical tools, including economic models, to address major trade policy questions over the next 5-10 years? Why or why not?
a. What non-modeling approaches should the Commission's analytical toolkit include?
b. What is the full suite of models ( e.g., industry-specific versus economy-wide; short-term versus long-term) that the Commission should have available for use in its analysis?
2. What factors or topics should the Commission's economic analysis be able to consider? Would they include, but not be limited to, the following:
a. Effect of trade on labor markets
i. Short-term effect on workers
ii. Long-term effect on workers ( e.g., changes in workforce capacity or skill sets in certain industries)
iii. Effect on the quality of jobs available for workers, including any shifts in wages, benefits, or job security
b. Effect of trade on investment
c. Effect of hostile trade actions, including boycotts, export controls, or other trade sanctions placed on the United States or U.S. persons
d. Effect of trade on distribution of wealth/income within the United States, including across geographic regions and demographic groups
e. Effect of trade on the environment
f. Effect of trade on immigration
g. Interaction of trade policy with domestic policies and regulations ( e.g. intellectual property, environmental regulations, labor regulations, tax policy, immigration policy)
h. Interaction of trade with domestic and international protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights
i. Interaction with trade imbalances
j. Interaction with market concentration
k. Other topics you believe would be useful for the Commission to consider
3. Given the Commission's statutory obligations, which of the above topics should the Commission prioritize?
4. Please discuss what trade questions are well suited to modeling, and which are better served by a different sort of analysis, such as descriptive trend analysis, legal analysis, or other analytical approaches.
5. How effective have the Commission's models been at evaluating the effects of major trade policy changes in past years? Please reference specific examples.
6. How can the Commission best engage in quality control of its modeling prospectively and evaluate the accuracy of its modeling retrospectively? Should the Commission regularly and publicly undertake model validation to evaluate the accuracy of its models?
7. Are there existing alternatives to Commission models that are more accurate, or that would capture factors that the Commission should consider? What trade-offs, if any, might such other models have?
8. Are there other branches of economics or disciplines outside of economics that might be useful in helping the Commission improve its modeling and other analytical techniques? Please provide specific examples of techniques, papers, authors, or other details to help the Commission identify these items.
9. How can the Commission incorporate or improve any of the following practices, and are there examples of best practices from a Commission report or external report:
a. Sensitivity analysis to test the importance of assumptions on model outcomes
b. Indications as to the level of certainty of model estimates
c. Plain narrative explanation and data visualization
d. Transparency of model assumptions and limitations
e. Replicability of model releases
10. Should the Commission attempt to quantify the impact of nontariff measures (NTMs) on trade? If quantification is appropriate, how should this be conducted? How should the Commission account for the potential non-trade-related impacts of NTMs ( e.g., on public health and the environment)?
11. What datasets should be created, refined, or expanded upon for the Commission's use on understanding the effects of trade policy?
12. How can the Commission make the best use of AI tools for quantitative analysis?
13. Are there any ways in which the Commission's information-gathering techniques such as public hearings, field visits, written submission periods, or surveys can be improved?
14. From whom ( e.g., the public and/or technical experts) should the Commission receive input regarding its analytical approaches, and with what frequency and in what manner should the Commission solicit such input? Would the Commission benefit from establishing a public advisory council for economic modeling?
15. Anything else that the submitter believes would help the Commission improve its modeling.
III. Submission Instructions
Written submissions: Interested persons are invited to file written submissions and other information concerning the matters to be addressed in this request. All written submissions should be addressed to the Secretary, and should be received no later than 5:15 p.m., March 25, 2027. All written submissions must conform to the provisions of section 201.8 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.8). Filings must be made through the Commission's Electronic Document Information System (EDIS, https://edis.usitc.gov) or via email. Persons with questions regarding electronic filing should contact the Office of the Secretary, Docket Services Division (202-205-1802), email EDIS3help@usitc.gov, or consult the Commission's Handbook on Filing Procedures.
Any submissions that contain confidential business information (CBI) must also conform with the requirements in section 201.6 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR 201.6). Section 201.6 of the rules requires that the cover of the document and the individual pages be clearly marked as to whether they are the “confidential” or “nonconfidential” version, and that the CBI is clearly identified by means of brackets. All written submissions, except for CBI, will be made available for inspection by interested persons.
All information, including CBI, submitted may be disclosed to and used: (i) by the Commission, its employees and Offices, and contract personnel (a) for developing or maintaining the records of this or a related proceeding, or (b) in internal investigations, audits, reviews, and evaluations relating to the programs, personnel, and operations of the Commission including under 5 U.S.C. Appendix 3; or (ii) by U.S. government employees and contract personnel for cybersecurity or other security purposes. The Commission will not otherwise disclose any CBI in a manner that would reveal the operations of the firm supplying the information.
By order of the Commission.
Issued: November 23, 2026.
Secretary to the Commission.

content:
大西洋理事会：亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席中国
中国东亚 能源与环境 地缘政治与能源安全
2026 年 11 月 25 日 • 上午 10:04（美国东部时间）
中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席
霍尔木兹海峡地震发生九个月后，能源安全问题被提上上周日本-东盟和亚太经济合作组织 (APEC) 峰会的议程。五年来的第二次价格冲击迫使亚洲政策制定者重新考虑能源安全规划和机构，但中国并没有带头，尽管它在地区能源安全中发挥着重要作用。
中国的优先事项是国内而非地区
作为世界上最大的石油进口国，中国与经历霍尔木兹海峡供应中断的邻国依赖进口的国家有很多共同点。然而，关于新的合作能源安全规划机制和机构的新兴区域政策讨论基本上没有提及这一点。
在过去的八个月里，中国一直专注于国内能源优先事项，其行为有时会损害其他亚洲进口商。美国和以色列袭击伊朗仅一周后，中国就禁止了几乎所有石油产品的出口许可证。中国在随后几个月放松了这些限制，但在柴油和其他燃料库存大幅下降后，十月份北京再次限制产品出口。
中国只是东亚第三大石油产品出口国（仅次于韩国和新加坡），但其出口配额的意外变化改变了市场平衡。例如，2025 年，中国供应了澳大利亚近三分之一的航空燃油进口，因此 3 月份的航空燃油禁令让澳大利亚航空公司纷纷寻找替代品。
更广泛地说，中国缺乏透明度给邻国带来了挑战。其2025年至2026年3月的库存增加支撑了全球石油需求，而炼油厂开工率下降、国内燃料价格上限和出口限制等综合因素导致2月至6月原油进口出现前所未有的下降。分析师指出，中国在石油市场的定价能力源于其原油购买的时间和数量。然而，虽然国内考虑推动了这些决定，但它们往往让中国的邻国围绕其行动进行规划。尽管宣布建立东盟-中国能源合作伙伴关系，但其邻国有理由对中国的承诺持谨慎态度。
在经历了能源危机最初几个月的急剧下降之后，亚洲石油进口已经反弹。但这次中断影响了所有依赖中东石油和天然气的进口商。日本通常 90% 以上的原油从中东进口，因此被迫从美国或拉丁美洲寻找替代品（9 月份，美国原油占日本进口量的 27%，高于去年的 3%）。通常从中东进口大部分液化石油气的印度已转向美国供应。其他亚洲进口商一直在努力获取石化原料。
进口商正在重新评估他们的供应商关系。正如国际能源署 (IEA) 执行董事法提赫·比罗尔 (Fatih Birol) 在 2026 年 4 月大西洋理事会活动中所说，进口商现在有三个重要目标：“能源来源多元化。能源结构多元化。贸易路线多元化。”对于长期依赖石油的亚洲进口商来说，这是一项艰巨的任务。

China’s conspicuous absence in Asian energy security plans - Atlantic Council
China East Asia Energy & Environment Geopolitics & Energy Security
November 25, 2026 • 10:04am ET
China’s conspicuous absence in Asian energy security plans
Nine months into the Strait of Hormuz shock, energy security was on the agenda at last week’s Japan-ASEAN and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summits. The second price shock in five years has forced Asian policymakers to rethink energy security planning and institutions—but China is not leading the charge despite its significant role in regional energy security.
China’s priorities are domestic, not regional
As the world’s largest oil importer, China has much in common with neighboring import-dependent countries weathering the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption. Yet it is largely absent from emerging regional policy discussions over new cooperative energy security planning mechanisms and institutions.
Over the past eight months, China has focused on domestic energy priorities—and its actions have sometimes harmed other Asian importers. Only a week after the US and Israeli attack on Iran, China banned export licenses for nearly all petroleum products. China relaxed those restrictions in subsequent months, but in October—after a significant decline in stocks of diesel and other fuels—Beijing again restricted product exports.
China is only the third largest petroleum product exporter in East Asia (after South Korea and Singapore), but unexpected changes to its export quotas alter market balances. For example, China supplied nearly one-third of Australia’s jet fuel imports in 2025, so its March jet fuel ban left Australian airlines scrambling for alternatives.
More broadly, China’s lack of transparency creates challenges for its neighbors. Its 2025-March 2026 inventory builds supported global oil demand, while a combination of lower refinery runs, caps on domestic fuel prices, and export restrictions contributed to an unprecedented decline in crude imports between February and June. Analysts note that China’s pricing power in oil markets stems from the timing and volume of its crude purchases. But while domestic considerations drive these decisions, they often leave China’s neighbors to plan around its actions. Despite the announcement of an ASEAN-China Energy Cooperation Partnership, its neighbors have reason to be cautious about China’s commitment.
After steep declines in the early months of the energy shock, Asian oil imports have rebounded. But the disruption has affected all importers that depend on Middle Eastern oil and gas. Japan typically imports more than 90 percent of its crude oil from the Middle East, so it has been forced to find alternatives from the United States or Latin America (in September, US crude oil accounted for 27 percent of Japan’s imports, up from 3 percent the previous year). India, which normally imports most of its liquefied petroleum gas from the Middle East, has turned to the United States for supply. Other Asian importers have struggled to secure petrochemicals feedstocks.
Importers are re-evaluating their supplier relationships. As International Energy Agency (IEA) Executive Director Fatih Birol stated at an April 2026 Atlantic Council event, importers now have three important objectives: “Diversify from whom you get your energy. Diversify your energy mix. And diversify your trade routes.” This is a difficult task for Asian importers with longstanding dependence on the Middle East, especially those with refineries configured to process crude oil grades from the Gulf and Iraq.
Addressing energy security threats with new institutions
Governments in the region see two major threats to their energy security. First, the shale revolution and the decline in US oil imports have given Washington freer rein to act in ways that can raise their energy costs and jeopardize supplies. And second, that global energy security institutions are no longer fit for purpose, since they were created amid the 1970s oil shocks—when Asia made up a much smaller share of the global economy and global oil and gas consumption.
Energy leaders see a need for new Asian energy security architecture, as governments seek to diversify supplies, build inventories, and explore joint purchasing and sharing mechanisms. Japan aims to lead this effort and has proposed several new programs to bolster energy security.
In Manila last week, leaders from Japan and Southeast Asia updated plans for the Tokyo-led Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) initiative and the related Partnership on Wide Energy and Resource Resilience Asia (POWERR Asia) framework. The AZEC action plan emphasizes cooperation on emissions reductions, carbon removal, and decarbonization of the transportation sector. Takaichi also proposed a new Asian oil security task force and referred to it as “an Asian version of the International Energy Agency.”
In April, Japan committed up to 1.5 trillion yen ($9.4 billion) under POWERR Asia to support regional procurement of new hydrocarbon supplies, infrastructure to bolster fuel storage and supply chain resilience in Asia, and diversification of energy sources. State institutions including the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) and Japan Bank for International Cooperation are expected to support these plans that aim to broadly support Asian energy security. In several bills expected to be approved by Japan’s Diet in December, Takaichi’s government tasks JOGMEC with investing in alternative supply infrastructure including bypass pipelines and storage facilities.
At the Japan-ASEAN summit in Manila, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also proposed a new “POWERR Gulf” initiative to enhance cooperation between oil exporters in the Gulf and Asian importers. Inventories will likely be a key focus. Japan in particular is already building on existing joint stockpiling with Gulf national oil companies Saudi Aramco, Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, and Kuwait Petroleum Corporation. On November 20, Saudi Arabia and Japan announced an expanded joint oil stockpiling program. Japan intends to buy 8 million barrels of Saudi crude oil to replenish its stockpiles, and will lend Saudi Arabia new crude oil storage capacity of 16 million barrels, in addition to Aramco’s current 8.2 million barrels of capacity. Under Japan’s current joint oil stockpiling program, Gulf national oil companies lease storage capacity and use it for commercial operations in normal times, but Japanese companies have preferential rights to this crude oil in times of emergency. If the broader region embraces POWERR Gulf, the Gulf-Japan arrangement could become a template for other nations.
Asia will need more than one energy blueprint
The effectiveness of these new energy security initiatives remains to be seen. Japan and other countries in the region will remain highly dependent on the Middle East for crude oil and petroleum products. Energy resource endowments and energy systems also vary greatly across ASEAN countries, so their vulnerabilities and planning principles may differ from one country to the next.
Governments also face a strategic choice. After the second oil and gas price shock in five years, some policymakers in Southeast Asia and South Asia may lean toward more drastic changes in energy policy to emphasize resilience and use of domestic energy resources. Governments in these regions may well decide to direct scarce resources toward expanding electrification, renewable energy generation, battery storage, and grid resilience rather than new fossil fuel infrastructure.
It is notable that Japan is playing such a prominent role in region-wide energy security initiatives. This is unsurprising, since import-dependent Japan excels in long-term energy security planning and policy, including through its Strategic Energy Plans. Some officials and analysts in the broader region, however, worry that the proposed frameworks are too focused on fossil fuels, arguing that new investment should focus on electrification and renewable energy.
Opportunities for energy security leadership
As Asian governments devise new plans and institutions to bolster energy security and resilience, China is both absent and inescapable. China is the world’s largest oil importer, holds the world’s largest oil stockpiles, and is a key customer for nearly all the Gulf countries. More than any other importer, its actions will affect prices and energy security for its neighbors.
Beyond the oil and gas sector, China’s “electrostate” model and its many innovations in electrification, electric vehicle manufacturing, battery technology, and clean energy deployment will be important for Asian countries seeking to cut import dependence and build energy resilience. Yet it is not playing an especially active role in emerging multilateral discussions about how to bolster energy security in Asia. China’s lack of transparency and focus on domestic issues leaves a policy and planning gap that Japan is well positioned to fill.

zh_title: 告别浪漫战士：港币1,688元套餐让粉丝在移居澳大利亚前与冠军见面
summary: 告别浪漫战士：港币1,688元套餐让粉丝在澳大利亚前与冠军见面 |中国劳工布告栏 星期四, 2026 年 11 月 26 日 · 香港 香港及中国劳工英文新闻 告别浪漫战士：港币 1,688 元套餐让球迷在移居澳大利亚前与冠军见面 香港赛马会推出 500 个套餐，供球迷在退役冠军浪漫战士前往澳大利亚之前与他告别。港币 1,688 元的套餐包括自助早餐、12 月 12 日沙田见面会及毛绒玩具。独立套装售价为港币 438 元。香港
content:
告别浪漫战士：港币1,688元套餐让粉丝在澳大利亚前与冠军见面 |中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
告别浪漫战士：港币1,688元套餐让粉丝在移居澳大利亚前与冠军见面
香港赛马会发放了500个包裹，供球迷在退役冠军“浪漫战士”前往澳大利亚之前送别。港币 1,688 元的套餐包括自助早餐、12 月 12 日沙田见面会及毛绒玩具。独立套装售价为港币 438 元。
香港赛马会推出了 500 个套票，让赛马爱好者在这位退役冠军离开香港之前，最后一次近距离观赏这位退役冠军。价值港币1,688元的「浪漫战士全球冠军礼包及专属体验」套装包括12月12日于沙田举行的见面会。
体验活动于浪琴表香港国际赛前的周六早上 7 点开始，在 Champion Circle 或 Hay Market 享用两人份自助早餐，买家可以在那里观看国际赛马的比赛。上午 10 点，每位包裹持有者和一名嘉宾前往沙田游行场参加浪漫战士退休见面会。持有两张门票即可优先入场参加上午 11 点至下午 1 点举行的浪琴表香港国际赛马嘉年华。
该套装还包括“全球冠军包”，内含一个坐着的浪漫战士毛绒玩具、一张特别版八达通卡、一个行李牌和一个全球冠军箱。赛马日（12 月 13 日）可在沙田兑换纪念礼品券，届时马场仅限 18 岁或以上人士入场。
未能出席周六的车迷可以以港币 438 元单独购买全球冠军包，并于 12 月 13 日到沙田赛马活动区领取。俱乐部将每份优惠的上限限制为 500 份，分布在各个销售网点，并且不予退款。该体验套装不适合三岁以下儿童。
“浪漫战士”于9月退役，成为历史上收入最高的赛马，31场比赛中赢了24场，奖金达2.8874亿港元。他在香港、澳大利亚、日本和阿拉伯联合酋长国取得了 15 场第一组胜利，创造了香港纪录。岑丹尼的冠军为詹姆斯·麦克唐纳赢得香港杯四连冠，上赛季他成为第三匹完成香港三冠王的马匹。
11月22日，马主刘永强在沙田接受马会颁发的终身成就奖。浪漫战士将于国际赛事结束后前往澳大利亚，因此12月是当地车迷见到他的最后机会。

Farewell to Romantic Warrior: HK$1,688 package lets fans meet champion before Australia move | China Labour Bulletin Board
Thursday, 26 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Farewell to Romantic Warrior: HK$1,688 package lets fans meet champion before Australia move
The Hong Kong Jockey Club has released 500 packages for fans to say goodbye to retired champion Romantic Warrior before he leaves for Australia. The HK$1,688 set includes a breakfast buffet, a meet-and-greet at Sha Tin on 12 December, and a plushie. A standalone pack is available for HK$438.
The Hong Kong Jockey Club has released 500 packages for racing fans to get a last close look at Romantic Warrior before the retired champion leaves Hong Kong. The HK$1,688 "Romantic Warrior Global Champion Pack and Exclusive Experience" set includes a meet-and-greet at Sha Tin on 12 December.
The experience starts at 7am on the Saturday before the LONGINES Hong Kong International Races with a breakfast buffet for two at either Champion Circle or Hay Market, where buyers can watch the international horses work. At 10am, each package holder and a guest head to the Sha Tin parade ring for the Romantic Warrior Retirement Meet-and-Greet. Two tickets then give priority entry to the Pre-LONGINES Hong Kong International Races Carnival from 11am to 1pm.
The set also includes the Global Champion Pack, which holds a sitting Romantic Warrior plush, a special-edition Octopus card, a luggage tag and a Global Champion case. A voucher for a commemorative gift can be redeemed at Sha Tin on race day, 13 December, when racecourse entry is limited to those aged 18 and over.
Fans who cannot attend on the Saturday can buy the Global Champion Pack on its own for HK$438 and collect it at the Racing Event Zone at Sha Tin on 13 December. The club has capped each offer at 500, spread across its sales outlets, and no refunds are given. The experience set is not suitable for children under three.
Romantic Warrior retired in September as the highest-earning racehorse in history, having won 24 of his 31 starts and HK$288.74 million in prize money. His 15 Group 1 wins, a Hong Kong record, came in Hong Kong, Australia, Japan and the United Arab Emirates. Danny Shum's champion won four straight Hong Kong Cups for James McDonald, and last season he became only the third horse to complete Hong Kong's Triple Crown.
Owner Peter Lau accepted the club's Lifetime Achievement Award for the horse at Sha Tin on 22 November. Romantic Warrior is due to leave for Australia after the International Races, so December is the last chance for local fans to see him.

title: 神舟二十四號成功發射 首位巴基斯坦航天員登中國「天宮」意味什麼？
summary: 神舟二十四號成功發射 首位巴基斯坦航天員登中國「天宮」意味什麼？ - BBC News 中文 中國神舟二十四號自中國西北部戈壁沙漠發射升空，執行將三名航天員送入太空的任務。 其中一人是來自巴基斯坦的穆罕默德·齊尚·阿里（Muhammad Zeeshan Ali），40歲的他創造歷史，成為首名登上中國「天宮」太空站的外籍航天員，將與兩名中國航天員湯洪波及武毅一同執行任務。 對阿里而言，這是巴基斯坦的榮耀時刻；對中國而言，則是其與美國爭奪太空主導地位競賽中的又一進展。 新華社報道
content:
神舟二十四號成功發射 首位巴基斯坦航天員登中國「天宮」意味什麼？ - BBC News 中文
中國神舟二十四號自中國西北部戈壁沙漠發射升空，執行將三名航天員送入太空的任務。
其中一人是來自巴基斯坦的穆罕默德·齊尚·阿里（Muhammad Zeeshan Ali），40歲的他創造歷史，成為首名登上中國「天宮」太空站的外籍航天員，將與兩名中國航天員湯洪波及武毅一同執行任務。
對阿里而言，這是巴基斯坦的榮耀時刻；對中國而言，則是其與美國爭奪太空主導地位競賽中的又一進展。
新華社報道，國家主席習近平與巴基斯坦總統扎爾達里就中巴航天員執行聯合飛行任務互致賀電。
圖像加註文字，11月25日：2026年11月25日，中國航天員湯洪波、武毅與巴基斯坦航天員穆罕默德·齊尚·阿里在中國酒泉出席「神舟24號」乘組的歡送儀式。
阿里在早前記者會談及這次任務對自己及巴基斯坦的重要意義，他表示，「我肩負著巴基斯坦的名字，也肩負著2.5億巴基斯坦人民的期望。」
他又指，「對每一位在觀看這次任務的孩子，我想說，抬頭看看天空，記住我就在那裡，帶著你們的夢想一起飛翔。」
BBC駐中國記者碧嘉蘭分析，這次任務不僅是一項科學成就，也是一項地緣政治宣示。
中國首次安排外籍航天員進入太空，主要有兩個目的：科學合作與外交影響力。
阿里將在為期數天的短期軌道飛行期間，進行一系列生物科技及光合微生物領域的實驗，其後返回地球。
北京希望藉這次飛行進一步鞏固與伊斯蘭堡的關係，尤其是在兩國正紀念建交75周年之際。
中國多年來已向太空計劃投入數以十億美元計資金，而其重點項目天宮太空站目前由三人航天員團隊駐守，並約每六個月輪換一次。
如今，中國希望向外界展示，天宮太空站有能力成為國際科研平台，而非僅供中國使用的設施。
與此同時，北京試圖把自己塑造成美國主導太空計劃以外的重要替代選擇，並計劃於2030年前首次把中國航天員送上月球。
建立國際合作夥伴關係有助提升影響力和國際公信力。因此，中國希望透過這次任務傳達一個訊息：中國也能為其他國家提供將航天員送入太空的機會。
圖像加註文字，巴基斯坦航天員穆罕默德·齊尚·阿里（Muhammad Zeeshan Ali）出席記者會。
由於巴基斯坦沒有自行將航天員送上太空的運載工具，因此這次任務所有關鍵環節都依賴中國提供支援。
阿里與另一名進入神舟二十四號最終遴選階段的巴基斯坦候選人庫拉姆·達烏德（Khurram Dawood），均在中國接受訓練，並在中國專家的指導下於中國太空站模擬設施進行相關工作。
神舟二十四號於週三早上8時多發射升空，中國官方估計，飛船從發射到與天宮太空站對接大約需要三個半小時。
據路透社報道，阿里將在天宮太空站停留約一周，遠短於中國航天員一般約六個月的駐站時間。他其後將與兩名今年5月較早前抵達太空站的中國航天員一同返回地球。至於中國航天員湯洪波、武毅，則將與神舟二十三號乘組成員朱楊柱一同在天宮太空站駐留六個月。朱楊柱目前正研究人體如何適應長時間太空生活。
神舟二十四號乘組在太空期間將進行多項實驗及技術測試，涵蓋太空生命科學（space life sciences）、航天醫學（aerospace medicine）及燃燒科學（combustion science）。
例如，研究人員將探討太空環境如何影響血管老化（vascular ageing）等生理過程，希望有助研發新的預防及治療策略。
來自巴基斯坦的阿里則將負責研究細菌光合作用（photosynthesis in bacteria）、太空輻射及微重力環境對藜麥種子的影響。
迄今全球約有50個國家曾把本國公民送入太空，但只有美國、中國及俄羅斯能夠依靠自主研發的太空船完成這項任務。在此背景下，中國邀請巴基斯坦派遣航天員前往天宮太空站，被視為一項具有重要意義的發展。
阿里曾在空軍服役，對為這次歷史性任務作準備所需的高強度體能及技術訓練並不陌生。他是首位接受專業航天員訓練後進入太空的巴基斯坦人。
由於太空船上的所有開關、軟件系統、操作程序及語音廣播均以普通話運作，阿里不僅要掌握日常會話，還必須熟悉大量專業技術詞彙。
據路透社報道，阿里在北京接受為期七個月的密集中文培訓，期間除了學習普通話，也學唱中文歌曲及學習中國詩詞，並接觸書法和乒乓球等活動。
根據多家媒體報道，阿里表示：「我接受過多種訓練，包括離心機訓練、救援與生存訓練，以及緊急程序訓練，但老實說，最大的挑戰是掌握中文。」
這項語言訓練被視為他能夠參與神舟二十四號任務的重要一環，因為整個飛行及太空站操作系統均以中文為工作語言。
2023年10月，常駐摩納哥的巴基斯坦裔極地探險家納米拉·薩利姆（Namira Salim）曾乘搭維珍銀河（Virgin Galactic）的Galactic 04任務進入太空。她於2006年購買這趟商業太空飛行的船票，票價為20萬美元。
所謂次軌道飛行（suborbital flight），是指飛行器雖然到達外太空，但飛行速度未達到維持環繞地球運行所需的軌道速度（orbital velocity）。
Galactic 04任務共有六名乘員，包括三名維珍銀河員工，以及三名太空旅客；以廣義而言，薩利姆是首位進入太空的巴基斯坦人；阿里則是首名巴基斯坦專業航天員。
我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯這篇文章，它的原文是英文。在發佈之前，BBC記者檢查了翻譯的內容。

# US authorizes SpaceX to launch up to one million satellites for orbital data centers

The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX's plan to deploy up to one million satellites to build data centers in orbit, giving Elon Musk's company a major foothold in the industry. The authorization runs through 2040, as tech firms race to move computing infrastructure into space despite significant technical hurdles.

[Add France 24 to your favorites on Google to see France 24 content appear first in your search results.](https://f24.my/GDen)

Issued on: 26/11/2026 - 04:02

 1 min Reading time

Share

 By:

 The Starship megarocket lifts off on its 14h test flight from the SpaceX launch complex in Starbase, Texas, on September 28, 2026. © Steve Nesius, Reuters

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Wednesday authorized [SpaceX](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/spacex/) to launch up to one million satellites as part of its plan to build data centers in space. [Projects for orbiting data centers have multiplied since last year.](https://www.facebook.com/FRANCE24.English/videos/-could-we-see-data-centers-in-spacetom-standage-editor-of-the-economists-the-wor/2219908405590719/)

Alongside SpaceX and its Starmind constellation, [Google](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/google/) is pursuing its own work under the codename Suncatcher, while Blue Origin has submitted an application to the FCC for its "Project Sunrise."

Several startups are also in the race, including Starcloud, which successfully operated an advanced processor known as a GPU aboard a satellite in late 2025. Google also achieved this in October.

SpaceX's authorization runs until 2040, according to a document published Wednesday on the FCC's website.

SpaceX has the advantage of having its own rockets, which have already completed hundreds of missions.

In August, SpaceX boss [Elon Musk](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/elon-musk/) promised a first launch into orbit in the fourth quarter of 2027 and a ramp-up in 2028.

The company has struck a deal with [Nvidia](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/nvidia/), which will supply its latest-generation Vera Rubin processors, specially designed to operate in space.

Most space-based data center projects have a similar architecture: a constellation of satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO), positioned close together to ensure reliable connections between them.

Starmind's satellites will communicate with those already in orbit as part of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet network, which will then relay the data to Earth.

Other competing networks plan to receive data directly from Earth and send it back using lasers.

Not all the technical challenges have been resolved, including processors' ability to withstand the high levels of radiation in space.

Observers also point to the difficulty of withstanding extreme temperatures or avoiding damage from space debris and micrometeorites.

Locating a data center in space offers numerous advantages over building one on Earth.

Among those, a satellite in what is known as a sun-synchronous orbit can capture solar energy continuously and with eight times the efficiency of its ground-based equivalent.

_(FRANCE 24 with AFP)_

值此大埔宏富苑火灾一周年之际，财政司司长黄伟纶表示，政府已吸取事件教训，将继续支援受影响居民。
兼任房屋局局长的黄在电台节目中表示，目前仍有 13 户家庭尚未将产权出售给政府。当局将于下个月再次联系他们，讨论他们是否改变了主意。他强调，为了公平起见，政府不会提供更优惠的收购条件。黄补充说，通过立法手段收回产权将是最后一步，今年不会处理。他表示，恢复这13户家庭的权利没有硬性期限。
民政及青年事务局局长陈家英在同一节目中宣布大埔宏富法庭援助基金的两项新措施。宏富苑单位的每位业主将获得30万港元，而每位死者的家人（包括已故外籍家庭佣工的家人）将获得20万港元的“新生支援补贴”。陈茂波指出，业主的租金补贴已有所改善。
陈说，该基金仍在接收捐款，如果居民有需要，当局将用这些捐款来提供支持。

Hong Kong officials mark anniversary of Wang Fu Court fire | China Labour Bulletin Board
Thursday, 26 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong officials mark anniversary of Wang Fu Court fire
On the first anniversary of the Wang Fu Court fire in Tai Po, Financial Secretary Michael Wong said the government has learned lessons and will continue supporting residents. Secretary of Home and Youth Affairs Casper Chan announced new assistance measures, including HK$300,000 for each owner and HK
On the first anniversary of the fire at Wang Fu Court in Tai Po, Financial Secretary Michael Wong said the government has taken lessons from the incident and will continue to support affected residents.
Speaking on a radio programme, Wong, who also serves as acting Secretary for Housing, said 13 households have not yet sold their property rights to the government. Authorities will contact them again next month to discuss whether they have changed their minds. He stressed that the government will not offer more favourable acquisition terms for the sake of fairness. Wong added that using legislative means to recover property rights would be a final step, and will not be handled this year. He said there is no hard deadline for recovering the rights of those 13 households.
Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Casper Chan, speaking on the same programme, announced two new measures under the Tai Po Wang Fu Court Assistance Fund. Each owner of a unit in Wang Fu Court will receive HK$300,000, and each deceased person's family — including the family of a deceased foreign domestic helper — will receive HK$200,000 as a “new life support subsidy”. Chan noted that the rental subsidy for owners has already been improved.
Chan said the fund is still receiving donations and that authorities will use them to provide support if residents need it.

content:
AAHK 在 2027 年移交前寻找 SKYTOPIA 景点的运营商 |中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
机管局在 2027 年移交前寻找 SKYTOPIA 景点的运营商
香港机场管理局正在香港国际机场附近的 SKYTOPIA 娱乐中心寻找景点运营商，计划将 11 SKIES 打造成室内娱乐和餐饮目的地。当局将于20年4月1日从新世界发展手中接管该综合体
香港机场管理局 (AAHK) 正在为香港国际机场附近规划中的娱乐中心寻找更多景点的运营商，准备控制 11 个 SKIES，并将该综合体打造成更广泛的 SKYTOPIA 开发项目的核心。
机管局行政总裁张家辉表示，机管局预计 SKYTOPIA 会为不同年龄段的人士提供一系列互补的景点，其中一些已在计划中。更多细节可能会在 2027 年初公布，然后预计于 2028 年末和 2029 年分阶段开放。
根据一项提前终止开发商转租的协议，该机构计划于 2027 年 4 月 1 日从新世界发展手中接管 11 个 SKIES。张说，AAHK 不想将其作为传统购物中心重新开放，而是希望建立一个大型室内娱乐和餐饮目的地，购物场所仅占 20% 至 25% 的空间。
“我们希望为香港打造一个新的地标，”她说，并描述了香港居民、大湾区游客和国际旅客的目的地，其中包括航班间隔数小时的过境旅客。
SKYTOPIA是集休闲、商业、航空于一体的空港城市蓝图。其他项目包括扩建亚洲国际博览馆，设有一个可容纳 20,000 个座位的室内表演场地；规划中的机场湾码头，提供500多个游艇泊位；以及艺术品和贵重物品存储设施。张说，这些设施应该相互补充，音乐会观众可以在演出前后在娱乐中心用餐或聚集，而码头用户可以步行到达附近的景点。
访问将是该战略的另一部分。机场城干线是连接港珠澳大桥香港口岸和航天城的自主交通连接线，预计将于 2027 年开始运营，连接机场商业区。张表示，这项投资旨在加强航空业，而不是转移资源，额外的商业收入可能有助于为机场基础设施提供资金，并保持航空公司收费的竞争力。
张认为大湾区的市场、香港广泛的国际网络、独立的航权安排以及机场的服务水平是主要优势。 AAHK 希望在已建立的航线上增加班次，并连接到中亚、非洲和南美洲服务欠缺的市场，尽管新服务最终必须对航空公司具有商业可行性。她说，下一步的推动是自动化和人工智能，从自助乘客处理和自动驾驶车辆到行李处理系统和监控飞机周转操作的工具。

AAHK seeks operators for SKYTOPIA attractions ahead of 2027 handover
Airport Authority Hong Kong is seeking operators for attractions at its SKYTOPIA entertainment hub near Hong Kong International Airport, with plans to turn 11 SKIES into an indoor entertainment and dining destination. The authority will take over the complex from New World Development on April 1, 20
Airport Authority Hong Kong (AAHK) is seeking operators for more attractions at its planned entertainment hub near Hong Kong International Airport, as it prepares to take control of 11 SKIES and turn the complex into a centrepiece of its wider SKYTOPIA development.
AAHK chief executive officer Vivian Cheung Kar-fay said the authority envisages a number of complementary attractions at SKYTOPIA for different age groups, with a handful already in its plans. More details could be announced in early 2027, ahead of a phased opening targeted for late 2028 and 2029.
The authority is scheduled to take over 11 SKIES from New World Development on April 1, 2027, under an agreement to end the developer's sublease early. Rather than reopen it as a conventional mall, AAHK wants to establish a large indoor entertainment and dining destination, with shopping occupying just 20 to 25 per cent of the space, Cheung said.
“We want to build a new landmark for Hong Kong,” she said, describing a destination for residents, Greater Bay Area visitors and international travellers, including transit passengers with a few hours between flights.
SKYTOPIA is the airport-city blueprint combining leisure, commerce and aviation. Other components include the expansion of AsiaWorld-Expo, featuring a 20,000-seat indoor performance arena; the planned Airport Bay Marina, offering more than 500 yacht berths; and an art and valuables storage facility. Cheung said these facilities should reinforce one another, with concertgoers able to dine or gather at the entertainment hub before and after shows, while marina users could reach nearby attractions on foot.
Access will be another part of the strategy. The Airportcity Link, an autonomous transport connection between the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge's Hong Kong Port and SKYCITY, is expected to begin operating in 2027, providing a link to the airport's commercial district. Cheung said the investment is intended to strengthen aviation rather than divert resources from it, with additional commercial revenue potentially helping to fund airport infrastructure and keep charges for airlines competitive.
Cheung identified the Greater Bay Area's market, Hong Kong's extensive international network, its separate air traffic rights arrangements, and the airport's service standards as key advantages. AAHK wants more frequencies on established routes and connections to underserved markets in Central Asia, Africa, and South America, though new services must ultimately be commercially viable for airlines. The next push, she said, is automation and artificial intelligence, from self-service passenger processing and autonomous vehicles to baggage-handling systems and tools that monitor aircraft turnaround operations.

最近，我们的乔治城团队收到了大量媒体要求对涉及英伟达芯片技术曝光及其对美国国家安全影响的指控进行评论的请求。这些调查通常集中在中国情报部门如何进行间谍活动以及如何应对这些活动。
我们不会低估这种威胁。间谍活动、网络入侵和其他秘密活动是中国获取外国技术的长期特征。但我们十多年来的研究表明，这些活动仅占中国对外技术获取总体努力的一小部分——可能不是最大的一部分，也可以说不是最重要的。
相反，中国创建了一个全国性的生态系统，通过合法交易、非法活动和我们所说的“法外”转移的结合来运作：外部观察者无法获得其细节，其合法性也无法轻易确定。
由于这些不太引人注目的做法缺乏传统间谍活动的耸人听闻的吸引力，因此它们很少受到类似的关注。其结果是公众对中国技术获取体系的理解被扭曲，以及用于对抗该体系的资源的错误配置。
中国对外国技术的追求既不新鲜也不神秘。自 1949 年中华人民共和国成立以来，北京一直在运营完善的基础设施，用于识别、获取外国技术进步并将其改造为国内使用。
该企业包括政府部委、科研机构、商业实体、技术转移中心、专业协会、海外实验室以及旨在招募具有专业知识的科学家和工程师的项目。
它的前身可以追溯到19世纪中国努力获取西方技术，同时保留其国内政治和社会制度。历届中国政府都将这些努力正式化。其目标不仅仅是复制发明，而是利用知识产生商业和战略上有用的结果。
出于分析目的，我们将外国技术获取分为三大类。
合法转让包括购买技术、收购外国公司、联合研究、投资初创企业、海外实验室、大学合作以及招聘科研人员。这些交易本质上并不是不正当的。然而，交易可能是合法的，同时也存在战略风险。
非法转让包括传统间谍活动、网络盗窃、违反保密协议、盗窃商业秘密、所谓的“蜜罐”活动以及法律禁止的其他活动。这些是酒吧最熟悉的做法

Recently, our Georgetown team has been inundated with media requests for commentary on allegations involving the exposure of Nvidia chip technology and the implications for U.S. national security. These inquiries typically focus on how China’s intelligence services conduct espionage and what can be done to counter them.
We do not discount this threat. Espionage, cyber intrusions, and other clandestine activities are longstanding features of China’s efforts to acquire foreign technology. But our research over more than a decade suggests that these activities account for only a fraction of China’s overall foreign technology acquisition effort – probably not the largest fraction, and arguably not the most consequential.
Rather, China has created a whole-of-nation ecosystem that operates through a combination of legal transactions, illicit activities, and what we call “extralegal” transfers: arrangements whose details are unavailable to outside observers and whose legality cannot readily be established.
Because these less visible practices lack the sensational appeal of conventional espionage, they rarely receive comparable attention. The result is a distorted public understanding of China’s technology acquisition system and a misallocation of the resources intended to counter it.
China’s pursuit of foreign technology is neither new nor mysterious. Since the founding of the People’s Republic in 1949, Beijing has operated an elaborate infrastructure for identifying foreign technological advances, accessing them, and adapting them for domestic use.
The enterprise includes government ministries, scientific research institutions, commercial entities, technology transfer centers, professional associations, overseas laboratories, and programs designed to recruit scientists and engineers with specialized expertise.
Its antecedents extend further back, to China’s 19th-century efforts to acquire Western technology while preserving its domestic political and social institutions. Successive Chinese governments have formalized these efforts. The objective is not simply to copy inventions, but to leverage the knowledge to produce commercially and strategically useful results.
For analytical purposes, we distinguish among three broad categories of foreign technology acquisition.
Legal transfers include purchases of technology, foreign company acquisitions, joint research, investments in startups, overseas laboratories, university collaborations, and the recruitment of scientific personnel. These transactions are not inherently improper. Yet a transaction can be legal while also being a strategic risk.
Illegal transfers include traditional espionage, cyber theft, violations of nondisclosure agreements, theft of trade secrets, alleged “honey pot” operations, and other activities prohibited by law. These are the practices most familiar to the public, which media queries most frequently address – as in the case of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.
Extralegal transfers involve arrangements in which foreign technical knowledge is conveyed through channels that are not necessarily illegal but frequently opaque. Examples are undisclosed research affiliations, subsidized consulting, dual appointments, and the work of intermediaries whose relationships with China’s government are not apparent.
These categories are not exclusive. An otherwise legitimate collaboration may involve undisclosed conflicts of interest, while a commercial acquisition may be entirely lawful yet raise significant national security concerns.
Our concern is that the second category attracts disproportionate attention, while the first and third may facilitate transfers of equal or greater strategic consequence.
The scale and institutional character of China’s acquisition efforts distinguish them from isolated acts of industrial espionage.
One component is China’s science and technology intelligence (科技情报, STI) system. This network collects, analyzes, and distributes foreign technical information to domestic research and industrial organizations. Its civilian institutions include the Institute of Scientific and Technical Information of China, complemented by specialized organizations serving particular industries and defense requirements.
Another component is the ubiquitous “talent programs” – a network of organizations that identify and recruit overseas technical expertise. Chinese national and local authorities have sponsored numerous programs offering research funding, salaries, laboratory facilities, and other incentives to scientists and engineers working abroad.
Some arrangements involve permanent relocation to subsidized “commercialization centers.” Others permit researchers to maintain positions overseas while executing projects or consulting assignments in China. These include so-called “dual-base” (两个基地) arrangements, through which an individual may sustain professional activities in two countries.
Participation in such programs or in their global analogs – the Sino-U.S. (or Japanese, German, etc.) “professional associations” – does not by itself establish misconduct. That depends on the nature of the work, the information transferred, and whether participants comply with applicable disclosure requirements and contractual obligations.
Unlike a clandestine intelligence operation, much of this infrastructure is publicly acknowledged in Chinese government documents and institutional announcements. Its strategic significance lies not in secrecy alone, but in its organization, persistence, and cumulative effects.
Our research on China’s access to foreign artificial intelligence (AI) technology provides an instructive example.
China’s 2017 New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan explicitly encouraged cooperation with foreign universities and research institutions, the recruitment of international AI specialists, overseas mergers and acquisitions, venture capital investment, and the establishment of research facilities abroad.
Subsequent initiatives promoted international academic exchanges, joint laboratories, and other mechanisms for accessing foreign expertise. These are not clandestine activities; they are stated elements of Chinese national technology policy.
Our 2019 CSET study, “China’s Access to Foreign AI Technology,” found that the principal mechanisms supporting foreign AI acquisition were not necessarily illegal. We also concluded that many such transfers were poorly monitored and that the United States lacked sufficient information to assess their aggregate consequences.
The problem is not that U.S. counterintelligence and law enforcement agencies have exaggerated the importance of Chinese espionage. Their investigations have exposed serious threats to U.S. technological and economic security. But successful investigations can create a misleading impression of the overall threat because criminal cases are visible, measurable, and newsworthy. Legal and extralegal transfers are harder to identify, much less quantify.
This distortion has practical consequences. Measures designed to prevent the theft of classified information or proprietary technology will not necessarily address transfers occurring through legitimate research, investment, or commercial relationships.
A related danger is treating Chinese students, scientists, or Americans of Chinese ancestry as presumptive security risks. Such generalizations are unjustified, undermine useful cooperation, and can damage the United States’ ability to attract and retain needed talent.
Recognizing the full scope of China’s technology acquisition system does not imply that the United States should retreat from international scientific cooperation or attempt to prevent all technology flows to China. It does, however, suggest several priorities.
First, investments in counterintelligence should be complemented by sustained open-source research into China’s technology policies, transfer organizations, recruitment programs, commercial investments, and research relationships.
Second, research institutions and companies should have clearer guidance on disclosure obligations and the protection of sensitive research. Transparency is a more practical starting point than blanket restrictions on international collaboration.
Third and most importantly, protecting U.S. technology cannot substitute for developing it. Sustained investment in research, education, and infrastructure is the best way to sustain American technological competitiveness.
The latest allegations involving semiconductor technology deserve serious investigation. Where wrongdoing is established, legal remedies should follow. But individual espionage cases are not an adequate guide to the scale or character of China’s efforts to acquire foreign technology. The strategic challenge is China’s system for acquiring foreign technology, not merely the spies. Until U.S. policymakers and the public recognize that distinction, we are prosecuting only the most visible part of a problem whose larger dimensions remain poorly understood.

Yip Ka-kui survived Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades, but he lost his home and his wife. Their half-melted wedding rings are among the few traces that remain of their lives. Hongkongers pay tribute on December 2, 2025, to the victims who died in the fatal fire in Tai Po Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. A year after the devastating November 26, 2025 fire killed 168 people in a Hong Kong housing estate, survivors and bereaved families are struggling with their loss. AFP spoke to survivors of the world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980: Yip Ka-kui Yip, 68, often finds himself retracing the path to the apartment complex that he used to take with his wife of four decades, Pak Shui-lin, whose death he says he still “cannot accept”. Embed from Getty Images Survivors say Pak saved lives by knocking on neighbours’ doors to alert them to the fire. Simple moments of daily life remind Yip of her absence. It’s as though “she is at home waiting for me to return”, he said. He still sends life updates, such as their granddaughter’s report card, to his wife’s number. Yip also sent their half-melted wedding rings for restoration, hoping that objects salvaged from the ruins can be passed down through generations as a reminder of the incident. The government’s apology “lacked sincerity”, he told AFP, adding that he hoped the society would ensure “justice is served”. Chu Chu, 38, recalled a coroner lifting the cloth covering his 76-year-old father’s charred remains recovered from their gutted flat, stirring ashes into the air. Embed from Getty Images “It felt like my dad was actually vanishing into the sands of time,” he said. “I feel like I haven’t found my dad. Not long before the fire, I could still talk to him. “I still can’t fathom what I saw in the mortuary was actually him.” His 45-year-old sister also fears their memories of their father might “drift away” after his belongings were destroyed. She still keeps the milk candies he gave her son for his birthday, six days before the fire. Their father used to work as a vehicle mechanic for the colonial-era British garrison and as a night-shift taxi driver. Among his belongings that survived the fire were a military blade and a jar of 50-cent coins — symbols of his hardworking spirit and unconditional love for the family, the siblings said. Betty Ho Ho, 61, lived in the housing estate for 35 years and spent two decades paying off her apartment. Embed from Getty Images She had just begun to enjoy retirement when she said the fire “took everything away from me”. For Ho, the tragedy revealed “problems with the entire system and the government structure”. Officials, she said, failed to heed residents’ complaints before the fire. She now lives in government-arranged temporary housing, but is reluctant to call it home. Unlike most other residents, Ho did not accept a government buyout and instead called for the housing complex to be rebuilt on the same site — a proposal rejected by authorities. “That home is so close, but you can’t go back,” she said at her current residence, from which she can see her old flat. Ho said she felt “helpless” a year after the disaster. “It’s impossible to think about the next five years, I can’t even imagine it.” Harry Leung Leung was among the last residents to escape the fire. “We didn’t properly say goodbye to a place where we had lived for so long,” said Leung, who was in his late 20s and had lived in the flat since childhood. He said he took the government’s buyout offer out of necessity. Wang Fuk Court on November 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “(The officials) had sugarcoated this as a mutually agreeable transaction,” he told AFP. As part of the buyout scheme, he bought another property but was saddled with more than HK$1 million (US$128,000) in debt. That financial burden was “never part of my life plan”, he added. “I’m still young… but for other residents who have already retired and may have little income, such change is an overburden for them.” Rhodora Alcaraz Tunacao Tunacao, 29, was a Filipino migrant domestic worker widely hailed as a hero for protecting a three-month-old baby girl during the fire one day after starting work in Hong Kong. Embed from Getty Images After being treated in the intensive care unit for smoke inhalation, she returned to the Philippines in December. But she remains under emotional stress, according to Esther Tse, an advocate for workers rights who visits her regularly. Tunacao also suffers from lung problems, requiring regular follow-ups and medication, Tse said. At times, she coughed up black phlegm. She needs depression medication and is easily agitated, but mental health professionals are scarce in her region, Tse added.

title: Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy: Why Hong Kong’s works regulation must break from civil service culture
zh_title: 宏福苑火灾惨案：为何香港的工程规管必须脱离公务员文化
summary: 宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们考虑一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第二）
content:
宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们考虑一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第一）。然而，我们在宏福苑火灾悲剧和其他与工程相关的丑闻中却表现出了监管的无能。调查火灾的独立审查委员会将监管失误描述为“系统性和普遍性”。香港在金融服务、公共卫生、诚信（反腐败）和其他领域的监管无疑相对较好。因此评价很高。因此，我们不能说工程监管的缺位和/或不力（不仅是宏福苑火灾，还有玛丽医院电梯事件、太宗电梯防火板事件等）代表了整个香港的公共监管。问题是，为什么建筑监管如此草率和参差不齐，明显优先考虑行政便利，或许还保护建筑业？
政府的工务部门历史悠久，是殖民地香港最早的政府职能之一，人员全部由公务员组成。当局于 1843 年设立测量总署。1870 年演变为测量部，并于 1883 年更名为工务署 (PWD)。工务署管理所有工务职能。 1982 年，官员们将这个庞然大物拆分为七个工程部门。它们大多由现任发展局局长监管。该报告向我们表明，几十年来，监管制度未能充分优先考虑服务和保护公众的情况一直被容忍。那些领导建筑和建设的人大多是从公务员队伍内部提拔的，公务员队伍分为专业队伍。新入职的公务员在进入时就已经融入了本部门实践中的价值观。团队领导者和团队成员执行非正式规范，指导新进入者应如何行事以及对他们的期望。接受这些非正式规范对于在部门中相处和取得进步是必要的。 “不要破坏现状”的文化占主导地位。官僚问责制度在这些规范内运作。官僚文化具有“粘性”，难以改变。现在想想我们表现良好的监管机构：香港金融管理局、证券及期货事务监察委员会、廉政公署。
在最近的各个时期，这些当局都是在公务员系统之外设立的。在这些当局中，当局优先考虑的是与过去的做法的彻底决裂。独立委员会关于宏福苑火灾的报告副本，2026 年 10 月 29 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。委员会对火灾的审查报告特别指出了住房部门独立检查组（ICU）的行为。独立审查组本应监督宏福苑的外墙翻新和维护工作，批准计划、进行检查并确保符合建筑安全标准。作者

【原文 English Original】
A year on from the Wang Fuk Court blaze, which claimed 168 lives, let’s consider whether the government’s response is sufficient. Authorities apologised and housing chief Winnie Ho resigned. These are welcome moves, and the focus now is on reform. But one area stands out: Hong Kong’s apparently uneven regulatory quality. Hongkongers pay tribute to victims who died in the fatal fire in Tai Po Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The World Bank rates Hong Kong’s regulatory regime highly. The city ranks eighth out of some 200 territories globally and second in Asia after Singapore (globally ranked as No. 1). And yet we have demonstrated regulatory incapacity in the Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy and other works-related scandals. The independent review committee looking into the blaze described the regulatory failings as “ systematic and pervasive .” Hong Kong regulates financial services, public health, integrity (anti-corruption) and undoubtedly other areas relatively well. Hence the high rating. So, we cannot say that absent and/or poor works regulation (not only the Wang Fuk Court fire disaster, but the Queen Mary Hospital elevator case , the Taizoom elevator fire panel case , etc.) is representative of Hong Kong public regulation as a whole. The question is why building and construction regulation is so sloppy and uneven, apparently prioritising administrative convenience and perhaps protecting the construction industry? The works side of the government is ancient, created among the earliest government functions in colonial Hong Kong and staffed entirely by civil servants. Authorities set up the Surveyor General’s Office in 1843. It morphed into the Survey Department in 1870, and was renamed the Public Works Department (PWD) in 1883. PWD managed all works functions. In 1982, officials broke up this behemoth into seven works departments. They are mostly supervised by the Secretary for Development who is still in her post. The report shows us that a regulatory regime hat failed to sufficiently prioritise serving and protecting the public was tolerated for decades. Those leading building and construction are mostly promoted from within the civil service, which is organised into professional streams. Newly hired civil servants are socialised into the values in practice of their department when they enter. Team leaders and team members enforce informal norms that guide new entrants into how they should behave and what is expected of them. Accepting these informal norms is necessary to get along and ahead in the department. A “don’t rock the boat” culture dominates. Bureaucratic accountability systems operate within these norms. Bureaucratic culture is “sticky” and difficult to change. Now consider our well-performing regulators: the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Securities and Futures Commission, the Independent Commission Against Corruption. Each of relatively recent vintage, these authorities were set up outside the civil service. In them, authorities prioritised a sharp break from past practice. Copies of the independent committee’s report on the Wang Fuk Court fire, on October 29, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The committee review report into the fire singles out the behaviour of the housing department’s Independent Checking Unit (ICU). The ICU was supposed to supervise external wall renovation and maintenance work at Wang Fuk Court, approving plans, conducting inspections and ensuring compliance with building safety standards. Authorities classified Wang Fuk Court’s renovation as lower-risk “minor works” although it was an eye-popping HK$330 million project. This reduced the statutory level of ICU oversight required. The unit was also responsible for investigating and addressing residents’ reports and safety complaints. The report noted in particular the ICU’s “lack of sense of crisis, regulatory lapses, systemic blind spots, and enforcement failures.” This is a damning judgement. The ICU is composed of senior professionals including many structural engineers, maintenance surveyors, architects, and technical staff. Not only did the ICU fail in its duty to serve and protect citizens, but the professionals among them failed in their duty to uphold the values of professionalism, integrity, and excellence. The government set up a new public housing building control section which is welcome. But transferring the existing ICU staff who bring with them values in practice that led to the tragedy is a mistake. I urge the government to set up a new body outside the existing works bureaucracy. Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on December 2, 2025, days after a fatal fire engulfed seven of the eight blocks of the residential estate. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Beyond government, action is needed too. Professional bodies should enforce discipline among their members. Many professionals were involved in the various works scandals. Professional bodies such as the Engineers Registration Board should investigate those involved, and if found culpable, take action with consequences, such as suspending or cancelling their licences to practise in Hong Kong.
