reported control transfers in May-Jul. 2016"}]} Notes [1] A cooptee is an MSS collaborator, whom the ministry uses for operational support—typically in exchange for favors. They can help make introductions, serve as a go-between for the MSS and a source, provide excuses for sources to travel to the PRC, or otherwise assist the MSS in its operations. The MSS may also approach these people because of the access, business, or other ability that they have to support operations ( National Interest , June 11, 2017). [2] In November 2014, CITIC Securities (中信证券) bought a 3.8 percent stake in a technology firm under a stock return swap with Hexi, helping Gu gain control of the listed company ( CSRC , May 12, 2017). Ms. Huang worked in securities financing at CITIC at the time. The deal may have brought her into contact with Kang a year before she joined Hexi ( Hexi Investment , March 17, 2017). [3] In 2014, Hexi subscribed for shares in Century Huatong connected to its acquisitions of Tianyou Software (天游软件) and Wuxi SevenCool (无锡七酷网络). In 2017, Wuxi SevenCool sold the gaming company Hangzhou Shengfeng (杭州盛锋) to Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), whose ultimate controller is Kang (CNINF, March 9, 2014 , March 7, 2017 ). [4] The name of this firm, Shanghai Lingsu (上海凌素), closely resembles another firm within Ms. Huang’s business network, Shanghai Lingsuda (上海领素达), which invests primarily in smart mobility and ride-hailing platforms (see the Interactive Map) ( CAIC , August 16, 2023; Hong Kong Exchange , December 23, 2024). Yunxi also entered the ownership chain of a data center holding company, also based in Shanghai, and in 2025 changed its own registered name to Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing Data Group (上海珑腾智算数据集团) ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 13, 2023; Times Weekly , November 9). In Shanghai business circles, it is common to register a series of companies with names that share the same Chinese characters or use different characters with the same pronunciation. Other businesspeople can then easily tell who actually controls a company from its name alone. [5] Kang had previously used companies he controlled, including Hexi, to take over three major Phicomm shareholding vehicles ( Sina Finance , August 10, 2018). [6] Such data centers under Kang’s control, with refurbishment nearing completion, would very likely use Nvidia chips smuggled into the PRC through Huang’s Megaspeed. [7] The business tactic of offering one’s spouse to another man reaches even much further back. During the Warring States period, Zichu (子楚), a prince of Qin (秦), took an interest in Zhao Ji (赵姬), the consort of the merchant Lu Buwei (吕不韦). Lu, considering how much he had already bet on Zichu to be the next King of Qin, offered Zhao Ji, who was already pregnant, to him. After Zichu became king of Qin, Lu was appointed chancellor and wielded power over the Qin court ( Records of the Grand Historian , accessed November 11). A historical conspiracy theory even held that Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇), first emperor of ancient China, was Lu and Zhao Ji’s son. In the early 2010s, PRC financial media and business books often portrayed Lu Buwei as a merchant who knew how to bet on real power (through whatever means), fueling an interest in him among businessmen of the era (see Fortune China , March 23, 2011). That was precisely when Kang rose to prominence in business. The post Alice Huang’s Shady Shanghai Ties to Business and Government appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Launch Preview: Russian, Chinese, and SpaceX rockets to launch space station missions
zh_title: 发射预览：俄罗斯、中国和 SpaceX 火箭将发射空间站任务
summary: 十枚火箭将于下周发射，其中三枚将访问近地轨道上的两个不同空间站。进步号 MS-36 和 CRS NG-25 预计将向国际空间站运送物资，而神舟二十四号计划将下一批宇航员送入中国天宫空间站，其中包括第一位国际访客。除了空间站飞行之外，猎鹰 9 号还将从范登堡发射两次 USSF 任务，而中国也将向轨道发射四联有效载荷。最后，Electron 将发射一颗合成孔径雷达卫星。联盟号2.1b
content:
十枚火箭将于下周发射，其中三枚将访问近地轨道上的两个不同空间站。进步号 MS-36 和 CRS NG-25 预计将向国际空间站运送物资，而神舟二十四号计划将下一批宇航员送入中国天宫空间站，其中包括第一位国际访客。除了空间站飞行之外，猎鹰 9 号还将从范登堡发射两次 USSF 任务，而中国也将向轨道发射四联有效载荷。最后，Electron 将发射一颗合成孔径雷达卫星。联盟号 2.1b |进步 MS-36 11 月 24 日星期二，俄罗斯向国际空间站 (ISS) 发射了进步 MS-36。 Progress MS-36 于世界标准时间 10:13 从哈萨克斯坦拜科努尔航天发射场的 Site 31/6 升空。 Progress MS-36，也被 NASA 称为 Progress 97P，是对国际空间站的补给任务。 Progress 是一艘源自联盟号的航天器，能够携带约 2.5 吨的货物到国际空间站。 Progress MS-36 是 Progress 的第 189 次飞行，于 1978 年首次飞行并与礼炮 6 号空间站对接。 Progress MS-32 从拜科努尔航天发射场升空。 （图片来源：NASA+）联盟 2.1b 是一款三级煤油和液氧运载火箭，源自 R-7 洲际弹道导弹。联盟号 2.1b 可以向近地轨道 (LEO) 输送高达 8,700 公斤的重量。可以配备可选的第四级 Fregat 或 Volga，用于最终轨道调整。
周二的飞行将是联盟号 2.1b 2026 年的第 10 次飞行，也是整体的第 109 次飞行。 阿丽亚娜 64 |亚马逊狮子座 (LE-04) 在周二的三次发射中的第二次，阿丽亚娜 64 火箭向近地轨道发射了另一批 36 颗亚马逊狮子座卫星。发射窗口于世界标准时间 10:45 开始，并延长至世界标准时间 11:14，阿丽亚娜 6 号在该窗口结束时发射。这次发射是阿丽亚娜 6 号计划进行的 18 次狮子座发射中的第四次。阿丽亚娜 6 是由阿丽亚娜集团为欧洲航天局开发的两级液氢和液氧动力火箭。阿丽亚娜 6 可以配备两个或四个固体火箭助推器来增加升空推力，LE-04 则配备四个。周二的发射是 2026 年阿丽亚娜 6 号的第五次发射任务，也是总共的第十次飞行。阿丽亚娜 64 在 LE-01 任务期间上升（图片来源：ESA/M. Pédoussau） Falcon 9 | USSF-266 在周二的第三次发射中，猎鹰 9 号为美国太空军 (USSF) 发射了一个机密有效载荷。 USSF-266 原定于 11 月 23 日星期一从加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 于 11 月 24 日发射升空。 USSF-266 的发射窗口于太平洋标准时间上午 7:55（世界标准时间 15:55）开始，并延长至太平洋标准时间上午 11:55（世界标准时间 19:55），猎鹰 9 号于太平洋标准时间上午 11:08（世界标准时间 19:08）发射。根据空投区，USSF-266 很可能是 USSF 天基机载移动目标指示器计划 (SB-AMTI) 的一部分。 SB-AMTI 是在 Starshield 卫星总线的基础上构建的，而 Starshield 卫星总线本身又源自 Starlink 卫星总线。
助推器 B1081 进行了第 29 次飞行，之前曾飞行过 Crew 7、CRS-29、PACE、Transporter 10 和 13、EarthCARE、NROL-186 和 -48、TRACERS & Others、CSG-3、USSF-153 和 USSF-481。这款特殊助推器是从 SpaceX 目前所有活跃的 Falcon 9 发射台上进行过飞行的少数助推器之一。 B1081 在发射后大约八分钟降落在 SpaceX 的无人机“当然我仍然爱你”在太平洋上。长征2F/G |神舟二十四号周三，中国向天宫空间站发射了下一次载人飞行任务。她

【原文 English Original】
Ten rockets are set to launch over the next week, with three visiting two different space stations in low-Earth orbit. Progress MS-36 and CRS NG-25 are expected to deliver supplies to the International Space Station, while Shenzhou 24 is scheduled to launch the next crew to the Chinese Tiangong Space Station, including its first international visitor. Outside of space station flights, Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of USSF missions from Vandenberg, and China is set to launch a quadruple-header of payloads to orbit. Lastly, Electron will launch a synthetic aperture radar satellite. Soyuz 2.1b | Progress MS-36 On Tuesday, Nov. 24, Russia launched the Progress MS-36 to the International Space Station (ISS). Progress MS-36 lifted off at 10:13 UTC from Site 31/6 at the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. Progress MS-36, also called Progress 97P by NASA, is a resupply mission to the ISS. Progress is a Soyuz-derived spacecraft capable of carrying around 2.5 tonnes of cargo to the Station. Progress MS-36 served as the 189th flight of Progress, which first flew in 1978 and docked with the Salyut 6 space station. Progress MS-32 lifts off from Baikonur Cosmodrome. (Credit: NASA+) Soyuz 2.1b is a three-stage kerosene-and-liquid-oxygen launch vehicle derived from the R-7 intercontinental ballistic missile. Soyuz 2.1b can deliver up to 8,700 kg to low-Earth orbit (LEO). An optional fourth stage, Fregat or Volga, can be equipped for final orbital adjustments. Tuesday’s flight will be the 10th Soyuz 2.1b flight in 2026 and the 109th overall. Ariane 64 | Amazon Leo (LE-04) The second of three launches on Tuesday saw an Ariane 64 rocket deliver another batch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites to LEO. The launch window opened at 10:45 UTC and extended until 11:14 UTC, with Ariane 6 launching at the end of the window. This launch was the fourth of 18 Leo launches scheduled on Ariane 6. Ariane 6 is a two-stage, liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen-powered rocket developed by ArianeGroup for the European Space Agency. Ariane 6 can be equipped with either two or four solid rocket boosters to augment liftoff thrust, with LE-04 flying with four. Tuesday’s launch was the fifth Ariane 6 mission of 2026, and the 10th flight overall. Ariane 64 ascents during the LE-01 mission (Credit: ESA/M. Pédoussau) Falcon 9 | USSF-266 The third launch on Tuesday saw Falcon 9 launch a classified payload for the United States Space Force (USSF). Originally scheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, USSF-266 launched on Nov. 24 from Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) in California. The launch window for USSF-266 opened at 7:55 AM PST (15:55 UTC) and extended until 11:55 AM PST (19:55 UTC), with Falcon 9 launching at 11:08 AM PST (19:08 UTC). Based on drop zones, USSF-266 is most likely part of the USSF’s Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator Program (SB-AMTI). SB-AMTI is built off of the Starshield satellite bus, which itself is derived from the Starlink satellite bus. Booster B1081 flew its 29th flight after previously flying Crew 7, CRS-29, PACE, Transporter 10 and 13, EarthCARE, NROL-186 and -48, TRACERS & Others, CSG-3, USSF-153, and USSF-481. This particular booster is one of a few boosters to have flown from all of SpaceX’s currently active Falcon 9 pads. B1081 landed on SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific approximately eight minutes after launch. Chang Zheng 2F/G | Shenzhou 24 On Wednesday, China launched its next crewed mission to its Tiangong Space Station. Shenzhou 24 lifted off from Site 91 at the Jiquan Satellite Launch Complex (JSLC). The launch is currently set for 10 minutes into a 40-minute-long window at 00:18 UTC. The crew was launched aboard a Chang Zheng 2F/G (CZ-2F/G) rocket, which has carried every Chinese crewed mission to date. The three-person crew flew to Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou spacecraft, which borrows many characteristics and designs from Russia’s crewed Soyuz vehicle. Chang Zheng 2F/G with Shenzhou 24 leaves the assembly building. (Credit: CCTV) Shenzhou 24 features a crew of three astronauts, with two Chinese taikonauts, Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, and one Pakistani astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Shenzhou 24 will be Ali’s first spaceflight, and he will spend a short duration aboard Tiangong. This flight marks the first time a non-Chinese astronaut has ever visited Tiangong, which has been in orbit since 2021. The CZ-2F/G is a two-stage, hypergolic rocket equipped with four side boosters that stand 58 m tall. The vehicle is fueled by dinitrogen tetroxide and unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine (UDMH), both of which are highly carcinogenic. Shenzhou 24 will be the 18th crewed Chinese flight and the 24th overall in the Shenzhou program. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload The first of two launches on Thursday features a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) that will deliver an unknown payload to orbit. This mission is set to liftoff at 09:35 UTC, five minutes into a 22-minute window, from Launch Complex 3 (LC-3) at the Xichang Satellite Launch Center. CZ-2D is a two-stage launch vehicle, with an optional third stage, standing 41 m tall. The rocket is powered by hypergolic fuels and is capable of lofting 3,500 kg to LEO. Thursday’s flight will be the eighth mission of 2026 for CZ-2D, and the 109th overall. Electron | Night Owls Never Sleep Flying from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on Friday, Nov 27, Rocket Lab’s Electron will launch a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite to LEO for Synspective. The mission, named “Night Owls Never Sleep,” is scheduled to liftoff at 00:05 UTC. SAR is used to image the surface of the Earth and can penetrate through cloud layers. Launch 101 coming right up. We're preparing to launch our 101st Electron next week to deploy another StriX Earth-imaging spacecraft for @synspective . The "Night Owls Never Sleep" launch window opens: 1:00 pm NZDT, Nov 27 00:00 UTC, Nov 27 9:00 am JST, Nov 27 7:00 pm… pic.twitter.com/pfblD6s70R — Rocket Lab (@RocketLab) November 20, 2026 Electron is a two-stage, small-lift vehicle capable of delivering up to 300 kg to LEO. The vehicle is fueled by liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen, which powers nine Rutherford engines on the first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Rutherford on the second stage. This mission will serve as Electron’s 22nd mission of 2026 and 101st overall. Chang Zheng 6A | Unknown Payload On Friday, China is set to launch a Chang Zheng 6A (CZ-6A) from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, carrying an unknown payload into orbit. The launch window opens at 12:53 UTC and extends until 13:15 UTC. Currently, liftoff is scheduled for seven minutes into the window at 13:00 UTC. CZ-6A is a two-stage, liquid kerosene-and-liquid-oxygen rocket capable of delivering up to 8,000 kg to LEO. CZ-6A is additionally powered by four solid rocket boosters, which augment first-stage thrust. The vehicle stands 50 m tall with a normal fairing or 52 m tall with an extended fairing. This flight will serve as the 10th CZ-6A mission of 2026 and 29th overall. Chang Zheng 6C | Unknown Payload The last launch of the week from China features a Chang Zheng 6C (CZ-6C) also launching from Taiyuan, delivering an unknown payload to LEO. The launch window opens at 03:46 UTC and extends until 04:15 UTC, with liftoff scheduled for 03:50 UTC, four minutes into the window. CZ-6C is a two-stage, liquid kerosene- and liquid oxygen-powered rocket capable of delivering 4,500 kg to LEO. CZ-6C stands 43 m tall and is considered a single-stick variant of CZ-6A, flying without the solid rocket boosters. Sunday’s launch will be CZ-6C’s second of 2026, and third overall. Falcon 9 | USSF-380 Falcon 9 is set to fly again from VSFB on Sunday, delivering USSF-380 to LEO for the USSF. The launch window opens at 8:39 PM PST on Nov. 28 (04:39 UTC on Nov. 29) and extends until 2:39 AM PST (08:39 UTC, both on Nov. 29). USSF-380 is a classified mission for the USSF but is believed to be part of its Space-Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio. SBST is built off of the Starshield satellite bus. The exact number of satellites being launched is unknown but is believed to be similar to that of a typical Starlink mission, based on Falcon 9’s drop zones. Booster B1082 will support this mission on its 27th flight. B1082 has previously supported USSF-62 (WSF-M 1), OneWeb #20, NROL-145, Transporter 18, and 22 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, B1082 will land aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You approximately eight minutes after launch. Falcon 9 | CRS NG-25 The final launch of the week will see a Falcon 9 deliver the CRS NG-25 cargo resupply mission to the ISS. CRS NG-25 will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) in Florida, with the instantaneous launch window opening on Sunday, Nov 29, at 10:50 AM EST (15:50 UTC). Cygnus XL approaches the ISS for berthing. (Credit: NASA) CRS NG-25 will be the fifth of six planned Cygnus flights aboard Falcon 9, as Northrop Grumman and Firefly Aerospace work to bring their upcoming Antares 330 rocket online in the near future. Additionally, CRS NG-25 will be the third flight of Cygnus XL, which can carry 5,000 kg of cargo to the Station. CRS NG-25’s Cygnus XL is named “ SS James ‘Jim’ Lovell ” after the Apollo 8 and Apollo 13 astronaut who passed away in August 2025. Supporting CRS NG-25 will be booster B1096 on its ninth flight. B1096 has previously supported the Starlink Group 6-87, KF-01, NROL-77, NROL-95, GPS III SV09, CRS-34, CRS-35, and IMAP & Others missions. The booster will return to CCSFS to land at Landing Zone 40 (LZ-40), which is located directly adjacent to SLC-40. Sunday’s recovery attempt will be Falcon 9’s 700th attempted recovery, of which 682 have been successful. CRS NG-25 will serve as the 125th Falcon 9 mission and the 281st orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. (Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches from Florida. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Russian, Chinese, and SpaceX rockets to launch space station missions appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .

title: Observations from Taiwan’s Education Frontline amid Cognitive Warfare
zh_title: 认知战中台湾教育前线的观察
source: 华盛顿全球台湾研究中心

content:
下载整期 PDF 作为全球台湾研究所致力于促进声音多元化的一部分，全球台湾简报偶尔会发表台湾年轻人撰写的文章。我们很高兴以一名高中生的视角来阐述年轻人在复杂的互联网信息环境中所面临的挑战，以及台湾学校关于公民教育的持续争论。台湾面临着一些严重的威胁，不仅来自直接的军事力量，还来自我在同龄人中经常看到的自我挫败的态度。尽管外国观察家警告两岸可能发生冲突，但年轻人流行的社交媒体平台上却充斥着“战争不会爆发”、“台湾无论如何也不会赢”或“谁统治我们并不重要”等言论。但这些言论并不代表台湾大多数青年群体的声音，也不应被视为整个一代人放弃的证据。然而，随着对民主的冷漠成为日常谈话的一部分，它产生了一种值得关注的脆弱性。问题的出现并不仅仅是因为一些学生对政治了解太少。事实上，我们许多人在与我们学校设计的环境截然不同的信息环境中遭遇政治。公民教育仍然主要通过教科书、考试和课堂讲座进行。
然而，政治叙事现在通过短视频、影响者、模因和推荐算法传达给我们。如果学校以中立的名义避免讨论有争议的问题，学生将不会变得政治中立：相反，他们会去其他地方学习政治。当政治通过信息传播时 中国社交媒体平台已成为台湾信息环境的重要组成部分。 TikTok、抖音和 Rednote 等平台模糊了娱乐和政治影响力之间的界限。事实上，可能影响台湾人的内容并不总是需要采用明显的宣传。现代天际线、高铁、传统文化、美食、乡村生活、普通家庭的视频都能让中国成为一个熟悉而有吸引力的国家。政治信息可以通过娱乐视频传播，而台湾年轻人可能根本不认为这些是政治信息。这不是一个边缘问题。事实上，Doublethink Lab 2025 年的一项研究（使用台湾传播调查的数据）发现，50.73% 的高中生使用 TikTok。研究人员还采访了 16 名 15 岁至 18 岁的台湾用户，发现政治视频有时会意外地出现在社交媒体群组中，尤其是在 2024 年总统选举前后。尽管如此，研究人员发现，大多数青少年仍然对中华人民共和国政府持负面看法，反对统一。
因此，声称使用中国平台会让台湾青少年“亲中国”的说法过于简单化。更重要的问题可能是台湾年轻人在这些平台上遇到什么样的政治信息，以及他们如何理解这些信息。当我们超越屏幕上出现的内容时，这种担忧变得更加清晰。 2025 年对 700 名台湾 Z 世代成员进行的一项同行评审研究发现，更频繁地使用中国社交媒体平台（包括 TikTok、Rednote 和微博）与对两岸事务的政治了解较低有关

DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF As part of the Global Taiwan Institute’s commitment to promoting a diversity of voices, the Global Taiwan Brief occasionally publishes articles written by Taiwanese youth. We are pleased to present this perspective from a high school student about the challenges young people face in navigating a complex internet information environment, and continuing debates over civic education in Taiwan’s schools. Taiwan faces several serious threats, not only from direct military forces, but also from a self-defeating attitude that I see frequently in people of my age. While foreign observers warn of the possibility of a cross-Strait conflict, social media platforms popular among young people are filled with claims that “War won’t break out,” “Taiwan could never win anyway,” or “It doesn’t matter who governs us.” Nonetheless, these statements do not represent the voice of the majority of youth groups in Taiwan, and they should not be seen as proof that the entire generation has given up. However, as indifference toward democracy becomes a part of everyday conversation, it creates a sort of vulnerability that deserves attention. The problem arises not simply because some students know too little about politics. In fact, many of us encounter politics in an information environment very different from the one for which our schools were designed. Civic education still largely proceeds through textbooks, exams, and classroom lectures. Political narratives, however, now reach us through short videos, influencers, memes, and recommendation algorithms. If schools avoid discussing controversial issues in the name of neutrality, students will not become politically neutral: instead, they will go somewhere else to learn about politics. When Politics Spreads Through the Feed Chinese social media platforms have become a major part of Taiwan’s information environment. Platforms such as TikTok, Douyin, and Rednote blur the line between entertainment and political influence. Indeed, content that may impact Taiwanese does not always have to employ obvious propaganda. Videos of modern skylines , high-speed rail, traditional culture, food, rural life, or ordinary families can render China a familiar and attractive country. Political messages can then spread through entertainment videos, and Taiwanese youth may not perceive these as political messages at all. This is not a marginal issue. In fact, a 2025 Doublethink Lab study —using data from the Taiwan Communication Survey—found that 50.73 percent of high-school students used TikTok. Researchers also interviewed sixteen Taiwanese users aged fifteen to eighteen and discovered that political videos had sometimes appeared unexpectedly in social media groups, especially around the 2024 presidential election. Nonetheless, the researchers found that most of these teenagers still had negative views of the PRC government and opposed unification. It is thus an oversimplification to claim that using Chinese platforms makes Taiwanese teenagers “pro-China.” The more important question may be what kind of political information Taiwanese youth encounter on those platforms, and how they understand it. That concern becomes clearer when we look beyond what appears on the screen. A 2025 peer-reviewed study of 700 members of Taiwan’s Generation Z found that more frequent use of Chinese social media platforms—including TikTok, Rednote, and Weibo—was associated with lower political knowledge about cross-Strait affairs, and a weaker ability to tell the different usages of language between China and Taiwan. Greater use of Chinese social media was also linked to a decreased ability to identify People’s Republic of China (PRC) disinformation. This does not necessarily mean that young people are being “brainwashed.” The problem may be more subtle. If people have less knowledge about an issue, it becomes harder for them to judge whether the information they see is reliable in the first place. The numbers from another Doublethink Lab nationwide survey make this picture even more complicated. Among 2,612 Taiwanese respondents aged fifteen and above, the majority of both frequent and non-frequent TikTok users rejected the idea of giving up democracy for cross-Strait peace. Yet there was still a difference between the frequent and non-frequent users. The study found that 30.3 percent of frequent users were willing to accept giving up democracy for peace, compared with 23.4 percent of non-frequent users. Frequent users were also more likely to believe that unification with China might not significantly change everyday life in Taiwan. These numbers do not prove that TikTok caused these attitudes. But they do suggest that cognitive influence does not have to make young Taiwanese actively admire Beijing. Sometimes, it may simply make the differences between democratic and authoritarian systems feel less important, or make resistance seem less worthwhile. What “Politics Out of Schools” Originally Meant If political influence increasingly reaches students through their phones, then Taiwan must also ask what role schools should play. Here, our democratic history creates an ironic situation. During the authoritarian period of Taiwan, politics was not absent from Taiwanese campuses. Rather, politics was deeply intertwined with education. Historical records show that Kuomintang (國民黨) organizations, the China Youth Corps (中國青年救國團), military instructors, and state security agencies were involved in monitoring and managing university campuses. In 1986 and 1987, as Taiwan moved toward democratization, students involved in the “Freedom of Love” movement (自由之愛運動) at National Taiwan University demanded freedom of speech, university autonomy, and reform of the University Act (大學法) , as well as the removal of party organizations, the Youth Corps, and military instructors from campuses. This history matters because the original democratic demand was not that students should stop discussing politics. Instead, it was that the party-state should stop controlling political life in schools. Indeed, demands for political institutions to leave campuses appeared alongside demands for greater freedom of expression. Removing political control is not the same as removing political discussion. Taiwan’s legal framework still reflects this distinction. Article 6 of the Educational Fundamental Act (教育基本法) requires education to follow a principle of neutrality and prohibits schools from either campaigning for particular political organizations, or forcing teachers and students to participate in political activities. The restriction is directed at the institution, not at the student. Taiwan democratized its schools by making institutions politically neutral, not by requiring students to be politically silent. Image: A teacher and students at Baozhong Junior High School in Yunlin County, Taiwan (December 2019). Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) From Political Neutrality to Political Silence Yet in practice, the memory of authoritarian political indoctrination may have encouraged a broader habit of avoiding controversial politics in school. The idea that “politics should not enter schools” (政治不入校園) can be interpreted not only as a warning against party control, but also as a reason for teachers to avoid politically sensitive issues. This is different from the original purpose of educational neutrality, which was to protect students from forced ideology, rather than to stop them from discussing political life. The same tension can also be seen inside schools. A National Academy for Educational Research (國家教育研究院) survey of high-school history teachers found broad support for teaching transitional justice, but more than 60 percent of teachers worried that such teaching could be influenced by partisan viewpoints. Among teachers who did not design additional lessons on transitional justice, fear of being accused of partisan indoctrination was the second most common reason— after lack of class time. This does not mean that teachers do not want to discuss politics. Rather, it shows how easily civic education can be confused with political indoctrination, even in a democratic society. The tension is especially clear because Taiwan’s curriculum has moved in the opposite direction. The 108 Curriculum (108課綱) included transitional justice in high-school history, and education researchers have also recommended using multiple historical perspectives to encourage discussion and reflection. Formally, schools are therefore expected to help students think critically about history, understand different perspectives, and reflect on democratic values. At the same time, teachers may still worry about being accused of taking sides. As many of my classmates have noticed, political issues can therefore become exam facts that we memorize for answer sheets, but quickly escape our memory. Civics exists as an academic subject, but politics does not always become part of students’ real lives. History can feel distant from our own identities, while democratic rights become background conditions that we assume will always exist. When students then hear “If there’s war, just surrender” or “It doesn’t matter who is in charge,” they may understand the danger of war without having seriously thought about what political change could mean for freedom of speech, elections, personal rights, or the rule of law. This is where the role of the classroom becomes important. Schools should not tell students which party to support or what position to take on cross-Strait relations. Instead, they should give students a place to ask questions, test claims, compare evidence, and discuss difficult issues. Research using data from 3,953 Taiwanese students in the International Civic and Citizenship Education Study found that an open classroom climate for discussion was associated with stronger civic knowledge and expected electoral participation. In other words, students do not become better citizens simply because disagreement is kept out of the classroom. They need opportunities to learn how to disagree while still respecting evidence, rights, and one another. Rebuilding Civic Resilience Taiwan can learn from the experiences of other democracies. Austria has included political education in its formal education system and emphasizes that controversial issues should also be presented as controversial in the classroom, while avoiding political indoctrination. Finland , meanwhile, treats media literacy as an important part of education and integrates it across subjects, helping students understand information, media, and misleading content. These two examples show that political education and media literacy do not have to mean telling students what to believe. Instead, they can help students understand political issues, recognize different viewpoints, and evaluate the information they receive. Taiwan has also begun to recognize this need. In 2025, the Ministry of Education (教育部) announced plans to develop teaching materials on understanding China, including cross-Strait relations, national identity, and possible risks. By July 2025 , thirteen teaching materials had undergone initial review, and were still being revised and supplemented. However, as a student on the front line of Taiwan’s education system, I was barely aware of this plan. Most of the teachers and classmates I asked had not heard about it either. Even if the material is still under review, students should be able to understand what is being prepared, why it is needed, and when they may actually have the chance to use it. A policy cannot have much effect on students if the students themselves barely possess awareness of it. For this reason, the Taiwanese government should expedite the development of these materials and simultaneously seek to raise awareness among students and teachers regarding what changes are underway. However, teaching materials alone may not be enough. Taiwan should also consider adding more opportunities for civic education and discussion in schools, especially on topics such as cross-Strait relations, democracy, media literacy, and how political information affects our daily lives. Taiwan does not need to copy either Austria or Finland’s models exactly. Its own history provides the more important lesson. Taiwan’s democratization movement fought to remove one-party control from schools so that thought could become freer. The purpose of that effort was never to create classrooms in which politics could not be discussed. Modern cognitive warfare makes this distinction urgent. Algorithms do not respect the principle of “politics out of schools.” They enter teenagers’ lives every day, deciding what we see. If schools in democracies respond by remaining silent, they leave the most politically consequential part of students’ education to systems designed not to educate citizens, but to maximize attention. The challenge, then, is not to bring partisan politics back into schools. It is to bring democratic politics back into civic education. Students should understand how Taiwan’s freedoms were won, how authoritarian systems differ from democratic ones, how algorithms can shape political perception, and how to examine claims without automatically accepting or rejecting them because of party labels. Taiwan’s psychological defense will not be built by teaching young people what to think. It will be built by giving them the knowledge and habits necessary to decide what is worth defending for themselves. The main point: As political information increasingly reaches Taiwanese youth through social media, schools’ reluctance to discuss controversial issues may leave students more vulnerable to misleading narratives and cognitive influence. Political neutrality should not mean political silence. Instead, Taiwan’s civic education should encourage open discussion, critical thinking, and media literacy, allowing students to develop their own informed judgments about democracy and the challenges it faces. The post Observations from Taiwan’s Education Frontline amid Cognitive Warfare appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

The Death of Logic and Sanity in Silicon Valley bbert@hudson.org Tue, 11/24/2026 - 13:49 SVG Commentary Nov 24, 2026 Washington Times The Death of Logic and Sanity in Silicon Valley Our technology giants are helping China challenge American supremacy   Miles Yu Senior Fellow and Director, China Center Miles Yu Commentary Caption The headquarters of NVIDIA in the Silicon Valley, Santa Clara, California, November 6, 2025. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print Something has gone terribly wrong in Silicon Valley . The industry that made America the world’s technological superpower has produced executives whose commercial ambitions increasingly collide with national security. Their dealings with communist China expose an astonishing paradox: American technology companies help China catch up with the United States, then warn that China is catching up, and finally use that warning to demand permission to sell China even more advanced technology. No one is more vocal in advancing this lunacy than Nvidia’s now-reinstated CEO Jensen Huang . Mr. Huang’s latest scandal has been sensationalized, focusing on his illicit relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed . Yet the bigger issue is Mr. Huang’s absurd ideas about China and its artificial intelligence industry. Mr. Huang has repeatedly argued that China is catching up with or even winning the AI race, that American export controls are futile or “the dumbest thing we’ve ever done” and that restricting advanced chip sales to China will ultimately undermine American technological leadership. He says those resisting his ideas — whom he labels “ China hawks” — are unpatriotic and un-American. These arguments are intellectually vacuous, characteristically arrogant, strategically reckless and remarkably self-seeking for Nvidia’s commercial interests. Worse, they reflect a broader Silicon Valley mentality that confuses corporate profits with America’s national interest. Consider the contradictions. If China is winning the AI race, why are Chinese companies so desperate for Nvidia’s advanced chips? If American AI models such as Claude and ChatGPT are losing their technological edge, why do China’s top AI firms, such as Kimi and Alibaba, seek to extract their capabilities through large-scale distillation? If American export controls are futile, why does Beijing devote extraordinary resources to circumventing them? How can supplying America’s foremost strategic adversary with the technologies underpinning American supremacy possibly strengthen America’s competitive advantage? Mr. Huang’s vicious dismissal of “ China hawks” as wearing a “badge of shame” makes defending American technological superiority sound disgraceful whenever it interferes with corporate profits. His arguments collapse under the absurdity of their own logic. In fact, this is Silicon Valley’s self-fulfilling prophecy, a circular argument that converts the consequences of its own commercial decisions into justification for repeating them. China’s technological progress remains critically dependent on American semiconductor designs, advanced AI chips, computing infrastructure and technical expertise. Without access to these capabilities, Beijing would face far greater obstacles in developing cutting-edge AI. China’s scientists and engineers are capable, and its government invests enormous resources in innovation. Yet its relentless pursuit of American technology reveals how much its technological ambitions still depend on foreign breakthroughs. Mr. Huang’s corporate behavior is also in question. Multiple reports indicate that Megaspeed has purchased more than $4.8 billion in advanced Nvidia AI chips since June 2024 and has erased the records of these transactions from its books. American authorities have investigated suspected diversion through Southeast Asian intermediaries. Reports have also raised questions about Ms. Huang’s suspected ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter reportedly contacted Commerce Department investigators, citing clearance from Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler, regarding the Megaspeed investigation. Nvidia denies wrongdoing and says it stopped supplying Megaspeed in June 2025, but recent reports dispute the denial. Congress and law enforcement should investigate the Megaspeed affair, examine possible interference with export-control enforcement and close loopholes involving third-country intermediaries, remote computing access and sensitive technology licensing. Proven violations deserve serious penalties. Nvidia is hardly alone. Consider Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su, Mr. Huang’s distant cousin. In 2016, under her leadership, AMD entered into a technology-licensing agreement worth approximately $293 million, plus royalties, with Chinese partners affiliated with the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The arrangement transferred valuable x86-compatible processor technology and first-generation Zen intellectual property into China’s industrial ecosystem. The available record indicates the transaction was lawful. Its strategic wisdom deserves scrutiny. Why should American companies help develop China’s indigenous computing capabilities and then warn Americans about the technological challenge they helped create? Cisco provides another cautionary example. Falun Gong practitioners accused the company of supplying technologies that helped China’s Golden Shield surveillance system identify and track religious believers. Cisco disputed the allegations, and this year the U.S. Supreme Court dismissed the lawsuit, holding that the Alien Tort Statute does not allow aiding-and-abetting liability against corporations. Yet the controversy illustrates the risks of American technology becoming entangled with authoritarian surveillance. The Chinese Communist Party systematically mobilizes civilian technology for military modernization, intelligence operations and political control. U.S. executives advocating greater access to technology for China must confront these strategic consequences. America’s technological supremacy rests on decades of innovation, enormous investment and hard-won expertise. Allowing these advantages to strengthen its principal strategic adversary threatens the foundations of American security. Silicon Valley has perfected a vicious cycle of strategic folly: Sell advanced American technology to China , often knowingly and furtively through a third, surrogate country such as Singapore. Watch Beijing close the gap. Warn Americans that China is catching up. Declare export controls futile. Demand permission to sell even more advanced technology to China . Repeat. Each turn enriches Silicon Valley , strengthens Beijing and erodes America’s technological supremacy. The closer China gets, the louder the alarm — and the louder the alarm, the greater the pressure to sell China more. Eventually, the prophecy fulfills itself: Silicon Valley helps China catch up, warns America that China is catching up, and uses that warning to help China catch up even faster, until America loses the race its own technology giants helped China win. In other words, Silicon Valley has lost its mind. In explaining his support for Mr. Huang’s reinstatement, President Trump has said Mr. Huang has learned his lessons. Let us hope these lessons learned will help Silicon Valley regain its sanity. Read in the Washington Times. Enjoyed this analysis? Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

summary: 香港与南沙完成跨境救护演习 |中国劳工公告2026年11月26日星期四·香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港和南沙完成跨境救护车演习 香港和南沙成功完成北向跨境救护车转运演习。此次演习为将现有的双向转运试点计划延伸至南沙铺平了道路，这是扩大大湾区医疗一体化的努力的一部分。香港与广东南沙市成功完成北行跨境救护车合作
content:
香港与南沙完成跨境救护演习 |中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港与南沙完成跨境救护演习
香港与南沙顺利完成北向跨境救护车转运演练。此次演习为将现有的双向转运试点计划延伸至南沙铺平了道路，这是扩大大湾区医疗一体化的努力的一部分。
11月26日，官员宣布，香港与广东省南沙市成功完成北向跨境救护车转运演习。此次演习是将现有双向转运试点计划延伸至南沙，推进大湾区医疗一体化的一步。
卫生局局长罗仲茂表示，此次演习为扩大南沙双向转运安排奠定了基础。他表示，香港政府和内地有关部门将尽快落实相关措施。
试点计划于2024年11月30日推出，运作顺利。截至2026年11月中旬，已有30名患者从深圳、珠海、南沙、澳门的定点医院转往香港指定公立医院。 3名患者已从香港公立医院转往深圳和珠海的医院。
经专业医学评估，所有转运患者均需继续住院治疗，病情相对稳定，无法独立出境，不适合救护车转运通过现有检查站。
2025年施政报告提出扩大该计划，要求有序扩展跨境救护车患者转运，包括双向转运。 2026年3月，香港与深圳、珠海、澳门实施双向转机安排。

Hong Kong and Nansha complete cross-border ambulance drill | China Labour Bulletin Board
Thursday, 26 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong and Nansha complete cross-border ambulance drill
Hong Kong and Nansha have successfully completed a northbound cross-border ambulance transfer drill. The exercise paves the way for extending the existing two-way transfer pilot scheme to Nansha, part of efforts to expand medical integration in the Greater Bay Area.
Hong Kong and the Guangdong city of Nansha have successfully completed a northbound cross-border ambulance transfer drill, officials announced on 26 November. The exercise is a step towards extending the existing two-way transfer pilot scheme to Nansha, advancing medical integration in the Greater Bay Area.
Secretary for Health Lo Chung-mau said the drill laid the foundation for expanding the two-way transfer arrangement to Nansha. He noted that the Hong Kong government and relevant mainland authorities would work to implement the measures as soon as possible.
The pilot scheme, launched on 30 November 2024, has operated smoothly. As of mid-November 2026, 30 patients had been transferred from designated hospitals in Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Nansha and Macau to specified public hospitals in Hong Kong. Three patients had been transferred from Hong Kong public hospitals to hospitals in Shenzhen and Zhuhai.
According to professional medical assessments, all transferred patients required continued hospital treatment, were in relatively stable condition, could not travel across the border independently and were not suitable for transfer by ambulance through existing checkpoints.
The expansion of the scheme was proposed in the 2025 Policy Address, which called for the orderly extension of cross-border ambulance patient transfers, including two-way transfers. In March 2026, Hong Kong implemented two-way transfer arrangements with Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Macau.

content:
香港概述了促进太空技术发展的措施中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港概述促进太空技术发展的措施
香港代理创新部长详细介绍了政府对太空技术的支持，包括新的资金和研究中心。该市的目标是在首次宇航员飞行后加深对国家太空任务的参与。
署理创新、科技及工业局局长在 2026 年 11 月 26 日的立法报告中表示，香港政府概述了一系列促进香港太空技术发展的措施。
部长在有关抓住国家航天发展和北领地大学城项目机遇的议案辩论中发言时指出，神舟二十四号于11月25日成功发射，香港首位宇航员李家英博士于2026年5月在神舟二十三号上担任有效载荷专家。
创新及科技支援计划于2024年特别征集太空科技项目，向六个项目拨款逾1亿港元。部长表示，香港科技大学主导的温室气体探测器“天云相机”成为香港首个进入天宫空间站的科学有效载荷。
地方高校参与了嫦娥探月任务和天文火星探测计划，贡献了相机指向系统、采样设备和地形测绘技术。部长补充说，天问三号火星样本返回任务选择了香港大学和香港中文大学的仪器。
政府在InnoHK计划下成立了香港太空机器人及能源中心，并计划建立一个新的InnoHK太空制造技术中心。部长表示，2026年施政报告建议在创新科技及工业局内设立前沿技术部门，以协调长期太空发展。
新的空间技术项目征集将支持卫星技术、空间探索仪器、航空材料和遥感方面的研究。该部长表示，政府还致力于通过改善融资、保险、卫星许可和数据交易服务来吸引航空航天公司。
本地四所大学开设航天相关本科课程，航天科技元素已纳入中小学课程。该部长表示，政府于2025年9月推出了30亿港元的前沿技术研究支持计划，以促进国际合作并吸引海外人才。

Thursday, 26 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong outlines measures to boost space technology development
Hong Kong's acting innovation minister detailed government support for space technology, including new funding and research centres. The city aims to deepen participation in national space missions following its first astronaut's flight.
The Hong Kong government outlined a series of measures to boost the city's space technology development, the acting secretary for innovation, technology and industry said in a legislative address on 26 November 2026.
Speaking during a debate on a motion about seizing opportunities from national space development and the Northern Territory University Town project, the minister noted the successful launch of Shenzhou-24 on 25 November and Hong Kong's first astronaut, Dr Li Jiaying, who served as a payload specialist on Shenzhou-23 in May 2026.
The Innovation and Technology Support Programme launched a special call for space technology projects in 2024, granting over HK$100 million to six projects. The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology-led greenhouse gas detector, Tianyun Camera, became the first Hong Kong scientific payload to enter the Tiangong space station, the minister said.
Local universities have participated in the Chang'e lunar missions and Tianwen Mars exploration programme, contributing camera pointing systems, sampling devices and terrain mapping technologies. Instruments from the University of Hong Kong and Chinese University of Hong Kong were selected for the Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission, the minister added.
The government established the Hong Kong Space Robotics and Energy Centre under the InnoHK programme and plans a new InnoHK centre for space manufacturing technology. The 2026 Policy Address proposed creating a frontier technology unit within the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau to coordinate long-term space development, the minister said.
A new call for space technology projects will support research in satellite technology, space exploration instruments, aerospace materials and remote sensing. The government is also working to attract aerospace companies by improving financing, insurance, satellite licensing and data trading services, the minister said.
Four local universities offer aerospace-related undergraduate programmes, and space technology elements have been incorporated into primary and secondary school curricula. The government launched a HK$3 billion Frontier Technology Research Support Scheme in September 2025 to promote international collaboration and attract overseas talent, the minister said.

content:
香港教育官员概述了推动航空航天研究的计划中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港教育官员概述了促进航空航天研究的计划
香港教育局正在将航空航天纳入学校课程，并利用北区大学城培养航天人才。此举是继特区首次宇航员任务之后进行的，旨在与国家太空目标保持一致。
香港教育局副局长11月26日表示，根据国家航天雄心和香港2026年施政报告，香港教育局正在加强航天创新教育和人才培养。
副秘书长在立法会发言时表示，政府正在将航空航天纳入中小学课程。 2026 年 6 月数字教育蓝图重点关注科学、技术和人工智能，包括更新科学和物理课程以涵盖太空主题。
该市首位航天员李开平在国家支持下执行神舟二十三号任务。政府举办“天宫班港澳专场”，学生观看神舟二十三号航天员进行实时实验。该局制作了教材来维持兴趣。
四所香港大学提供航空航天课程并进行太空研究。局方将鼓励院校拓展航空航天项目和研究合作，以北区大学城项目为契机，创造新的发展空间。
副秘书长表示，航天局将继续推动航天教育和人才培养，以支持国家的航天雄心和香港的长远需要。

Hong Kong education official outlines plans to boost aerospace studies
Hong Kong's Education Bureau is integrating aerospace into school curricula and using the Northern District University City to boost space talent. The move follows the SAR's first astronaut mission and aims to align with national space goals.
Hong Kong's Education Bureau is strengthening aerospace innovation education and talent development, in line with national space ambitions and the city's 2026 policy address, a deputy secretary said on 26 November.
Speaking in the Legislative Council, the deputy secretary said the government is integrating aerospace into primary and secondary curricula. The June 2026 Digital Education Blueprint focuses on science, technology and artificial intelligence, including updates to science and physics courses to cover space topics.
The city's first astronaut, Likaiping, flew on the Shenzhou-23 mission with national support. The government held a 'Tiangong Class, Hong Kong and Macao Special Session' where students watched Shenzhou-23 crew conduct real-time experiments. The bureau has produced teaching materials to sustain interest.
Four Hong Kong universities offer aerospace courses and conduct space research. The bureau will encourage institutions to expand aerospace programmes and research collaborations, using the Northern District University City project to create new space for development.
The deputy secretary said the bureau will continue to promote aerospace education and talent cultivation to support China's space ambitions and Hong Kong's long-term needs.

前同学称黄爱丽在浸大逃课并穿设计师品牌 |中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
前同学称黄爱丽在浸大逃课、穿设计师品牌
一位以前的同学告诉《纽约时报》，后来与英伟达老板黄仁勋有联系的爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)在香港浸会大学攻读硕士学位期间很少上课，并且穿着设计师品牌的衣服。该报告详细介绍了她的背景、商业投资以及在一个计算项目中的角色，该项目支持
据 11 月 26 日发表的一份报告称，黄爱丽的一位前同学告诉《纽约时报》，她在香港浸会大学 (HKBU) 攻读硕士学位期间经常逃课并穿着设计师品牌的衣服，早在她与英伟达老板黄仁勋的婚外情成为全球头条新闻之前。
报道称，黄爱丽在湖南省湘潭市南珠山镇长大，她的父亲黄国斌在当地一家国有兵工厂担任职员。据报道，她先在附近的一所护士学校学习，然后离开家乡到中央电视台工作。
2006年，她在香港浸会大学攻读媒体管理硕士课程——据她以前的同学回忆，她很少出现在课堂上，但总是穿着设计师品牌的衣服。
2010年，黄乐和姐姐黄钰在北京一家会员制高尔夫俱乐部注册了一家公司。然而，报道称，该公司的年收入仅为约 4,500 美元（35,100 港元），她决定在 2014 年将股份转让给姐姐。
黄丽娟后来涉足投资领域，与从事金融行业的丈夫康伟共同投资，逐步建立了横跨多家公司的业务网络。报告称，在 COVID-19 大流行期间，黄和康在当地政府的支持下参与了长三角人工智能高级计算中心的开发。
报道称，该项目配备了英伟达芯片，并向企业租赁算力，使其成为芯片供应链中的关键环节。 《纽约时报》指出，这些芯片最终流向了中国航空工业集团公司等军事承包商，而该计算项目为黄仁勋进入黄仁勋的社交网络铺平了道路。

Former classmate says Alice Huang skipped classes, wore designer labels at HKBU
A former classmate told The New York Times that Alice Huang, later linked to Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, rarely attended classes during her master's at Hong Kong Baptist University and wore designer labels. The report details her background, business ventures, and role in a computing project that supp
A former classmate of Alice Huang has told The New York Times that she frequently skipped classes and wore designer labels during her master's studies at Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU), long before her extramarital affair with Nvidia boss Jensen Huang made global headlines, according to a report published on 26 November.
Alice Huang grew up in Nanzhushan, a town in Xiangtan, Hunan province, where her father, Huang Guobin, worked as a clerk at a state-owned weapons factory, the report said. She first studied at a nearby nursing school before leaving her hometown to work at China Central Television, according to the report.
In 2006, she enrolled in a master's programme in media management at HKBU — where, as her former classmate recalled, she was rarely seen in class but always in designer labels.
In 2010, Huang Le and her elder sister Huang Yu registered a company at a members-only golf club in Beijing. However, the firm generated annual revenue of only about US$4,500 (HK$35,100), and she decided to transfer her stake to her sister in 2014, the report said.
Alice Huang later ventured into investment, teaming up with her husband Kang Wei, who works in the finance sector, to co-invest and gradually build a business network spanning multiple companies. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Huang and Kang took part in developing the Yangtze River Delta Artificial Intelligence Advanced Computing Center, backed by support from local authorities, the report said.
The project was equipped with Nvidia chips and leased computing power to businesses, making it a key link in the chip supply chain, the report said. The New York Times noted that the chips eventually went to military contractors such as the Aviation Industry Corporation of China, and that the computing project paved Alice Huang's way into Jensen Huang's social network.

content:
香港领导人在广州大湾区论坛上宣扬人工智能驱动的服务贸易 |中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港领导人在广州大湾区论坛上宣扬人工智能驱动的服务贸易
香港行政长官在广州举行的2026年粤港澳大湾区服务贸易大会上致辞，强调人工智能在贸易中的作用，并概述香港通过创新、互联互通和CEPA升级促进服务贸易的战略。
11月26日，香港行政长官在广州举行的2026年粤港澳大湾区服务贸易大会暨人工智能+服务贸易配对活动开幕式上致辞，强调服务贸易和人工智能在全球商业中日益重要。
当前，世界经济格局快速调整，服务贸易已成为高质量发展的重要引擎，人工智能正在从根本上改变贸易模式。他表示，此次会议的人工智能加服务贸易重点是及时的。
他将这次活动与APEC中国年联系起来，并指出，第一个正式活动是2月在广州举行的高官会议，而APEC领导人峰会之前的最后一次部长级会议是10月在香港主办的财长会议。他还提到习近平主席最近在深圳亚太经合组织工商领导人峰会上表示支持建立世界湾区经济合作联盟。
行政长官强调大湾区的战略重要性以及香港作为亚太经合组织成员和该地区核心城市的角色。他表示，将发挥香港连接国内外市场的优势，推动服务贸易向更高水平发展，为建设亚太共同体作出贡献。
他概述了香港于九月公布的第一个五年计划，该计划与国家战略保持一致，重点发展香港作为金融、航运、贸易、创新科技和高端人才的中心。他表示，创新科技是香港发展的核心，香港将积极配合国家人工智能+战略，提升在跨境供应链管理、专业服务和数码贸易等方面的优势。
为加速服务贸易，行政长官呼吁通过基础设施建设、监管协调和民心相通加强互联互通，促进人员、货物、资本和数据的流动。他强调《关于建立更紧密经贸关系的安排》（CEPA）的重要性，并表示香港将与商务部合作升级CEPA，深化服务业合作。
他形容香港是超级联系人和超级增值者，为内地企业走出去和海外企业在大湾区寻找机会提供双重平台。他指出，内地企业海外拓展专责小组已协助超过360家内地企业在香港设立或拓展业务，而2026年6月，超过30家内地企业代表访问中亚，达成96项协议，总价值超过16.5亿美元。

Hong Kong leader touts AI-driven services trade at Greater Bay Area forum in Guangzhou
Hong Kong's chief executive addressed the 2026 Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Services Trade Conference in Guangzhou, highlighting AI's role in trade and outlining Hong Kong's strategy to boost services trade through innovation, connectivity and CEPA upgrades.
Hong Kong's chief executive addressed the opening of the 2026 Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Services Trade Conference and an AI-plus-services trade matching event in Guangzhou on 26 November, stressing the growing importance of services trade and artificial intelligence in global commerce.
Noting that the global economic landscape is undergoing rapid adjustment, the chief executive said services trade has become a key engine for high-quality development, while AI is fundamentally changing trade models. He described the conference's AI-plus-services trade focus as timely.
He linked the event to the APEC China Year, noting that the first official activity was a senior officials' meeting in Guangzhou in February, while the last ministerial meeting before the APEC leaders' summit was a finance ministers' meeting hosted by Hong Kong in October. He also referenced President Xi Jinping's recent statement at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, supporting the establishment of a world bay areas economic cooperation alliance.
The chief executive highlighted the Greater Bay Area's strategic importance and Hong Kong's role as both an APEC member and a core city in the region. He pledged to leverage Hong Kong's strengths in connecting domestic and international markets to drive higher-level services trade and contribute to building an Asia-Pacific community.
He outlined Hong Kong's first five-year plan, announced in September, which aligns with national strategies and focuses on developing Hong Kong as a hub for finance, shipping, trade, innovation and technology, and high-end talent. He said innovation and technology are central to Hong Kong's development, and that Hong Kong will actively align with the national AI-plus strategy to enhance its advantages in cross-border supply chain management, professional services and digital trade.
To accelerate services trade, the chief executive called for greater connectivity through infrastructure, regulatory alignment and people-to-people ties, facilitating the flow of people, goods, capital and data. He stressed the importance of the Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) and said Hong Kong will work with the Ministry of Commerce to upgrade CEPA and deepen services cooperation.
He described Hong Kong as a super-connector and super-value-adder, serving as a dual platform for mainland companies going global and overseas firms seeking opportunities in the Greater Bay Area. He noted that a task force for mainland enterprises expanding overseas has helped over 360 mainland companies set up or expand in Hong Kong, and that a June 2026 visit to Central Asia with over 30 mainland enterprise representatives resulted in 96 agreements worth over US$1.65 billion.

summary: 香港称宏富苑逾1,730户完成业权转让 |中国劳工布告栏 星期四, 2026 年 11 月 26 日 · 香港 香港及中国劳工英文新闻 香港称，望富苑超过 1,730 户家庭完成业权转让 香港财政副司长表示，望富苑 1,914 户家庭中，超过 1,730 户已根据特别销售计划完成业权转让。大约还剩下 70 个，其中 13 个不打算出售。当局将在下个月联系他们并继续提供支持服务。香港副财政司司长兼署理房屋委员会
content:
香港称宏富苑逾1,730户完成业权转让 |中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港称旺富苑逾1,730户完成业权过户
香港副财政司长表示，宏富苑的 1,914 个住户中，有 1,730 多个已根据特别销售计划完成业权转让。大约还剩下 70 个，其中 13 个不打算出售。当局将在下个月联系他们并继续提供支持服务。
香港副财政司司长兼署理房委会主任黄伟立11月26日表示，大埔宏富苑已有1,914户住户与政府签署有约束力的出售协议，超过1,730户已完成所有业权过户手续。其余约 70 户家庭中，有 57 户表示希望将产权出售给政府，但仍在等待产权核实和相关法律程序完成。另外13人表示目前不打算出售其作品，当局将在下个月再次联系他们进行进一步沟通。
黄在谈到香港电台的“千禧年”节目时表示，在政府的特别销售计划下，已有超过1,400户家庭选择了新单位。余下约500户家庭中，部分住户以绿表计划购买房委会单位，部分则选择购买私人房屋。黄补充说，当局早前已为王府苑居民安排了两次大型搬家活动，随后又为约80户居民安排了小规模搬家活动。进一步详情将由政务司司长张耀东稍后公布。
至于原宏富苑用地，黄表示，未来将用作大埔或新界东所需的社区设施，但当局会优先完成业权收购，然后拆除建筑物。将与社区讨论土地的未来用途。
民政及青年事务局局长麦美诗也在同一计划中发表讲话，她表示将继续为居民提供支持，包括通过“一起守望”和“团结起来”计划，为有需要的人提供情感支持。她强调，这些计划不会停止，居民可以通过“一户一社工”制度获得服务。至于居民的长远福利需要，麦表示，这些并非单靠大埔宏富法庭援助基金，而是依靠大埔宏富法院援助基金。现行制度下的现有福利服务也能满足居民的需要。

Hong Kong says over 1,730 Wang Fu Court households complete title transfer | China Labour Bulletin Board
Thursday, 26 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong says over 1,730 Wang Fu Court households complete title transfer
Hong Kong’s deputy financial secretary said more than 1,730 of Wang Fu Court’s 1,914 households have completed title transfer under a special sales scheme. About 70 remain, with 13 not intending to sell. Authorities will contact them next month and continue support services.
Hong Kong’s Deputy Financial Secretary and Acting Housing Authority Director Wong Wai-lap said on 26 November that 1,914 households at Wang Fu Court in Tai Po have signed binding sale agreements with the government, and more than 1,730 have completed all title-transfer procedures. Of the remaining approximately 70 households, 57 have indicated they wish to sell their titles to the government but are still awaiting title verification and completion of the relevant legal processes. The other 13 have said they do not plan to sell their titles at present, and authorities will contact them again next month for further communication.
Speaking on RTHK’s ‘Millennium’ programme, Wong said that under the government’s special sales scheme, more than 1,400 households have already selected their new flats. Of the remaining 500 or so households, some have purchased Housing Authority flats under the Green Form scheme, while others have chosen to buy private housing. Wong added that the authorities had earlier arranged two large-scale sessions for Wang Fu Court residents to move their belongings, followed by small-scale arrangements for about 80 households. Further details will be announced in due course by Chief Secretary for Administration Cheung Yiu-tung.
Regarding the original Wang Fu Court site, Wong said it will be used in future for community facilities needed in Tai Po or the New Territories East, but the authorities will prioritise completing title acquisition and then demolishing the buildings. The future use of the land will be discussed with the community.
Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Macy Mak, also speaking on the same programme, said support for residents will continue, including through the ‘Watch Together’ and ‘Unite Together’ programmes, which provide emotional support to those in need. She stressed that these programmes will not be discontinued, and residents can access services through the ‘one household, one social worker’ system. As for the long-term welfare needs of residents, Mak said these are not solely dependent on the Tai Po Wang Fu Court Assistance Fund; existing welfare services under the current system can also address residents’ needs.

根据差饷物业估价署的数据，10月份香港私人住宅物业价格环比下跌0.6%，结束了连续两个月的上涨。价格指数为319，同比增长8.2%。租金创历史新高 连续十二连涨

租金指数再创新高，连续12个月上涨。 10月份，该指数达到213.2，月涨幅接近0.5%，涨幅较上月略有扩大，年涨幅接近6.7%。前10个月，租金累计上涨6.3%。

Hong Kong private home prices fall 0.6% in October, ending two-month rise
Hong Kong's private residential property prices fell 0.6 per cent month-on-month in October, ending two consecutive months of gains, according to the Rating and Valuation Department. The price index stood at 319, with annual growth of 8.2 per cent. Rents hit a new record, rising for the 12th straigh
Hong Kong's private residential property prices eased in October, ending two consecutive months of gains, official data showed. The Rating and Valuation Department reported that the city's private住宅 price index for October stood at 319, down about 0.6 per cent month-on-month but up nearly 8.2 per cent year-on-year. In the first ten months of the year, prices accumulated a rise of about 6.5 per cent.
Prices of中小型 units fell 0.6 per cent month-on-month in October, with an annual increase of about 8.2 per cent. Large units recorded a 0.3 per cent monthly decline and a 7.9 per cent annual rise. Over the first ten months,中小型 and large units rose 6.4 per cent and nearly 7.5 per cent, respectively.
The rental index hit a new high, rising for the 12th consecutive month. In October, the index reached 213.2, with a monthly increase of nearly 0.5 per cent — slightly wider than the previous month — and an annual rise of nearly 6.7 per cent. In the first ten months, rents cumulatively increased by 6.3 per cent.

content:
香港前立法会议员黄锦辉在中文大学校园酒后驾车被判刑中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 26 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
香港前议员黄锦辉在中文大学校园酒后驾车被判刑
前立法会议员黄锦辉6月在香港中文大学校园承认醉酒驾驶、粗心驾驶等四项罪名后，被判处120小时社区服务、12个月禁驾及罚款6000港元。
前立法会议员黄锦辉承认四项与香港中文大学（中大）校园酒后驾驶事故有关的罪名，在沙田裁判法院被判处 120 小时社区服务、12 个月禁驾及罚款 6,000 港元。
案情透露，6月29日晚，黄某酒后驾车在中大校园内与两辆车相撞，并没有停车而离开现场。随后，他被指控酒驾、危险驾驶、交通事故后未停车、未报告交通事故等罪名。检方随后将危险驾驶罪名修改为粗心驾驶，黄先生对全部四项罪名均表示认罪。
事件发生后，黄先生辞去在立法会的所有职务。此次宣判标志着这起因黄先生曾担任立法会议员而引起公众广泛关注的案件的结案。
法院判处120小时的社区服务令、12个月的驾驶资格取消期以及6000港元的罚款。黄先生此前在早些时候的听证会上承认了这些罪行。

Former Hong Kong lawmaker Kam-fai Wong sentenced for drunk driving on Chinese University campus | China Labour Bulletin Board
Thursday, 26 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Former Hong Kong lawmaker Kam-fai Wong sentenced for drunk driving on Chinese University campus
Former Legislative Council member Kam-fai Wong was sentenced to 120 hours of community service, a 12-month driving ban, and a HK$6,000 fine after pleading guilty to four charges including drunk driving and careless driving on the Chinese University of Hong Kong campus in June.
Former Legislative Council member Kam-fai Wong has been sentenced at the Shatin Magistrates' Court to 120 hours of community service, a 12-month driving ban, and a fine of HK$6,000 after pleading guilty to four charges related to a drink-driving incident on the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) campus.
The court heard that on the evening of 29 June, Wong drove under the influence of alcohol on the CUHK campus, colliding with two vehicles and leaving the scene without stopping. He was subsequently charged with drunk driving, dangerous driving, failing to stop after a traffic accident, and failing to report a traffic accident. The prosecution later amended the dangerous driving charge to careless driving, and Wong pleaded guilty to all four counts.
Following the incident, Wong resigned from all his positions in the Legislative Council. The sentencing marks the conclusion of a case that drew significant public attention due to Wong's former role as a lawmaker.
The court imposed a community service order of 120 hours, a driving disqualification period of 12 months, and a financial penalty of HK$6,000. Wong had previously admitted to the offences at an earlier hearing.

香港财政司司长陈茂波于2026年11月26日抵达海牙，率团前往荷兰促进投资、金融服务和科技合作。他首先与荷兰外交部秘书长克里斯蒂安·雷贝根会面，讨论香港的“一国两制”安排、营商环境、经济金融状况，以及如何深化双边贸易和创新联系。
陈肇始表示，是次访问旨在展示香港在金融、投资、创新以及北领地发展方面的新机遇，鼓励香港与荷兰加强合作。
财政司司长还会见了荷兰财政部司库贾斯珀·韦塞林，就荷兰和欧洲的经济和资本市场发展进行了深入交流。陈先生向Wesseling介绍了香港金融市场发展和促进创新及科技产业的政策，特别是吸引重点企业落户的措施。
此外，陈肇始与荷兰国际关系学院克林根达尔研究所代表会面，介绍香港最新情况，并就中国经济发展和国际发展交换意见。
陈肇始礼节性拜会中国驻荷兰大使沉波，就中荷关系及香港与荷兰深化合作交换意见。
代表团于11月26日（海牙时间）继续访问荷兰。

Hong Kong finance chief begins Netherlands visit with trade and innovation talks
Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Paul Chan arrived in The Hague on 26 November 2026, meeting Dutch officials to discuss business ties, innovation cooperation and the city's new opportunities under the Northern Territories development plan.
26 Nov 2026 at 09:00 HKT · updated 26 Nov, 09:18 · 1 min read
Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan arrived in The Hague on 26 November 2026, leading a delegation to the Netherlands to promote investment, financial services and technology cooperation. He first met Secretary-General of the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs Christiaan Rebergen, discussing Hong Kong's 'one country, two systems' arrangement, its business environment, economic and financial conditions, and ways to deepen bilateral trade and innovation ties.
Chan said the visit aims to showcase Hong Kong's new opportunities in finance, investment and innovation, as well as the development of the Northern Territories, to encourage more cooperation between Hong Kong and the Netherlands.
The financial secretary also met Jasper Wesseling, Treasurer-General of the Dutch Ministry of Finance, for an in-depth exchange on economic and capital market developments in the Netherlands and Europe. Chan updated Wesseling on Hong Kong's financial market developments and policies to promote innovation and technology industries, particularly measures to attract key enterprises to set up operations.
In addition, Chan met representatives of the Clingendael Institute, the Netherlands Institute of International Relations, to introduce Hong Kong's latest situation and exchange views on China's economic development and international developments.
Chan also paid a courtesy call on Chinese Ambassador to the Netherlands Shen Bo, exchanging views on Sino-Dutch relations and ways to deepen cooperation between Hong Kong and the Netherlands.
The delegation continues its visit to the Netherlands on 26 November (The Hague time).
