Amphibious transport dock USS Anchorage , which has been anchored offshore since Nov. 11, moved into CFAY following Frank Cable’s departure, according to local ship spotters . Royal Canadian Navy frigate HMCS Regina arrived in Yokosuka on Thursday for a port visit. Fast attack submarine USS Toledo (SSN-769) pulled into CFAY on Tuesday , according to local shipspotters. In the Miyako Strait PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fleet oiler CNS Chaohu (890) on Nov. 16, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fleet oiler CNS Chaohu (890) were spotted Monday sailing north 60 kilometers – 37 miles – west of Kume Island, having previously transited between Okinawa and Miyako Island to exit the Philippine Sea. A JMSDF P-3C Orion Maritime Patrol Aircraft shadowed the PLAN ships. Japan’s Joint Staff Office (JSO) noted that Qiqihar has traveled back and forth in Japan’s southwest region since Oct. 17 when it transited the Osumi Strait to enter the Pacific Ocean and then returned to the East China Sea through the Miyako Strait on Nov. 1. On Nov. 2, the PLAN destroyer sailed through the Miyako Strait to enter the Philippine Sea and returned the same way back into the East China Sea on Nov. 4. On Nov. 12, Qiqihar again sailed through the Miyako Strait to enter the Philippine Sea. The JSO also noted that Chaohu sailed south through the Miyako Strait to enter the Philippine Sea on Nov. 2. In the East China Sea A Chinese Y-9 electronic intelligence aircraft on Nov. 16, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Monday, a Chinese Y-9 electronic intelligence aircraft flew in from China and conducted a patrol circuit across the East China Sea, covering an area extending from south of the Danjo Islands to northwest of the island of Amami Oshima before returning to China. In response, the Japan Air Self-Defense Force scrambled fighter aircraft from the Southwestern Air Defense Command and other units. A Chinese TB-001 reconnaissance/attack Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) on Nov. 19, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Thursday, a Chinese TB-001 reconnaissance/attack Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flew in from China and over the East China Sea as far as the waters southwest of the Danjo Islands and proceeded southwest. The drone flew west of Okinawa before returning to China. The JASDF scrambled fighter aircraft from the Southwestern Air Defense Command in response. In the Sea of Japan A Russian Tu-95 bomber on Nov. 17, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo Russian aircraft violated Japanese territorial airspace on two occasions and prompted fighter aircraft scrambles as they entered the Air Defense Identification Zones (ADIZs) of Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Tuesday. The three countries initially did not provide specifics of the Russian aircraft but later released the flights were conducted by two Tu-95MS bombers and two IL-76 transports, which landed in Vietnam that same day. One Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace northwest of the island of Okinoshima. A second aircraft violated Japanese airspace in the same area minutes later. The two Tu-95MS bombers returned to Russia on Thursday, first passing through the Taiwan Air Defense Identification Zone. Republic of China Air Force fighter aircraft shadowed the Russian bombers. From morning to afternoon, the bombers flew in the airspace between Taiwan and Yonaguni Island. The aircraft flew over the East China Sea where they were joined by two Russian Tu-142 MPAs, which had flown in from the Sea of Japan and through the Tsushima Strait. The joint air group then flew through the Tsushima Strait to return to Russia. The JASDF scrambled fighter aircraft in response. In Vladivostok, Russia Russian Navy improved Kilo-class attack submarine RFS Yakutsk (B-610) arrived Nov. 13 at its new homeport of Vladivostok to join the Russian Navy Pacific Fleet. “The submarine completed an inter-fleet passage from the Baltic Fleet to the Pacific Fleet via the Northern Sea Route, covering more than 9,000 nautical miles,” reads a news release by the fleet. Yakutsk was built in St. Petersburg and commissioned into the Russian Navy Pacific Fleet in June of 2025. Japan previously tracked Yakutsk with amphibious landing ship RFS Nikolai Vilkov (081) and tugboat Fotiy Krylov on Nov. 10 as they transited La Pérouse Strait to enter the Sea of Japan. In Auckland, New Zealand USCGC Harriet Lane (WMEC-903) in Auckland, New Zealand, on Nov. 15, 2026. Royal New Zealand Navy photo Coast Guard Cutter USCGC Harriet Lane (WMEC-903) participated in Exercise Maru 26, a Proliferation Security Initiative exercise that ran from Monday to Wednesday in Auckland, New Zealand. Harriet Lane arrived in Auckland on Sunday and conducted drills with Royal New Zealand Navy patrol vessel HMNZS Taupo (P3570). Around 150 personnel from 30 countries participated in Maru 26, which was focused on countering the illicit trafficking of weapons of mass destruction and related materials. This post was written by Dzirhan Mahadzir.

title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动是否能够解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，特别是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

【原文 English Original】
The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

title: Beijing slams US for ‘suppressing’ Chinese firms after Huawei conviction
zh_title: 北京谴责美国在华为定罪后“打压”中国企业
summary: 周三，在美国陪审团裁定科技巨头华为窃取商业机密并就其在伊朗的工作向监管机构撒谎后，北京猛烈抨击美国“打压”中国企业。华为总部位于深圳。照片：华为。全球领先的电信设备制造商华为已成为唐纳德·特朗普总统政府的攻击目标，经过三个月的审判后，华为于周二在纽约联邦法院被定罪。这项裁决是在美国和中国的政治敏感时刻作出的，两国领导人试图表达特朗普所说的“f
content:
周三，在美国陪审团裁定科技巨头华为窃取商业机密并就其在伊朗的工作向监管机构撒谎后，北京猛烈抨击美国“打压”中国企业。华为总部位于深圳。照片：华为。全球领先的电信设备制造商华为已成为唐纳德·特朗普总统政府的攻击目标，经过三个月的审判后，华为于周二在纽约联邦法院被定罪。这项裁决是在美国和中国的政治敏感时期做出的，两国领导人上周在深圳会晤时试图展现特朗普所说的“奇妙”关系。陪审团裁定华为面临 12 项刑事罪名中的 10 项罪名成立，包括银行欺诈、合谋窃取商业机密以及合谋诈骗美国。中国周三予以回击，称“坚决反对美国打压和围堵中国企业，坚定支持中国企业维护合法权益”。特朗普政府长期以来一直声称华为存在代表中国政府从事间谍活动的风险，并此前敦促各国不要在新的 5G 移动网络中使用该公司的基础设施。 “没有任何人或公司可以凌驾于法律之上，”美国司法部长托德·布兰奇在定罪后的一份声明中表示。
“几十年来，华为及其三个子公司在谎言和盗窃的基础上在美国开展业务。”美国和中国国旗。资料图片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。华为周三驳回了这一判决，并在一份声明中表示，该判决“没有法律或事实依据”。 “我们将彻底审查相关判决，并采取一切必要的法律行动来捍卫我们的权益，”它补充道。 “必要的法律行动” 然而，陪审团确实宣判华为无罪，该公司表示，此举“欢迎”，并补充说，它“证实了这些指控缺乏事实依据，并证明了我们在过去八年中的一贯立场。” “我们认为政府的其余指控同样没有法律或事实依据……我们将彻底审查相关判决，并采取一切必要的法律行动来捍卫我们的权益，”声明继续说道。这些指控部分涉及华为与伊朗政府的业务往来。美国司法部表示：“华为多次对其在伊朗业务的性质撒谎，错误地告诉银行、记者和美国政府，它没有协助伊朗政府、军队或情报部门。”
“华为向银行谎报其在伊朗的活动，以获得数十亿美元并获得美元清算服务，这使华为成为全球电信服务市场的成熟参与者——部分原因是它的谎言。”这家设备制造商还被指控试图招募美国电信公司的员工，并在此过程中从他们那里获取技术信息。根据最初的起诉书，这些数据据称使华为能够开发与其竞争对手类似的产品，然后以较低的价格出售。资料图片：维基百科。美国司法部在一份新闻稿中表示：“被盗用的知识产权包括商业秘密信息和受版权保护的作品，例如互联网路由器的源代码和用户手册、天线技术和机器人测试技术。”华为甚至还推出了一款inter

【原文 English Original】
Beijing lashed out at the United States on Wednesday for “suppressing” Chinese companies, after a US jury found tech giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and lying to regulators over its work in Iran. Huawei headquarters in Shenzhen. Photo: Huawei. Huawei, the world’s leading telecom equipment manufacturer, has been targeted by President Donald Trump’s administration, and was convicted on Tuesday in a New York federal court after a three-month trial. The ruling comes at a politically sensitive time for the United States and China, whose leaders sought to project what Trump called a “fantastic” relationship when they met in Shenzhen last week. Jurors found Huawei guilty of 10 of the 12 criminal counts facing it — including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States. China hit back on Wednesday, saying it “firmly opposes the US suppressing and containing Chinese enterprises and firmly supports Chinese enterprises in safeguarding their legitimate rights and interests.” Trump’s administration has long alleged a risk of Huawei spying on behalf of the Chinese government, and previously urged countries not to use the company’s infrastructure in new 5G mobile networks. “No person or company is above the law,” US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement after the conviction. “For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft.” The US and Chinese flag. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Huawei rejected the conviction on Wednesday, saying in a statement it was “without legal or factual merit.” “We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests,” it added. ‘Necessary legal actions’ The jury did, however, acquit Huawei of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice, a move the company said it “welcomed,” adding that it “confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years.” “We believe the government’s remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit… We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests,” the statement continued. The charges in part involved Huawei’s business dealings with the government of Iran. “Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran’s government, military, or intelligence community,” the DOJ said. “Huawei lied about its activities in Iran to banks to obtain billions of US dollars and access to US-dollar clearing services, which enabled Huawei to be a sophisticated participant in a global marketplace for telecommunications services — in part because of its lies.” The equipment manufacturer was also accused of attempting to recruit employees of US telecoms firms and obtaining technological information from them in the process. That data allegedly enabled Huawei to develop products similar to those of its competitors, which it then sold at lower prices, according to the original indictment. File photo: Wikipedia. “The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology,” the DOJ said in a release. Huawei even launched an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors, prosecutors claimed. “Today’s verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead,” Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva said in a statement.

title: Tai Po fire: Wang Fuk Court residents who sold titles excluded from third owners’ meeting next month
zh_title: 大埔火警：宏福苑卖业居民下月第三次业主大会被排除
summary: 政府指定的遭受火灾的宏福苑管理员已宣布下个月举行第三次业主会议，但已出售业权的居民除外。 2026 年 8 月 20 日，宏福苑周边地区仍被警方封锁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。合安管理公司周一宣布，宏福苑自去年11月致命大火以来的第三次业主大会将于12月6日在大埔社区中心举行。这场大火造成 168 人死亡，数千人流离失所，成为香港数十年来最致命的火灾之一。与过去两次见面不同
content:
政府指定的遭受火灾的宏福苑管理员已宣布下个月举行第三次业主会议，但已出售业权的居民除外。 2026 年 8 月 20 日，宏福苑周边地区仍被警方封锁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。合安管理公司周一宣布，宏福苑自去年11月致命大火以来的第三次业主大会将于12月6日在大埔社区中心举行。这场大火造成 168 人死亡，数千人流离失所，成为香港数十年来最致命的火灾之一。与过去的两次会议不同的是，下个月的会议将在一个地点举行，这表明合安预计出席人数将会减少。过去两次会议是在四个场地进行转播，以容纳大量前宏福苑居民。消息公布后，一些根据政府回购计划出售公寓的居民被告知，他们将不再有资格参加业主会议。 HKFP看到，在通过在线系统发出的通知中，Hop On表示，未在土地注册处记录中列为公寓注册业主的居民将无法报名参加下个月的会议。政府表示，宏福苑共有1,984户业主，其中99.3%表示愿意根据回购计划出售业权，只有13户拒绝出售。
当局表示，他们计划最早于明年立法收购所有未售出的业权。2026 年 7 月 19 日，宏福苑居民参加在大埔社区中心举行的业主会议。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。居民正在签署正式销售协议，将其产权转让给政府，一些居民已经开始根据换屋安排选择新的政府补贴单位。但据一位吴姓居民表示，一些尚未正式转让产权的居民或许可以参加下个月的会议。吴周一告诉《香港新闻社》，她的家人原计划在本月底签署正式合同，但现在要等到下个月的会议之后。合安表示，会议议程将包括宏福苑财务状况报告、任命2026财年审计师的决定，以及可能出现的任何其他事务。

【原文 English Original】
The government-appointed administrator of fire-hit Wang Fuk Court has announced a third owners’ meeting next month, excluding residents who have sold their titles. The area surrounding Wang Fuk Court remains blocked by police force on August 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Hop On Management announced on Monday that the third Wang Fuk Court owners’ meeting since last November’s deadly blaze will be held on December 6 at the Tai Po Community Centre. The blaze killed 168 people and displaced thousands, making it one of Hong Kong’s deadliest fires in decades. In a departure from the past two meetings — which were broadcast across four venues to accommodate a large turnout of former Wang Fuk Court residents — next month’s meeting will take place at a single venue, signalling that Hop On anticipates lower attendance. Following the announcement, some residents who had sold their flats under a government buyback scheme were told they would no longer be eligible to attend the owners’ meeting. In a notice issued via an online system and seen by HKFP, Hop On said residents not listed as a flat’s registered owner in Land Registry records would be unable to sign up for next month’s meeting. The government has said 99.3 per cent of all 1,984 Wang Fuk Court homeowners have indicated they are willing to sell their titles under the buyback scheme, leaving only 13 households refusing to sell. Authorities have said they plan to introduce legislation as early as next year to acquire any unsold titles. Wang Fuk Court residents attend a flat owners meeting at Tai Po Community Centre on July 19, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Residents are in the process of signing formal sales agreements to transfer their titles to the government, and some have begun selecting new government-subsidised units under a flat-swap arrangement. But some residents who have yet to formalise their title transfer may be able to attend next month’s meeting, according to one resident surnamed Woo. Woo told HKFP on Monday that her family had planned to sign the formal contract at the end of this month, but would now wait until after next month’s meeting. Hop On said the meeting agenda will include a report on Wang Fuk Court’s financial status, a decision on the appointment of an auditor for the 2026 financial year, and any other business that may arise.

title: Mysterious MQ-25 Stingray-Like Chinese Drone Emerges At Little-Known Flight Test Center
zh_title: 神秘的MQ-25类似黄貂鱼的中国无人机出现在鲜为人知的飞行测试中心
summary: 卫星图像显示，中国浦城有一架不寻常的无人驾驶飞机，其配置与波音公司的舰载 MQ-25 Stingray 非常相似。虽然我们仍然不知道无人机的功能，但该设施本身似乎也成为中国不断扩大的无人驾驶飞机工业的一个日益重要的枢纽。 Vantor 向 TWZ 提供的宽视野卫星图像显示了 2026 年 4 月 23 日位于浦城的神秘无人机。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 这架无人机最初在浦城内府机场的卫星图像中被发现后引起了人们的关注。
content:
卫星图像显示，中国浦城有一架不寻常的无人驾驶飞机，其配置与波音公司的舰载 MQ-25 Stingray 非常相似。虽然我们仍然不知道无人机的功能，但该设施本身似乎也成为中国不断扩大的无人驾驶飞机工业的一个日益重要的枢纽。 Vantor 向 TWZ 提供的一张广角卫星图像显示了 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的神秘无人机。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 这架无人机最初引起了人们的关注，因为它在中国西北部陕西省蒲城内府机场的卫星图像中被发现，可通过苹果地图查看。无人机出现在跑道上的单独图像也可以通过必应地图获得。 TWZ 随后从 Vantor 获得了浦城的图像，显​​示了相关无人驾驶飞机。真是一个惊喜！苹果地图上发现三架无人机出现在蒲城。 CH-7、九天和类似MQ-25的无人机。 pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 18 日再次出现在 bing 地图上！这次它出现在跑道上 pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 除了不明飞行器之外，今年 4 月从蒲城拍摄的图像还揭示了似乎是 CH-7 隐形飞翼无人机和重型喷气动力九天母舰无人机的例子。 2026 年 4 月 23 日，一架 CH-7 停泊在蒲城。
卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 2026 年 4 月 23 日在蒲城的九天无人机母舰。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor 与不明飞行器最明显的比较是波音的 MQ-25 Stingray。 MQ-25是一种舰载无人飞机，主要为美国海军飞机提供空中加油，扩大舰载机联队的航程和操作灵活性。它还为未来无人海军航空能力奠定了基础。范托称，就尺寸而言，这架身份不明的中国无人机翼展约为66英尺，长度为49英尺。相比之下，MQ-25 的翼展约为 75 英尺，长度约为 51 英尺。 MQ-25 黄貂鱼。波音公司的这款中国无人机似乎具有相似的总体设计类别，但现阶段存在一些值得注意的重要差异。最引人注目的之一是前机身。与MQ-25不同，MQ-25的前部具有相对扁平的铲状外观，中国飞机似乎有一个更传统的锥形机头。也许这可以包含一个容纳雷达设备的锥形天线罩。这个理论，而且它只是一个理论，可以通过机头与黄色底漆机身的不同颜色来支持。进气量也不同。
与 MQ-25 相关的异国情调的齐平进气道不同，中国设计有一个更传统的背部进气道，看起来呈锯齿状，有助于雷达信号和/或分成两个通道。另一种可能性是飞机有两个发动机，尽管基于明显的分叉进气道，这仍然是推测性的。左侧浦城图像中的无人机和 MQ-25 的并排视图，提供了它们入口的比较视图。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor/Boeing 尾部配置也可能很独特，具有横向展开的 V 型尾翼，如 MQ-25，但可能采用可见控制面，而不是全移动水平尾翼设计。综合起来，这些功能

【原文 English Original】
Satellite imagery has revealed an unusual uncrewed aircraft at Pucheng, China, with a configuration that bears very strong similarities to Boeing’s carrier-based MQ-25 Stingray . While we still have no idea about the function of the drone, the facility itself also appears to be an increasingly important hub for China’s expanding uncrewed aircraft industry . A wider-view satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor shows the mystery drone at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The drone initially attracted attention after being spotted in a satellite image of Pucheng Neifu Airport in Shaanxi Province, in northwestern China, available through Apple Maps. A separate image of the drone, where it appears on a runway, is also available through Bing Maps. TWZ subsequently obtained imagery of Pucheng from Vantor showing the uncrewed aircraft in question. what a suprise! Three UAV spotted at Pucheng on apple maps. CH-7, Jiutian and a MQ-25 like UAV. pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 18, 2026 spotted again on bing maps! and it's on the runway this time pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 19, 2026 As well as the unidentified aircraft, imagery from Pucheng dating from April of this year also reveals what appears to be a CH-7 stealthy flying-wing drone and an example of the heavyweight jet-powered Jiutian mothership drone . A CH-7 at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor A Jiutian drone mothership at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The most obvious comparison for the unidentified aircraft is Boeing’s MQ-25 Stingray. The MQ-25 is a carrier-based uncrewed aircraft developed primarily to provide aerial refueling for U.S. Navy aircraft, extending the range and operational flexibility of carrier air wings. It also provides a foundation for future uncrewed naval aviation capabilities . In terms of dimensions, the unidentified Chinese UAV has a wingspan of approximately 66 feet and a length of 49 feet, according to Vantor. In contrast, the MQ-25 measures approximately 75 feet in wingspan and 51 feet in length. MQ-25 Stingray. Boeing The Chinese drone appears to occupy a similar general design category, but there are several important differences notable at this stage. One of the most noticeable is the forward fuselage. Unlike the MQ-25, whose forward section has a relatively flattened, shovel-like appearance, the Chinese aircraft appears to have a more conventional, tapered nose. Perhaps this could incorporate a conical radome housing radar equipment. That theory, and it is just a theory, could be supported by the different color of the nose compared to the yellow primer-painted airframe. The air intake is also different. Rather than the exotic, flush inlet associated with the MQ-25 , the Chinese design has a more conventional dorsal intake that appears serrated to help with radar signature and/or split into two channels. Another possibility is that the aircraft has two engines, although that remains speculative, based on the apparent bifurcated intake. A side-by-side look at the drone seen in the image of Pucheng, at left, and an MQ-25, offering comparative views of their inlets. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/Boeing The tail configuration may also be distinctive, with a laterally flared V-tail, like the MQ-25, but possibly incorporating visible control surfaces instead of an all-moving tailplane design. Taken together, these features suggest an aircraft that shares some of the MQ-25’s general design philosophy but is not an attempt at a direct clone. Long-time Chinese aerospace observer and TWZ contributor Andreas Rupprecht , who has been following developments surrounding the aircraft, believes China could be following a development path similar to Boeing’s, potentially producing a carrier-based uncrewed aerial refueling platform that can also undertake intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. “I think China is actually following the same path as Boeing here, and it’s heading towards a tanker that can also take on other roles as an ISR platform,” Rupprecht told us. A radar-equipped aircraft with substantial endurance could potentially perform surveillance and other sensor-related missions when not being used as a tanker. The potential development of a multirole uncrewed tanker at Pucheng would also fit into a much broader push by China to expand the role of uncrewed aircraft in its naval aviation forces. One of the most notable developments is the GJ-21 , a navalized derivative of the GJ-11 Sharp Sword stealth uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV). Featuring folding wings and provisions for catapult launches and arrested recoveries, the low-observable flying-wing design is intended to operate from China’s growing fleet of large-deck warships , including the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . In October 2026, Chinese state media reported that the GJ-21 had successfully completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the vessel, a significant milestone in the development of shipborne fixed-wing combat drones. GJ-21 carrier-based UCAV. via Chinese internet The GJ-21 effort is taking place alongside the introduction of China’s new catapult-equipped Fujian aircraft carrier, which has begun operating the J-35 stealth fighter, J-15T carrier-based fighter, and KJ-600 airborne early warning aircraft. Taken together, these developments point to an increasingly ambitious effort to integrate uncrewed aircraft into China’s future carrier air wings , potentially spanning stealthy strike platforms, surveillance systems, and other specialized support aircraft. The unidentified Pucheng aircraft could represent another, quite different part of that wider effort — or something else altogether. At the same time, this aircraft is roughly 20 percent dimensionally smaller than the MQ-25, which would mean it would have less fuel to give. It’s also worth noting that Boeing’s MQ-25 emerged from an unmanned combat air vehicle (UCAV) design that included low-observable features. Multirole UCAV concepts predating it also looked very similar. The MRE concept from Lockheed during the 1990s looks very similar to the MQ-25 we know today. (Lockheed Martin) In addition, Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), for instance, the FQ-42 Vengeance, and also the XQ-67 Off-Board Sensing Station share a similar overall design. With this in mind, and remembering its different nose section, this could just as easily be a true multirole UCAV or even a CCA, such as one designed for force protection of high-value aerial assets, and it may not even be carrier-capable. Rupprecht cautioned that the manufacturer of the mystery drone remains unidentified. However, one of the more interesting clues about the aircraft’s possible origins comes from Shenyang Aircraft Corporation (SAC). Rupprecht pointed to a propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025, which he believes could fit the development lineage of the larger aircraft now visible at Pucheng. The sub-scale propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025. The background reads (rough translation): “Rollout Ceremony for Final Assembly of Shenyang’s First ‘Surrogate Flight Test’ Pilot-Test Verification Platform UAV.” via Chinese internet A smaller, propeller-driven demonstrator could provide a relatively inexpensive way to investigate aerodynamic characteristics, autonomous flight controls, mission systems, and other technologies before progressing to a much larger aircraft. This piston-powered, propeller-driven aircraft with a broadly similar configuration to the MQ-25 was seen in a video flying, as well. 突然想起中国一家民营无人机公司，做过一款MQ-25活塞桨叶版 https://t.co/Y69dfzpLNS pic.twitter.com/IzU08PC8DK — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) November 18, 2026 Whether the Pucheng aircraft is related to this SAC demonstrator or if it’s an entirely separate program remains unknown. Beyond the external resemblance, there are no indications that they are linked, and the aircraft could just be a general test surrogate platform. The configuration isn’t totally novel in the advanced UAS world. The aircraft’s appearance is also interesting given the location where it has been spotted. Pucheng Neifu Airport is located in Shaanxi Province, and its surrounding aviation facilities include an area identified in Apple Maps as the National Aeronautics Industrial Base Pucheng General Aviation Industrial Park Guanliban. The industrial park has its own smaller runway, separate from the main airport infrastructure. A close-up of Pucheng with no drones visible, as of June 16, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 The site had remained relatively obscure to outside observers until roughly the past one to two years, according to Rupprecht. More recently, however, various aircraft manufacturers have apparently been conducting testing there. This raises the possibility that Pucheng is not simply an individual manufacturer’s flight-test location, but a facility used by multiple organizations developing and evaluating uncrewed aircraft. Rupprecht also raised the possibility that Pucheng could potentially be a specialized uncrewed aircraft testing facility associated with China’s Flight Test Establishment at Xi’an, commonly known as CFTE. “I cannot say (yet) whether this — and this is my theory — is effectively a branch of the CFTE at Xi’an, which is for crewed and this is a base for uncrewed ones,” Rupprecht explained. A satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor provides an overview of Pucheng as of April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor If Pucheng does serve as a shared testing location for multiple manufacturers, it could help explain the appearance of several otherwise unrelated UAV designs at the same site. Returning to the mystery drone, the combination of its apparent size, configuration, and possible connection to earlier Chinese demonstrator programs makes it an interesting development to watch. Regardless, for now, the imagery from Pucheng offers a glimpse of a potentially significant new Chinese uncrewed aircraft program. 美国关税提案增加了印度贸易协议的利害关系海峡时报
美国关税提案增加了印度达成贸易协议的赌注
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
美国计划对印度商品征收17%的关税，如果印度未能与美国达成贸易协议，关税将提高至25%。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 26 日 06:37
更新于 2026 年 11 月 26 日 12:25
美国计划对印度商品征收17%的关税，如果未能达成贸易协议，关税将升至25%，这给印度最大的出口市场带来压力。
分析人士表示，该提议具有强制性，增加了不确定性，而印度希望通过双边谈判解决关税问题。
美印贸易谈判自二月份以来一直在继续，但尽管最近形势乐观，但美国的调查和俄罗斯的石油制裁使协议变得复杂。
美国11月25日宣布的关税税率给印度带来了压力，要求其同意贸易协议，否则将面临更高的征税，这使得出口商和投资者对贸易前景不太清楚。
美国计划对印度商品征收 17% 的关税，低于越南、马来西亚和孟加拉国等地区同行。美国贸易代表的一份声明称，如果印度未能与其最大出口市场美国达成贸易协议，税率将提高至25%。
分析人士表示，美国的提议相当于胁迫，给贸易前景带来更多不确定性。
总部位于新德里的全球贸易研究计划创始人阿贾伊·斯里瓦斯塔瓦表示：“通过部署双税率结构——威胁对拒绝达成协议的国家征收高额基准关税，同时向签署协议的国家提供较低的税率——华盛顿重新获得了随意征收关税并获取单方面让步的议价能力。”
这些关税需接受公众意见征询程序，适用于美国的主要贸易伙伴，包括中国和欧盟，旨在解决对制造业产能过剩的担忧。它们标志着特朗普政府在遭到法院阻挠后恢复关税议程的最新努力。
自二月份同意框架以来，美国和印度的谈判代表一直就贸易协议进行谈判。美国的贸易调查以及最近通过的俄罗斯石油制裁法使谈判变得复杂。该立法使唐纳德·特朗普总统能够对印度等俄罗斯石油的最大买家征收高达 100% 的关税。
尽管局势紧张，但近几个月双方都对贸易协议即将敲定表示乐观。印度商务部长拉杰什·阿格拉瓦尔上周表示，“协议的各个方面都或多或少已经敲定”，但关税方面还需要进一步明确。
印度商工部在一份声明中表示，它在调查期间“建设性地参与”，任何与贸易相关的担忧都应通过美印双边协议谈判来解决。
均富会计师事务所（Grant Thornton Bharat）合伙人兼税务争议管理负责人马诺吉·米什拉（Manoj Mishra）表示，美国最新的提议“增加了印美贸易关系的不确定性”。他补充说，有竞争力的 17% 关税税率的可能性“凸显了加快双边贸易谈判的必要性”。彭博社

US tariff proposal raises stakes for India to clinch trade deal
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The US plans to impose a 17% tariff on Indian goods and the rate would be hiked to 25% if India fails to secure a trade deal with the US.
Published Nov 26, 2026, 06:37 AM
Updated Nov 26, 2026, 12:25 PM
The US plans a 17% tariff on Indian goods, rising to 25% if no trade deal is reached, putting pressure on India’s biggest export market.
Analysts say the proposal is coercive and adds uncertainty, while India wants tariff issues settled through bilateral talks.
US-India trade talks have continued since February, but US probes and Russian oil sanctions have complicated the deal, despite recent optimism.
US tariff rates announced on Nov 25 put pressure on India to agree to a trade deal or face a higher levy, leaving exporters and investors with little clarity on the trade outlook.
The US plans to impose a 17% tariff on Indian goods, lower than regional peers like Vietnam, Malaysia and Bangladesh. The rate would be hiked to 25% if India fails to secure a trade deal with the US, its biggest export market, according to a statement from the US Trade Representative.
Analysts said the US proposal amounts to coercion and creates more uncertainty about the trade outlook.
“By deploying a dual-rate structure – threatening steep baseline tariffs against countries that refuse a pact while offering lower rates to those that sign – Washington reclaims the bargaining power to impose duties at will and extract unilateral concessions,” said Ajay Srivastava, founder of the New Delhi-based Global Trade Research Initiative.
The tariffs, which are subject to a public comment process, apply to the US’ main trading partners, including China and the European Union, and are intended to address concerns over excess manufacturing capacity. They mark the latest effort by the Trump administration to reinstate its tariff agenda after being thwarted by the courts.
Negotiators from the US and India have been locked in talks over a trade deal since agreeing to a framework in February. The US trade probes, as well as a recently passed law on Russian oil sanctions, have complicated the negotiations. The legislation gives President Donald Trump the ability to impose tariffs of as much as 100% on the top buyers of Russian oil, like India.
Despite the tensions, both sides have in recent months expressed optimism that a trade deal was close to being finalised. India’s Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said last week that “every aspect of the deal has been more or less finalised”, but greater clarity was needed on the tariffs.
In a statement, India’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry said it had “engaged constructively” during the investigation, and that any trade-related concerns should be addressed through US-India talks for the bilateral deal.
The latest US proposal “adds to the uncertainty surrounding India-US trade relations”, said Manoj Mishra, a partner and tax controversy management leader at Grant Thornton Bharat. The possibility of a competitive 17% tariff rate “underscores the need to expedite bilateral trade negotiations”, he added. BLOOMBERG

title: Stratum AI model feeds Simberi’s mineral resource estimate
zh_title: Stratum AI 模型为 Simberi 的矿产资源估算提供数据
summary: Stratum AI 表示，在采矿业采用人工智能 (AI) 方面，它已经达到了一个“重要里程碑”——其模型支持了公开报告的矿产资源估算 (MRE)，这是采矿业首批此类案例之一。这家总部位于多伦多的深度科技公司与 St Barbara (ASX: SBM) 合作，将 Stratum 的风化和材料类型深度学习模型纳入巴布亚新几内亚 Simberi 黄金项目的 MRE 中。 “St Barbara 利用 Stratum AI 的专有算法对某些矿石进行分类，这些矿石以前被认为是
content:
Stratum AI 表示，在采矿业采用人工智能 (AI) 方面，它已经达到了一个“重要里程碑”——其模型支持了公开报告的矿产资源估算 (MRE)，这是采矿业首批此类案例之一。这家总部位于多伦多的深度科技公司与 St Barbara (ASX: SBM) 合作，将 Stratum 的风化和材料类型深度学习模型纳入巴布亚新几内亚 Simberi 黄金项目的 MRE 中。 Stratum 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Farzi Yusufali 表示：“St Barbara 利用 Stratum AI 的专有算法对以前被认为不适合 Simberi 现有碳浸出循环的某些矿石进行分类。” “最初的人工智能试点已经发展成为一项技术，现在支撑着 Simberi 可行性研究中的矿产资源估算。”该公司表示，MRE 的报告符合 JORC 准则，符合澳大利亚证券交易所的上市准则。人工智能在1969年勘探者放弃的地方开采铜金 Simberi位于巴布亚新几内亚的新爱尔兰省，由St Barbara、Lingbao Gold（SEHK：3330）和Kumul Mineral Holdings共同拥有。 9月，圣芭芭拉宣布有意将其在Simberi的权益出售给灵宝。该交易预计将于 2027 年初完成。Approach Stratum 已与 St Barbara 在 Simberi 合作四年多，开发基于人工智能的矿化分类方法。
这些模型最初部署在试点项目中，用于分析勘探数据。后来，它们被用于分析运营数据，使 St Barbara 能够确定哪些矿石适合通过现有的碳浸出 (CIL) 工厂进行加工，哪些矿石需要与硫化矿石一起储存以供日后处理。 Stratum 表示，能够区分矿石类型使 St Barbara 能够降低与产生额外废物相关的成本，并减少磨机的磨损。模型经过测试后，圣芭芭拉采用它们作为材料类型分类的首选方法。该模型帮助构建了 Simberi 的 2024 年资源和储量更新及其 2025 年可行性研究。 2024 年 5 月，该矿业公司表示，它在 Simberi 发现了额外 143,000 盎司的可处理材料，将矿山的处理寿命延长了 17 个月。 St Barbara 还表示，Stratum 的模型帮助其探明和推定矿石储量增加了 40%。

【原文 English Original】
Stratum AI says it has reached a “significant milestone” in the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in mining — its model has underpinned a publicly reported mineral resource estimate (MRE) in one of the first cases of its kind in the mining industry. The Toronto-based deep-tech company collaborated with St Barbara (ASX: SBM) to incorporate Stratum’s deep-learning models of weathering and material type into the MRE for the Simberi gold project in Papua New Guinea. “St Barbara has harnessed Stratum AI’s proprietary algorithms to classify certain ores that were previously considered to be unsuitable for Simberi’s existing carbon-in-leach circuit,” said Farzi Yusufali, Stratum’s co-founder and CEO. “What began as an AI pilot has evolved into a technology that now underpins the mineral resource estimate in Simberi’s feasibility study.” The company says the MRE was reported in line with the JORC Code, meeting the listing guidelines of the Australian Securities Exchange. AI strikes copper-gold where explorers gave up in 1969 Located in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea, Simberi is jointly owned by St Barbara, Lingbao Gold (SEHK: 3330) and Kumul Mineral Holdings. In September, St Barbara announced its intention to sell its interest in Simberi to Lingbao. The transaction is expected to be completed in early 2027. Approach Stratum has been working with St Barbara for more than four years at Simberi to develop an AI-based approach to classify mineralization. The models were initially deployed in pilot programs to analyze exploration data. They were later used to analyze operational data, allowing St Barbara to determine which ores were suitable for processing through the existing carbon-in-leach (CIL) plant and which needed to be stockpiled for later treatment alongside sulfide ores. Stratum says being able to differentiate between ores types allowed St Barbara to reduce costs associated with generating extra waste, and saved wear and tear on the mill. After the models were tested, St Barbara adopted them as its preferred method for material-type classification. The modelling helped build Simberi’s 2024 resource and reserve update and its 2025 feasibility study. In May 2024, the mining company said it was able to identify an additional 143,000 ounces of treatable material at Simberi, extending the mine’s processing life by 17 months. St Barbara also said that Stratum’s modelling had helped increase its proved and probable ore reserves by 40%.

content:
澳大利亚悉尼——

陆军对话是一个定期举行的论坛，使参与国能够协调战役工作、讨论行动优先事项并确定加强合作的机会。该论坛包括高级领导人参与活动和工作组，以推动整个印太地区的陆军活动。

太平洋陆军在悉尼陆军对话技术工作组期间加强合作 摄影：CPL Hamid Farahani

2026 年 11 月 17 日，陆军对话 - 技术工作组期间，来自澳大利亚、美国、日本和菲律宾的高级领导人和代表团成员出席了在悉尼维多利亚军营军官食堂举行的破冰活动。*** 本地字幕 *** 参加陆军对话 - 技术工作组的高级军事领导人和代表在正式讨论之前出席了在悉尼维多利亚军营举行的破冰活动。该活动为来自澳大利亚、美国、日本和菲律宾的代表提供了建立专业关系并讨论共同安全利益的机会。陆军对话-技术工作组是参与陆军的一个重要论坛，旨在加强合作并改善整个印太地区未来行动、活动和投资的同步性。
澳大利亚陆军主办了为期四天的论坛，汇聚了代表四个盟国和伙伴国的六个军种的人员：澳大利亚陆军、日本陆上自卫队、菲律宾陆军、菲律宾海军陆战队、美国太平洋海军陆战队和美国太平洋陆军。与会者的重点是在 2027 年及以后调整战略态势、提高作战持久力以及增强多边地面力量能力。

> “我们通过陆军对话等论坛建立的关系增强了我们在最重要的时候共同行动的能力，”

美国太平洋海军陆战队副司令马修·T·莫厄里少将说道。

> “将四个国家和六个军种聚集在一起，使我们能够更好地调整优先事项，提高互操作性，并在共同计划下作为一支统一的力量开展行动。这种合作加强了我们的集体准备，并加强了我们对自由开放的印太地区的承诺。”

SYDNEY, Australia --

Land Forces Dialogue is a recurring forum that enables participating nations to coordinate campaign efforts, discuss operational priorities and identify opportunities to enhance cooperation. The forum includes senior leader engagements and working groups that advance land force activities across the Indo-Pacific.

Pacific Land Forces Strengthen Cooperation During Land Forces Dialogue Technical Working Group in Sydney Photo by CPL Hamid Farahani

Senior leaders and delegation members from Australia, the United States, Japan and the Philippines attend an ice-breaker function at the Victoria Barracks Officers' Mess, Sydney, during the Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group on 17 November 2026. *** Local Caption *** Senior military leaders and delegates participating in the Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group attended an ice-breaker function at Victoria Barracks, Sydney, ahead of formal discussions. The function provided an opportunity for delegates from Australia, the United States, Japan and the Philippines to build professional relationships and discuss shared security interests. The Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group serves as a key forum for participating land forces to strengthen cooperation and improve synchronisation of future operations, activities and investments throughout the Indo-Pacific region.

The Australian Army hosted the four-day forum, which brought together personnel from six military services representing four allied and partner nations: the Australian Army, Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, Philippine Army, Philippine Marine Corps, U.S. Marine Corps Forces Pacific, and U.S. Army Pacific. Participants focused on aligning strategic posture, improving operational endurance, and enhancing multilateral land power capabilities through calendar year 2027 and beyond.

> “The relationships we build through forums like the Land Forces Dialogue strengthen our ability to operate together when it matters most,”

said Maj. Gen. Matthew T. Mowery, deputy commander, U.S. Marine Corps Forces, Pacific.

> “Bringing together four nations and six military services allows us to better align priorities, improve interoperability and campaign as a unified force under a shared plan. That cooperation strengthens our collective readiness and reinforces our commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific.”

The function provided an opportunity for delegates from Australia, the United States, Japan and the Philippines to build professional relationships and discuss shared security interests. The Land Force Dialogue – Technical Working Group serves as a key forum for participating land forces to strengthen cooperation and improve synchronisation of future operations, activities and investments throughout the Indo-Pacific region.

The Land Forces Dialogue provides a forum for sustained engagement on shared military priorities. The dialogue enables participating nations to coordinate campaign activities, align operational priorities and identify opportunities for future cooperation.

Participants reaffirmed their commitment to synchronize multilateral training objectives, increase operational effectiveness and enhance crisis-response capabilities. By building on established relationships and routine multinational training opportunities, the four nations continue to advance practical military cooperation and strengthen their ability to respond to shared security challenges.

title: 澳洲政府推出新福利：房东获 3500 澳元补贴，租客电费减半

content: 澳大利亚租客正迎来一些令人欣慰的生活成本缓解，一项鲜为人知的太阳能计划正帮助一些家庭大幅削减电费。 昆士兰州政府正在帮助租客降低电费，向房东提供最高3,500澳元的补贴，用于在出租房产安装太阳能板。 自去年12月启动以来，已有超过600名房东获得补贴，为租客安装太阳能系统。 据Crisafulli政府称，昆士兰州民的电价正在下降，该州东南部居民的电价降幅在7.2%至10.7%之间，而偏远城镇居民的电价降幅为7%。 不到12个月内，该计划已收到超过1,000份申请，其中600份已完成，400份待评估，大多数已安装系统超过5千瓦，从而获得全额3,500澳元补贴。 财政部长兼能源部长David Janetzki表示，“Supercharged Solar for Renters”计划旨在为辛勤工作的昆士兰州民提供具有成本效益的生活方式。 “房东们已经加入进来，租客们正从更便宜的电费账单中获益。这种缓解对家庭产生了真正的改变，”Janetzki说。 租客享受更便宜太阳能的回报 昆士兰州政府转述了房东和租客关于“Supercharged Solar for Renters”计划如何为他们双方省钱的故事。 房东Dave Pritchard表示，补贴使安装太阳能更加负担得起。另一方面，租客Stacey Kerr表示，拥有太阳能开辟了新的节省渠道。 “自从安装太阳能系统以来，与去年相比，我们的电费账单减少了一半，”Kerr说。 “对于租客来说，这是显著的节省，对我们日常家庭开支产生了真正的改变。” 昆士兰州在Energex和Ergon Energy网络中共有超过90万套屋顶太阳能系统接入，参与计划的房东必须使用Crisafulli政府能源路线图下持牌、认证的安装商。

title: China’s Cargo Drones Keep Getting Bigger With New W8000
zh_title: 新型 W8000 助力中国货运无人机不断发展壮大
summary: 中国部署越来越大的无人货运飞机的野心正在不断增强，白鲸航空推出了 W8000 货运无人机，据报道，这款货运无人机设计可承载 8 吨（略低于 18,000 磅）。该飞机代表了该公司自主货运航空计划的重大扩展，恰逢其较小的 W5000 已开始飞行测试。参观者在珠海 W8000 前合影。来自中国互联网 W5000（左）停在珠海的 W8000 旁边。来自中国互联网 W8000先于中国国际航空展亮相珠海
content:
中国部署越来越大的无人货运飞机的野心正在不断增强，白鲸航空推出了 W8000 货运无人机，据报道，这款货运无人机设计可承载 8 吨（略低于 18,000 磅）。该飞机代表了该公司自主货运航空计划的重大扩展，恰逢其较小的 W5000 已开始飞行测试。参观者在珠海 W8000 前合影。来自中国互联网 W5000（左）停在珠海的 W8000 旁边。来自中国互联网 W8000 在中国国际航空航天博览会（俗称中国航展）之前亮相珠海。在 12 月 7 日该活动开幕之前，我们已经抢先了解了一个平台，该平台旨在将无人货运能力提升到目前仅限于传统载人运输机的水平。据报道，其有效载荷为 8 吨，远高于 W5000，后者的设计载荷可达 5 吨（11,000 磅）。与 W5000 一样，W8000 可以通过后坡道装卸。 W8000 尾部的翻盖式门和后装载坡道。然而目前，双涡轮螺旋桨飞机 W8000 仍然是一个开发概念。其有效载荷数字只是设计目标，其航程、最大起飞重量和操作要求等细节仍不清楚。
为了进行比较，八吨的有效载荷将使 W8000 与 DHC-5 Buffalo 双引擎涡轮螺旋桨短距起降运输机处于同一类别。无论如何，此次亮相凸显了白鲸航空开发一系列大型无人驾驶货运飞机的雄心，目标是区域货运、偏远地区物流和潜在的军事运输任务，在这些任务中，自主飞机可以比传统货运业务提供优势。珠海W8000的后视图。来自中国互联网 双涡轮螺旋桨飞机 W8000 动力装置所使用的发动机尚未确定。通过中国互联网 更大的无人运输 W8000 的有效负载能力将使其能够运输大型设备、托盘货物、工业用品和其他大件货物。在商业环境中，大型自主货运飞机在公路或铁路基础设施有限或传统航空运输过于昂贵而无法频繁运营的航线上特别有用。尽管消除了机上机组人员，但飞机仍然需要维护人员、地勤人员、货物装载基础设施和支持性运营网络。最终，该飞机也可能被批准在受控空域内运行，取代载人支线货运业务，但这种用例在未来仍有一段路要走。不可避免的是，该飞机的发展也表明了大型货运无人机的潜在军事意义。
珠海的 W5000 和 W8000。来自中国互联网 W8000 可以为中国人民解放军 (PLA) 提供大量额外的空运选择，以保障在偏远、孤立或基础设施匮乏的地点作战的部队。这在印度-太平洋地区尤其重要，中国不断扩大的军事设施和岛屿前哨网络已经对频繁的补给飞行产生了需求。例如，在南中国海，大型货运无人机可以将设备、医疗用品、备件和其他必需品运输到远程设施，而无需载人运输

【原文 English Original】
China’s ambitions to field increasingly large, uncrewed cargo aircraft are growing, with Air White Whale unveiling its W8000, a cargo UAV reportedly designed to carry up to eight metric tons — a little less than 18,000 pounds. The aircraft represents a significant expansion of the company’s plans for autonomous freight aviation, coming just as its smaller W5000 has begun flight testing. Visitors pose in front of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W5000 (left) parked next to the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W8000 appeared in Zhuhai, ahead of the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China . Before that event opens its doors on December 7, we have gotten an early look at a platform intended to push uncrewed cargo capacity into a class now limited to conventional, crewed transport aircraft. Its reported eight-ton payload would put it substantially above the W5000, which is designed to carry up to five metric tons (11,000 pounds). Like the W5000, the W8000 can be loaded and unloaded via a rear ramp. Clamshell doors and rear loading ramp in the tail of the W8000. via Chinese internet For now, however, the twin-turboprop W8000 remains a developmental concept. Its payload figure is a design target, and details about its range, maximum takeoff weight, and operational requirements are still unclear. For purposes of comparison, an eight-metric-ton payload would put the W8000 in much the same category as the DHC-5 Buffalo twin-engine turboprop STOL transport. Regardless, the unveiling highlights Air White Whale’s ambitions to develop a family of large uncrewed cargo aircraft, targeting regional freight, remote-area logistics, and potentially military transportation missions where autonomous aircraft could offer advantages over conventional cargo operations. Rear view of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The engines used in the powerplant for the twin-turboprop W8000 are yet to be identified. via Chinese internet An Even Bigger Uncrewed Transport The W8000’s payload capacity would allow it to transport large equipment, palletized freight, industrial supplies, and other bulky cargo. In a commercial context, large autonomous cargo aircraft could be particularly useful on routes where road or rail infrastructure is limited, or where conventional air transport is too expensive to operate frequently. Although eliminating onboard flight crews, the aircraft would still require maintenance personnel, ground handling, cargo-loading infrastructure, and a supporting operational network. Ultimately, the aircraft could also be cleared to operate inside controlled airspace, displacing crewed feeder cargo operations, but that use case is still some way off in the future. Inevitably, the aircraft’s development also points toward the potential military relevance of large cargo UAVs. The W5000 and W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W8000 could offer the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) a substantial additional airlift option for sustaining forces operating from remote, isolated, or infrastructure-poor locations. This is particularly relevant in the Indo-Pacific, where China’s expanding network of military facilities and island outposts is already creating demand for frequent resupply flights. In the South China Sea, for example, large cargo UAVs could potentially transport equipment, medical supplies, spare parts, and other necessities to remote installations without requiring a crewed transport aircraft for every mission. They could also support operations in western China , including remote and high-altitude regions where road infrastructure is limited and conventional air transport can face additional challenges. There are also potential applications in a conflict, where conventional logistics infrastructure could be damaged or otherwise unavailable. Uncrewed transports would remove the risk to aircrews during routine resupply missions through contested airspace, although the aircraft themselves would remain vulnerable. They would also remove the need for combat search and rescue (CSAR) capabilities, which might be impossible to provide in at least some scenarios. Their usefulness would also depend, at least in some cases, on reliable communications, autonomous navigation, and the ability to operate without continuous access to satellite navigation. Profile view of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet W5000 Has Already Begun Flight Testing The W8000’s unveiling comes as Air White Whale’s smaller W5000 has reached a significant development milestone, completing its maiden flight on November 14. The five-ton cargo UAV reportedly conducted a roughly 30-minute test flight after taking off within approximately 600 meters (1,969 feet). During the flight, it reportedly conducted maneuvers and tested autonomous flight functions, datalink communications, propulsion, and flight-control systems before landing. China’s W5000 large cargo UAV has completed its maiden flight in the Ordos region of Inner Mongolia on 14 November. The aircraft reportedly took off after a 600 m (1,969 ft) ground run, climbed to 2,000 m (6,562 ft) and completed a 30-minute test flight. The trial included… pic.twitter.com/NNLqPKbLLZ — Drone Wars (@Drone_Wars_) November 14, 2026 The W5000 is designed to carry up to five metric tons of cargo, with a reported maximum range of 2,600 kilometers (1,616 miles), maximum takeoff weight of 10.8 tons (21,600 pounds), and cargo compartment volume exceeding 65 cubic meters (2,295 cubic feet). The aircraft is powered by twin turboprop engines. Chinese sources claim that Air White Whale has received 835 orders or prospective commitments from domestic logistics companies for the W5000, although the nature of those commitments and how many represent firm purchase contracts remain unclear. Commercial operations are currently planned to begin by the end of 2027, subject to further testing and certification. The W5000’s flight provides an indication of the company’s progress toward developing large uncrewed cargo aircraft, but the W8000 is a considerably more ambitious undertaking. Several other companies are also pursuing increasingly ambitious uncrewed transport aircraft. These include Tengden’s four-engine TB-001D Scorpion D , which first flew in October 2022 and is designed to carry up to 1.5 metric tons (3,307 pounds) of cargo, as well as the Star UAV System-developed AT200, another 1.5-ton-class cargo drone. The TB0D Scorpion D built by China’s Tengden Technology company completed its maiden flight in Sichuan on October 25, 2022. Twitter video screenshot Other designs include the state-owned Aviation Industry Corporation of China’s HH-100 , with a reported payload capacity of around 700 kilograms (1,543 pounds), and the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation’s CH-YH1000 , designed to carry approximately one metric ton (2,205 pounds). While these aircraft vary considerably in size, configuration, and intended missions, their development highlights China’s broader push to establish uncrewed cargo aviation as a viable logistics capability. A demonstrator of China’s HH-100 commercial cargo drone. Photo by Yue Shuhua/VCG via Getty Images VCG Outside of China, there is some other notable activity in this sector. The United States is also pursuing large uncrewed cargo aircraft for military logistics. As we reported , Textron Aviation and autonomy specialist Merlin recently unveiled the Cessna SkyCourier UX, a concept based on the twin-engine Cessna 408 SkyCourier. The proposed aircraft would use Merlin’s autonomous flight system and could carry approximately 6,000 pounds of cargo. Its designers are exploring a cockpit-less configuration with a hydraulically opening nose section for direct cargo loading, as well as kneeling landing gear and integrated loading systems to simplify operations at austere locations. With a reported range of around 900 nautical miles, the SkyCourier UX is intended to support distributed military forces, including across the Pacific, where it could move supplies between larger logistics hubs and smaller, remote operating locations. The U.S. Air Force has also experimented with autonomous Cessna Caravan aircraft through Joby Aviation and its former Xwing autonomy team, including logistics demonstrations across the Pacific. Better known for land vehicles, Oshkosh Defense also recently announced a partnership with Silicon Valley startup Grid Aero, with the aim of building large military cargo drones. These would draw upon Grid Aero’s experience developing the Lifter family, an autonomous aircraft series with modular payload capacity that the company describes as a “pickup truck of the skies.” The Lifter is planned to carry somewhere between 1,000 and 8,000 pounds over a distance of approximately 1,500 miles.  The Grid Aero Lifter. Oshkosh/Grid Aero While the United States is moving slower than China in this space, there is arguably an even stronger operational case for such capabilities in the U.S. military, given the expeditionary nature of a potential conflict across the vast distances of the Indo-Pacific . Sustaining forces spread across widely separated islands, remote airfields, and austere forward operating locations would place enormous demands on conventional airlift and sealift networks. China Targets A New Class Of Cargo Aviation Overall, the development of the W5000 and W8000 highlights China’s growing interest in cargo UAVs capable of moving freight measured in metric tons rather than kilograms. While smaller delivery drones are increasingly being explored for last-mile transportation, aircraft such as the W8000 are aimed at moving substantial loads between logistics hubs without requiring an onboard crew. If the W8000 progresses, it could eventually offer a heavier transport option alongside the W5000, allowing Air White Whale to target different cargo requirements and routes. The W5000 and W8000 at Zhuhai ahead of Airshow China. via Chinese internet For now, the W8000 points to where Air White Whale wants to take its cargo UAV program. The W5000’s flight-test program will be an important step in establishing whether the company can turn its designs into operational aircraft and start to offer a new class of uncrewed airlift. title: Amphibs USS Makin Island, USS John P. Murtha Depart Singapore
zh_title: 两栖战舰马金岛号和约翰·P·穆萨号两栖攻击舰离开新加坡
summary: 黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 于 2026 年 10 月 26 日抵达日本横须贺舰队活动司令部。美国海军照片 两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 和两栖运输船坞号 USS 约翰·P·默斯 a (LPD-26) 于周二从新加坡三巴旺出发，前往印度洋。根据当地船舶观察员和 AIS 数据，马金岛号和约翰·P·默塔号随第 13 海军陆战队远征部队的部队出发，正在通过马六甲海峡向北航行。 AIS数据显示两艘船当时位于马六甲以南的马六甲海峡
content:
黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 于 2026 年 10 月 26 日抵达日本横须贺舰队活动司令部。美国海军照片 两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 和两栖运输船坞号 USS 约翰·P·默斯 a (LPD-26) 于周二从新加坡三巴旺出发，前往印度洋。根据当地船舶观察员和 AIS 数据，马金岛号和约翰·P·默塔号随第 13 海军陆战队远征部队的部队出发，正在通过马六甲海峡向北航行。 AIS数据显示，两艘船于晚上10点位于马来西亚首都吉隆坡以南的马六甲海峡。当地时间，美国海军拉帕汉诺克号舰队加油船 (T-AO-204)。马金岛、约翰·P·穆萨、两栖运输船坞舰安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和已登船的第 13 远征远征队组成了马金岛两栖准备大队。安克雷奇及其第 13 海军陆战队远征部队分队目前驻扎在日本横须贺司令舰队活动司令部 (CFAY)。据 USNI News 此前报道，ARG 于 9 月 28 日从圣地亚哥出发。第13远征部队的海军陆战队空地特遣部队包括第13远征部队指挥分队、作为地面作战分队的第2/4营登陆队和作为其后勤分队的第13战斗后勤营。航空中队包括海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364（加强型）和海军陆战队战斗机攻击中队 (VMFA) 211，其中包括 MV-22B 鱼鹰、CH-53、AH-1Z 毒蛇和 F-35B 闪电 II。
ARG 于 10 月初驶入夏威夷进行港口访问，然后穿越太平洋。安克雷奇于 10 月 21 日至 22 日对关岛进行了短暂访问，然后重新加入 ARG，并于 10 月 26 日驶入 CFAY 进行港口访问。所有三艘 ARG 舰艇均于 11 月 7 日从 CFAY 出发，与约翰·P·穆萨号和安克雷奇号一起参加“马拉巴尔 2026”演习的海上阶段，这是澳大利亚、日本、印度和美国“四方”伙伴关系下的年度海军演习。演习于 11 月 5 日至 12 日在横须贺及其周边地区举行。印度海军什瓦利克级隐形多用途护卫舰INS Sahyadri (F 49)、日本海上自卫队日向级直升机驱逐舰JS Ise (DDH 182)、最上级护卫舰JS Mogami (FFM 1)、澳大利亚皇家海军安扎克级护卫舰HMAS Stuart (FFH 153)和美国海军圣安东尼奥级两栖运输舰2026 年马拉巴尔演习期间，美国海军安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和约翰·P·穆萨 (LPD-26) 号船坞编队在西太平洋航行，2026 年 11 月 7 日。美国海军照片 与约翰·P·穆萨和安克雷奇一起参加演习的有日本海上自卫队直升机驱逐舰 JS 伊势 (DDH-182)、护卫舰 JS 最上(FFM-1)、一艘日本海上自卫队潜艇、印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F49)、澳大利亚皇家海军护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH153)、一架美国海军 P-8A 海神海上巡逻机和一架日本海上自卫队 P-1 MPA。演习活动包括海军炮火、反水面战演习和反潜战演习。伊势和约翰·P.
穆萨号进行了互访、登船、搜查和扣押（VBSS）演习。“马拉巴尔2026”号完成后，约翰·P·穆萨号前往菲律宾海与马金岛会合。据当地船舶观察员称，“安克雷奇”号于 11 月 13 日在横须贺近海抛锚，并于 11 月 16 日停靠在 CFAY，占据了离开的潜艇母舰弗兰克·电缆号 (AS-40) 所腾出的空间。马金岛号和约翰·P·默撒号于周五穿越南中国海，抵达新加坡三巴旺进行港口访问。海军和五角大楼都没有表示安克雷奇是否会加入马

【原文 English Original】
Wasp-class amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) pulls in to Commander, Fleet Activities, Yokosuka, Japan, Oct. 26, 2026. US Navy photo Amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) and amphibious transport dock USS John P. Murth a (LPD-26) departed Tuesday from Sembawang, Singapore, and are heading toward the Indian Ocean. Makin Island and John P. Murtha , embarked with elements of the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, are transiting north through the Malacca Strait, according to local ship spotters and AIS data. AIS data shows the two ships were in the Malacca Strait south of Malaysia’s capital of Kuala Lumpur at 10 p.m. local time with fleet oiler USNS Rappahannock (T-AO-204). Makin Island , John P. Murtha , amphibious transport dock USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and the embarked 13th MEU form the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. Anchorage and its embarked 13th MEU elements are currently at Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka (CFAY), Japan. The ARG departed from San Diego on Sept. 28, USNI News previously reported . The 13th MEU’s Marine Air-Ground Task Force includes the 13th MEU command element, Battalion Landing Team 2/4 as the Ground Combat Element and Combat Logistics Battalion 13 as its logistic element. The aviation squadrons are Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364 (Reinforced) and Marine Fighter Attack Squadron (VMFA) 211, which includes MV-22B Ospreys, CH-53s, AH-1Z Vipers and F-35B Lightning IIs. The ARG pulled into Hawaii for a port visit in early October before transiting the Pacific. Anchorage made a short visit to Guam from Oct. 21-22 before rejoining the ARG, which pulled into CFAY on Oct. 26 for a port visit. All three ARG ships departed Nov. 7 from CFAY with John P. Murtha and Anchorage participating in the sea phase of Exercise Malabar 2026, an annual naval exercise under the “Quad” partnership of Australia, Japan, India and the U.S. The exercise ran from Nov. 5-12 in and around Yokosuka. Indian Navy Shivalik-class stealth multi-role frigate INS Sahyadri (F 49), Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Hyuga-class helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH 182), Mogami-class frigate JS Mogami (FFM 1), Royal Australian Navy Anzac-class frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH 153) and U.S. Navy San Antonio-class amphibious transport docks USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26) sail in formation in the Western Pacific Ocean during Exercise Malabar 2026, Nov. 7, 2026. US Navy photo Participating in the drills alongside John P. Murtha and Anchorage were Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH-182), frigate JS Mogami (FFM-1), a JMSDF submarine, Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri (F49), Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH153), a U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon Maritime Patrol Aircraft and a JMSDF P-1 MPA. Exercise activities included naval gunfire, anti-surface warfare drills and anti-submarine warfare drills. Ise and John P. Murtha carried out reciprocal visit, board, search, and seizure (VBSS) drills . Following completion of Malabar 2026, John P. Murtha headed out to the Philippine Sea to join Makin Island . Anchorage anchored offshore at Yokosuka on Nov. 13 and docked into CFAY on Nov. 16, taking the space vacated by departing submarine tender USS Frank Cable (AS-40), according to local ship spotters . Makin Island and John P. Murtha transited the South China Sea and pulled into Sembawang, Singapore on Friday for a port visit. The Navy nor the Pentagon has said whether Anchorage will join Makin Island and John P. Murtha . Makin Island and John P. Murtha are heading towards the Indian Ocean. Makin Island and John P. Murtha are expected to relieve the Boxer ARG in the Middle East. The Boxer ARG, which includes amphibious assault ship USS Boxer (LHD-4), amphibious dock landing ship USS Comstock (LSD-45) and amphibious transport dock USS Portland (LPD-27) and the embarked 11th MEU, deployed out from the West Coast in March, USNI News reported , putting it at eight months deployed. Boxer and Comstock were operating in U.S. Central Command as of Monday while Portland was operating in U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations, according to the USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker .

title: China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow
zh_title: 中国海军发展成为珠海航展的焦点
summary: 中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际防务、航空领域最重要的赛事之一
content:
中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际国防和航空航天史上最重要的活动之一，成为中国快速发展的航空和军事工业的主要公开展示地。两年一度的中国国际航空航天展览会（俗称中国航展）于 1996 年首次举办，为展示中国一些最先进的军事硬件提供了难得的机会，其中包括在其他地方很少如此详细展示的飞机和系统。虽然该活动也是中国航空航天工业向潜在国际客户推广其产品的主要平台，但它日益成为展示新军事能力和提供难以评估的项目的重要场所。
第十五届中国国际航空航天展览会（又称 2024 年中国航展）于 2024 年 11 月 15 日在中国广东省珠海市中国国际航空航天展览中心举行。摄影：VCG/VCG via Getty Images 前几届已经取得了一些特别重大的进展。 2016 年的展会上，J-20 隐形战斗机首次公开飞行亮相，而 2018 年的展会则以不同寻常的方式展示了这架飞机，包括展示其装载空对空导弹的内部武器舱。 2022年的展会上，歼20首次在珠海进行静态展示，同时还有运20重型运输机、直20直升机以及在展会上进行首次飞行演示的运20空中加油机。最近，2024 年的展会特别引人注目的是 J-35A 隐形战斗机的公开亮相和具有弹射能力的 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机的出现。一架 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机在 2024 年中国航展上进行飞行表演。CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images 今年的展览定于 12 月 7 日至 13 日举行，除其他外，将展示中国海军的广泛能力，特别强调其舰载航空能力的快速发展，这一点我们过去已经详细讨论过。
预计将亮相的最引人注目的飞机包括 J-15T 舰载战斗机、作战型 J-35 隐形战斗机、KJ-600 舰载机载预警和控制 (AEW&C) 飞机、Z-20 直升机的几种海军型号，也许最重要的是新型 JL-15 舰载教练机，它是陆基 JL-10 的发展型。JL-15 舰载教练机的照片突出显示了制动钩和弹射器发射杆。虽然我们之前在珠海见过 J-15T，但如果它配备国产 WS-10H2 发动机，将会引起特别的兴趣。这样的配置将让人们更仔细地了解中国舰载侧卫衍生产品的最新演变

【原文 English Original】
China’s People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) says it’s preparing a major presence at the upcoming 16th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition in Zhuhai, with warships , carrier-based aircraft , advanced weapons systems, and uncrewed platforms set to feature prominently. The expanded naval component will include a new maritime equipment exhibition area at Gaolan Port, located just on the other side of the bay, marking the first time the PLAN has established such a dedicated display at the event. Zhuhai has become one of the most important events on the international defence and aerospace calendar, serving as China’s principal public showcase for its rapidly developing aviation and military industries. First held in 1996, the biennial China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China, provides an unusual opportunity to see some of the country’s most advanced military hardware, including aircraft and systems that are rarely shown in such detail elsewhere. While the event also serves as a major platform for China’s aerospace industry to promote its products to potential international customers , it has increasingly become an important venue for revealing new military capabilities and offering glimpses of programs that are otherwise difficult to assess. A general view of the 15th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, or Airshow China 2024, at the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition Center on November 15, 2024, in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province of China. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Previous editions have produced some particularly significant developments. The 2016 show saw the J-20 stealth fighter make its first public flying appearance , while the 2018 edition provided an unusually revealing look at the aircraft, including a demonstration of its internal weapons bays, loaded with air-to-air missiles . The 2022 exhibition featured the J-20 on static display for the first time at Zhuhai, alongside the Y-20 heavy transport aircraft, Z-20 helicopter, and YY-20 aerial refueling tanker, which made its first flying demonstration at the event. More recently, the 2024 exhibition was particularly notable for the public debut of the J-35A stealth fighter and the appearance of the catapult-capable J-15T carrier-based fighter. A J-15T carrier-based fighter conducts a flight demonstration at Airshow China 2024. CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images This year’s exhibition, scheduled to take place from December 7 to 13, will showcase, among others, a broad range of the PLAN’s capabilities, with a particularly notable emphasis on the rapid evolution of its carrier aviation capabilities, something we have addressed in detail in the past . Among the most noteworthy aircraft expected to feature are the J-15T carrier-based fighter, the operational J-35 stealth fighter, the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft, several naval variants of the Z-20 helicopter, and, perhaps most significantly, the new JL-15 carrier-capable trainer, a development of the land-based JL-10 . A photo of the JL-15 carrier-capable trainer with the arrestor hook and catapult launch bar highlighted. Chinese internet via X While we have seen the J-15T at Zhuhai before, the aircraft will be of particular interest if it is shown with the indigenous WS-10H2 engine. Such a configuration would offer a closer look at the latest evolution of China’s carrier-based Flanker derivative and its ongoing transition toward a more domestically supported carrier aviation ecosystem. The appearance of the J-35 would be another major highlight. The aircraft represents a significant step in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ambitions, bringing a fifth-generation stealth fighter capability into the carrier air wing. Its presence would provide another opportunity to examine the progress of China’s next-generation naval fighter program. Back in 2014, Zhuhai saw the public debut of the FC-31 fighter demonstrator. At the time, it was still a land-based concept, and export was the main talking point, although there was already speculation about a naval variant, today’s J-35. A People’s Liberation Army Navy J-35 fighter during trials from the carrier Fujian last year. Chinese internet via X Meanwhile, the KJ-600 is arguably one of the most important developments in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ecosystem. The twin-engine turboprop aircraft is designed to provide airborne early warning and battle management capabilities, something that would transform the situational awareness and coordination available to China’s carrier strike groups. One of the first high-definition photos of the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft. Chinese internet via X Several variants of the Z-20 family are also expected to feature, reflecting the growing importance of helicopters in carrier operations, including airborne anti-submarine warfare, utility, and other maritime support missions. You can read more about the Z-20 family and other Chinese rotary-wing developments in this previous TWZ deep-dive on the topic . A Z-20F, the anti-submarine warfare variant of the naval Z-20 family. Three more naval Z-20s are seen in the hangar behind, including a Z-20J shipborne transport and assault variant. Chinese internet via X Perhaps the most intriguing aircraft on the list, however, is the JL-15. The JL-15 is derived from the Hongdu JL-10, also exported as the L-15 Falcon, a twin-engine advanced jet trainer and lead-in fighter trainer. The navalized development was initially reported to be designated JL-10J, but is now confirmed as being the JL-15. A tailhook-equipped mockup was spotted alongside the aircraft carrier Fujian in 2024. However, its operational status remains unclear, and China is known to have encountered difficulties with its earlier JL-9G naval trainer, whose tailhook was reportedly deleted following structural problems. Regarding the rumoured JL-10J carrier-capable jet trainer, another hint was spotted next to the carrier Fujian: It appears to be an unfinished JL-10J mockup stored on the dockside . So question is: Two tails as shown in the latest CG or just one like the regular JL-10? pic.twitter.com/BM8W8MRGWK — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) March 19, 2024 Its appearance would provide a particularly interesting indication of how China is thinking about training its next generation of carrier-based pilots. A carrier-capable development of the JL-10 would be an important addition to the emerging carrier aviation ecosystem, bridging the gap between conventional jet training and the demanding requirements of operating from an aircraft carrier. The JL-15 also makes an interesting comparison with the U.S. Navy’s somewhat stuttering efforts to introduce a new training jet for its carrier pilots. The U.S. Navy’s Undergraduate Jet Training System (UJTS) program is intended to replace its aging fleet of T-45 Goshawk trainers, but the acquisition effort has encountered considerable difficulties. Earlier this month, we described how Sierra Nevada Corporation (SNC) withdrew its proposed clean-sheet Freedom Jet from the competition, citing concerns over the Navy’s insistence on firm-fixed-price production commitments before the aircraft’s design had sufficiently matured. This leaves the Beechcraft M-346N , based on Leonardo’s established M-346 Master , as the only publicly known remaining contender . The program has also experienced schedule slippage, with the initial contract award now expected in the fourth quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Perhaps more significant is the difference in the two services’ approaches to carrier aviation training. The U.S. Navy has removed the requirement for its next-generation jet trainer to be capable of operating from an actual aircraft carrier, including carrier qualification and simulated carrier touch-and-goes at land-based facilities. Instead, it increasingly relies on advanced simulation, virtualized training, and assisted carrier landing technologies to prepare pilots for the demands of carrier operations. The JL-15, by contrast, is intended to support carrier-based pilot training. A dedicated carrier-capable trainer could offer China a more direct pathway for preparing pilots for operations aboard its increasingly sophisticated — and expanding — carrier fleet. Taken together, the PLAN aircraft being lined up for Zhuhai this year illustrate the increasingly sophisticated and integrated nature of China’s carrier aviation ambitions . As well as the aircraft carriers and their embarked aircraft, these ambitions also require other surface and subsurface vessels to operate effectively. Uncrewed systems will form another important part of the display. The exhibition will include aerial drones, uncrewed underwater vehicles, and other autonomous platforms, reflecting the PLAN’s growing interest in the potential of uncrewed warfare. Chinese media reports suggest that the WZ-2 uncrewed helicopter will receive its public debut at Zhuhai, while the PLAN may well also want to capitalize on its recent announcement that it had successfully launched and recovered a GJ-21 stealthy flying-wing uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . GJ-21. Chinese internet via X A chance to see the GJ-21 up close would be a huge deal, but there are many other naval drone options that could be revealed in more detail. There are likely to be more navalized collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) concepts and developments, especially since the adoption of the electromagnetic aircraft launch system (EMALS) catapult opens up a huge range of possibilities for uncrewed aircraft operating as part of a carrier air wing. Potentially, these could include the mysterious MQ-25-like drone that we recently discussed , the role of which remains unclear. On top of that, constant CCA testing at locations such as Malan suggests there could be much more to discuss than just the systems officially highlighted. Many other naval drones will surely be on display as well, including lower-end attritable concepts. Beyond static displays, China’s navy plans to organize flight demonstrations, formation flights, and simulated operational exercises. Its stated aim is to highlight not only the capabilities of individual platforms but also their ability to operate together in complex maritime environments. Photos have emerged showing apparent rehearsals for the display, presenting examples of the J-15, J-35, and KJ-600 to represent Beijing’s broader carrier air wing ecosystem. Two J-15s, two J-35s, and a KJ-600 purportedly taking part in a rehearsal for a formation fly-over at Zhuhai. Chinese internet via X It is not immediately clear which versions of the J-15 are participating in this formation flight: they could be J-15Ts, but another possibility is the electronic warfare version, the J-15DT , that we have profiled in the past. Regardless, they highlight how China’s carrier aviation ambitions are increasingly focused on catapult-assisted takeoff but arrested recovery (CATOBAR) operations, which offer many advantages . The J-15DT electronic warfare version of the Chinese carrier Flanker is outfitted for operations aboard catapult-equipped flattops like the Fujian . Chinese internet via X For the first time, the exhibition will also include a substantial surface fleet component, making use of the docks at the nearby Gaolan Port. Among the vessels expected to be featured are the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, the Type 055 guided-missile destroyer, and the Type 054A guided-missile frigate. Their presence will offer a public-facing showcase of China’s increasingly sophisticated surface fleet and its expanding range of maritime capabilities. It should also be recalled that it was at Gaolan Port where at least one Chinese uncrewed surface vessel , a distinctive trimaran craft, was first spotted. The Type 055 guided-missile destroyer Nanchang sails during the naval exercise Joint Sea-2021 on October 19, 2021, in the Western part of the Pacific Ocean. Photo by Sun Zifa/China News Service via Getty Images The broader messaging surrounding the exhibition is also notable. According to the PLAN, this year’s displays will place greater emphasis on operational readiness and training, with active-duty equipment that regularly participates in exercises and maritime security missions taking precedence over purely exhibition-oriented displays. This should underscore how Beijing has rapidly spun up its naval capabilities, introducing new and more capable equipment that is increasingly capable of more sustained out-of-area operations. The expanded naval presence at Zhuhai looks set to provide a substantial public showcase of China’s ongoing naval modernization. As well as the combination of the J-15T, J-35, KJ-600, and Z-20 variants, the JL-15 points to an increasingly comprehensive carrier aviation enterprise. And, judging by previous editions of the show, there will almost certainly be more novelties on display as well. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow appeared first on TWZ .
